repository.description: Adaptive memory for AI agents & teams — beyond RAG. Self-hosted MCP server that gets smarter every time you search: hybrid search + a neural memory graph that learns. Works with Claude, ChatGPT & any MCP client.
repository.name: memory-cloud
repository.readme:
Kagura Memory Cloud

Your next AI conversation starts with what you already know.
Shared, persistent memory for people, teams, and AI agents.
Open source · Self-hostable · MCP + REST API

English · 日本語

Open in ChatGPT · Request a cloud invite · Self-host · Benchmarks · Documentation

## Keep the context. Change the conversation. > **DolphinBench: 455 of 600 tasks (75.8%), self-tested on November 23, 2026.** With Hermes and GPT 5.6 Luna, Kagura Memory Cloud passed more tasks than each memory system in the benchmark's published Hermes + Luna results (Mem0 424, Hindsight 417, Honcho 411). The run is self-reported and awaits the maintainers' review: [run record](https://github.com/mem0ai/dolphinbench/pull/16) · [evidence](https://github.com/kagura-ai/dolphinbench/releases/tag/kagura-memory-cloud-hermes-20261123) · [comparison](#dolphinbench-memory-for-an-agent-that-acts). > **OpenAI Plugin released:** [Kagura Memory Cloud is available in ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6adacc9eaf5481919a85fad2aaa7aade). Add the plugin and sign in to Kagura to save and recall memories in your conversations. See [supported platforms](#supported-platforms) for the other ways to connect. You explained the project yesterday. Today you open a new chat, switch AI tools, or hand work to a teammate. The decisions and their reasons should come with you. **Kagura Memory Cloud gives your assistants a shared place to remember and recall that knowledge.** Save a decision in one session; retrieve it in another client connected to the same workspace and context. Browse, edit, and organize the memories in the web UI. It works with **ChatGPT, Claude, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Muse, Grok, and Microsoft 365 Copilot**. Use the published ChatGPT plugin or connect a compatible client over MCP. Applications can also use the REST API or [Python SDK](https://github.com/kagura-ai/kagura-memory-python-sdk). | When you… | Use shared memory to… | |---|---| | Resume a project | Recover decisions, constraints, and unresolved work. | | Switch AI assistants | Reuse the same project knowledge across tools. | | Work with a team | Share knowledge through workspace and context roles. | | Change a decision | Replace an outdated memory and retain its history. | | Build an agent | Retrieve relevant context without sending the entire conversation log. |


See memory retrieval in action — watch the demo.

## Quick start ### Choose how to try it | | Start here | What you need | |---|---|---| | **Hosted Kagura AI** | [Request an invite](https://www.kagura-ai.com/waitlist/) · [Connect your AI client](https://www.kagura-ai.com/help/connect/) | An invited account and a compatible AI client. Cloud registration is currently invite-only. | | **Self-hosted Memory Cloud** | Run the setup below | Docker Compose, Python 3.11+, Bash, and an embedding provider. | ### Supported platforms | Client | Start here | |---|---| | **ChatGPT — released OpenAI Plugin** | [Add Kagura Memory Cloud](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6adacc9eaf5481919a85fad2aaa7aade), then sign in to your Kagura AI account. | | **Claude / Claude Desktop** | [Connect over remote MCP](docs/mcp-clients.md#claude-desktop--claude-chat-web) and sign in to Kagura. | | **Claude Code** | [Connect MCP](docs/mcp-clients.md#claude-code-recommended); add the optional plugin for session workflows. | | **Codex** | [Connect MCP and install the optional skill plugin](docs/getting-started.md#codex-cli). | | **Cursor** | [Add the MCP server in Cursor settings](docs/getting-started.md#cursor). | | **Gemini / Gemini CLI** | Use a [custom MCP connector](docs/mcp-clients.md#gemini-custom-mcp-connector) or the [CLI configuration](docs/mcp-clients.md#gemini-cli). | | **Muse** | [Add a remote MCP server](docs/mcp-clients.md#muse) and sign in to Kagura. | | **Grok / Grok Bot** | [Connect over remote MCP](docs/mcp-clients.md#grok--grok-bot) and sign in to Kagura. | | **Microsoft 365 Copilot** | [Connect through MCP and OAuth](docs/microsoft-365-copilot.md), with operator setup of the OAuth client and Microsoft registration. | | **Other MCP clients / your own apps** | Use [Streamable HTTP or the REST API](docs/mcp-clients.md#other-mcp-clients--rest-api). | The published ChatGPT plugin connects to hosted Kagura AI and requires an account. For your own Memory Cloud deployment, use the [custom MCP connection instructions](docs/mcp-clients.md#chatgpt-desktop). ### Run locally On Linux, macOS, or Windows with WSL2, with Docker running: ```bash git clone https://github.com/kagura-ai/memory-cloud.git cd memory-cloud bash setup.sh ``` The interactive setup generates configuration secrets, installs the pinned Python dependencies and Kagura CLI, starts the services, runs migrations, and creates an admin account and MCP configuration. It uses `curl` if it needs to install `uv`. Node.js runs inside Docker; a host Node.js installation is only needed for frontend development. **Memory search needs embeddings:** configure an OpenAI API key or a reachable self-hosted embedding server. Google/GitHub sign-in is optional; the local admin can use a password and MFA. See the [setup guide](docs/getting-started.md) for manual steps and provider configuration. | Open | Purpose | |---|---| | [localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) | Sign in and manage your memories. | | `http://localhost:8080/mcp` | Connect a local MCP client. | | [localhost:8080/redoc](http://localhost:8080/redoc) | Explore the running server's REST API. | The root Compose stack is for local development. For a public server, use the [deployment guide](docs/deployment.md). ### Try your first memory 1. In the web UI, create a context named **my-first-project**. A context groups memories for a project or topic. 2. Connect your AI client using [MCP Client Setup](docs/mcp-clients.md). For Claude Code, setup generates a local `.mcp.json`; restart the client to load it. Other clients have their own configuration. Web-based clients need a reachable HTTPS server, rather than your machine's `localhost`. 3. Ask the assistant: > In Kagura's my-first-project context, remember: we chose PostgreSQL because the app needs transactions and relational queries. 4. Open a **new conversation** with the connected client and ask: > Search Kagura's my-first-project context. Which database did we choose, and why? Look for the saved memory in the web UI and a recall tool call in the new conversation. Then repeat the question in another client with access to the same context. Kagura stores what you or an integration explicitly saves. Connecting a client does not automatically import all of its past chats. Keep credentials out of memories and version control. ## Benchmarks: accuracy and cost together How much history does an assistant need to answer well? Our [public benchmark report](https://www.kagura-ai.com/ja/benchmarks/) measures answer quality as well as cost. | LoCoMo, 472 questions across 3 conversations | KMC v0.152.0 | Full conversation input | |---|---:|---:| | Answer accuracy, strict grading | **84.2%** | 89.0% | | Memory tokens read at answer time | **80% fewer** | Baseline | | Answer-time model cost | **66% lower** | Baseline | These are developer-run, preregistered results from November 10, 2026, excluding adversarial questions. Costs exclude memory construction and service fees. The tradeoff includes lower accuracy than full-history input; these are not official full-dataset scores or a guarantee for your workload. A November 12 rerun of **v0.156.0** scored **91.3% with lenient grading / 83.7% with strict grading**. It reused the same conversations after tuning and was not preregistered. Keep it separate from the original run and its cost measurements. ### DolphinBench: memory for an agent that acts [DolphinBench](https://github.com/mem0ai/dolphinbench) gives an agent three people's histories (13,539 messages) and then 600 tasks in simulated apps; a task passes only if the agent acts correctly on what it should remember. We ran it with the benchmark's Hermes setup and GPT 5.6 Luna, with Kagura Memory Cloud as the memory. | Memory (Hermes + GPT 5.6 Luna) | Tasks passed, of 600 | Source | |---|---:|---| | **Kagura Memory Cloud v0.156.0** | **455 (75.8%)** | Self-tested, November 23, 2026; [under review](https://github.com/mem0ai/dolphinbench/pull/16) | | Mem0 | 424 (70.7%) | Published by the benchmark | | Hindsight | 417 (69.5%) | Published by the benchmark | | Honcho | 411 (68.5%) | Published by the benchmark | | Hermes built-in memory | 394 (65.7%) | Published by the benchmark | | Supermemory | 355 (59.2%) | Published by the benchmark | Read the comparison with these limits: - **Self-tested.** The benchmark's maintainers have not verified our run. The published rows are theirs. - **Not held out.** We chose the plugin's recall settings after reading failures on the public tasks. - **Judge route.** The judge is the benchmark's model, settings and prompts, sent through the OpenAI API instead of Azure. - **Cost.** $97.90 of agent tokens at the benchmark's prices. The memory server's own models ran self-hosted and are not included. - **Other self-tested runs** awaiting review report 451 to 504 tasks, most with a different harness. Everything needed to check the score is public: the [run record and method note](https://github.com/kagura-ai/dolphinbench/blob/kagura-memory-cloud-hermes-20261123/docs/submissions/kagura-memory-cloud-hermes-20261123.md), the [evidence ZIP](https://github.com/kagura-ai/dolphinbench/releases/tag/kagura-memory-cloud-hermes-20261123) with all 600 task conversations and saved judge answers, and the plugin and adapter source at the same tag. **Evaluation is ongoing.** We are running additional evaluations and working to improve memory retrieval and answer accuracy. The published results above reflect the tested versions and conditions. See the [benchmark reading guide](docs/benchmarks.md) for FC and LongMemEval results, comparison limits, and the distinction between answer accuracy and retrieval metrics. [English public report](https://www.kagura-ai.com/benchmarks/) · [日本語・LoCoMo詳細](https://www.kagura-ai.com/ja/benchmarks/) ## What you get | Capability | How it helps | |---|---| | **Hybrid retrieval** | Semantic search + BM25 keyword matching, with optional reranking. | | **Memory you can maintain** | Update, supersede, inspect revisions, and remove outdated knowledge. | | **Session continuity** | Bootstrap a session with context, pinned notes, upcoming items, and recent changes. | | **Related-memory discovery** | Explore a graph of related memories; supported searches can strengthen associations. | | **Team controls** | Workspaces, private/shared contexts, roles, and scoped credentials. | | **Web management** | Search and edit memories, inspect history, manage members and integrations. | | **Your deployment choice** | Self-host the Apache-licensed server and choose your embedding provider. Model and infrastructure costs depend on that choice. | ### MCP tools Start with `remember`, `recall`, and `reference`. Session tools such as `bootstrap` and `changes_since` help an agent pick up previous work. Use `update_memory` or supersession when a fact changes. The default `/mcp` endpoint lists the core tools. Add `?profile=full` for the full catalog, or `?add_tools=explore` for graph exploration. Tool visibility and access permissions are separate; workspace and context roles still apply. See [tool profiles and roles](docs/mcp-tools.md#tool-profiles). ### Getting started with Claude Code Once MCP is connected, the optional plugin adds guided session and memory workflows. In Claude Code: ```text /plugin marketplace add kagura-ai/memory-cloud /plugin install kagura-memory@kagura-memory-cloud ``` Use `/kagura-memory:session-start` when you return to a project and `/kagura-memory:session-summary` to save useful knowledge before leaving. `/kagura-memory:recall`, `:remember`, and `:maintain` support day-to-day use. Installation and hook configuration are covered in [MCP Client Setup](docs/mcp-clients.md); Codex users have a [separate plugin setup](docs/getting-started.md#codex-cli). ## How it works ```text People and AI clients ── MCP / REST ── Kagura Memory Cloud ├─ Workspace → contexts → memories ├─ PostgreSQL: records, keywords, graph ├─ Qdrant: semantic retrieval └─ Web UI: browse, edit, share ``` `recall` finds relevant memories through hybrid search. `explore` follows relationships for discovery. Keeping these paths separate lets you choose direct retrieval or related knowledge. Background [Sleep Maintenance](docs/sleep-maintenance.md) consolidates memory according to configuration. Built with **FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Qdrant, Redis, and Next.js**. Read the [architecture](docs/architecture.md) and [core concepts](docs/concepts.md) for the underlying design. ## Documentation | I want to… | Read | |---|---| | Install and save my first memory | [Getting Started](docs/getting-started.md) | | Connect an AI client | [MCP Client Setup](docs/mcp-clients.md) | | Build an integration | [MCP Tools](docs/mcp-tools.md) · [REST API](docs/api-reference.md) · [Python SDK](https://github.com/kagura-ai/kagura-memory-python-sdk) | | Write useful memories | [Chunking Guide](docs/chunking-guide.md) · [Core Concepts](docs/concepts.md) | | Evaluate quality | [Benchmarks](docs/benchmarks.md) | | Deploy and operate | [Deployment](docs/deployment.md) · [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md) | | Find a specialist guide | [Documentation index](docs/README.md) | | See what changed | [Releases](https://github.com/kagura-ai/memory-cloud/releases) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) | ## Contribute Bug reports, documentation improvements, and contributions are welcome. Start with [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Report vulnerabilities through [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## License [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE).

name: CI

# No run for a tag push (#3027): a release tag is put on the squash commit of
# the release pull request, which this workflow checked just before.
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

# No job writes to the repository.
permissions:
  contents: read

# One group per PR (a new push cancels its older run); a manual run is its own run_id group.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0 # v7.1.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"

      # uv is pinned in lockstep with backend/pyproject.toml [tool.uv]
      # required-version, backend/Dockerfile and setup.sh (#1706);
      # tests/test_uv_version_lockstep.py enforces it. The cache is keyed on
      # backend/uv.lock, so a lock change is the only thing that refills it.
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          version: "0.11.19"
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: backend/uv.lock

      # The gate for (#1706): a pyproject.toml change without a matching
      # uv.lock update fails here, before anything is installed.
      - name: Lockfile is current
        run: cd backend && uv lock --check

      # Only the `lint` dependency group of the lock (one wheel), so lint and
      # format checks run the same ruff release a contributor gets from
      # `uv sync` without installing the runtime tree.
      - name: Install ruff (from the lock)
        run: |
          cd backend
          uv sync --locked --only-group lint --no-install-project
          echo "$PWD/.venv/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Lint
        run: cd backend && ruff check src/ tests/

      - name: Format check
        run: cd backend && ruff format --check src/ tests/

      # The plugin hook and digest scripts live outside backend/ and carry their own
      # ruff.toml (py39 target); mirrors the `lint` target in the Makefile.
      - name: Lint plugin scripts
        run: ruff check plugins/kagura-memory/hooks/ plugins/kagura-memory/scripts/ && ruff format --check plugins/kagura-memory/hooks/ plugins/kagura-memory/scripts/

      - name: Models no-Column guard
        run: make lint-models-no-column

  # Static type gate for the backend (#1442). The frontend has run
  # `tsc --noEmit` since day one; pyright was configured in
  # backend/pyproject.toml with a tier-by-tier plan (#599, #612) and a
  # `make type-check` target, but nothing enforced it — so it drifted red.
  # Two of the findings it had accumulated were real functional bugs that
  # ruff and the 6k-test suite both missed (#1440), plus a third (#1443).
  #
  # This is a HARD gate on purpose. `continue-on-error` would have surfaced
  # those bugs exactly as well as having no check at all.
  #
  # Kept as its own job rather than folded into `lint`: pyright needs the
  # project's real dependency tree installed, while `lint` only needs ruff
  # and stays fast.
  type-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0 # v7.1.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"

      # uv is pinned in lockstep with backend/pyproject.toml [tool.uv]
      # required-version, backend/Dockerfile and setup.sh (#1706);
      # tests/test_uv_version_lockstep.py enforces it. The cache is keyed on
      # backend/uv.lock, so a lock change is the only thing that refills it.
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          version: "0.11.19"
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: backend/uv.lock

      # EVERY optional extra, not just dev. This is load-bearing, not
      # thoroughness for its own sake: pyright silently stops analysing a module
      # whose imports it cannot resolve, so a missing extra turns real findings
      # into a single "unresolved import" line. google-genai/ollama
      # (`llm_providers`) hid #1443 — Gemini list_models always returning its
      # hardcoded fallback — behind exactly that. lancedb/pyarrow (`lite`) were
      # missed on the first attempt at this job and CI caught it.
      # If a new extra is added to pyproject.toml, add it here too, and to
      # `make install` (the local set: this one minus `neural`, #2523).
      # backend/tests/ci/test_type_check_env.py checks both.
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          cd backend
          uv sync --locked --extra dev --extra llm_providers --extra neural --extra lite
          echo "$PWD/.venv/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Type check
        run: cd backend && pyright src/ ../plugins/kagura-memory/hooks/

  # Shell-script quality gate for the blue-green deploy script. shellcheck
  # catches the `set -e` / quoting bug class behind #986 (a bare
  # `var=$(curl ...)` dying silently); the bats suite pins the three
  # verify_workers_blocked branches so that regression cannot return (#1000).
  shell:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # shellcheck is preinstalled on ubuntu-latest; bats is not.
      - name: Install bats
        run: sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y -qq bats

      - name: ShellCheck deploy.sh
        run: shellcheck terraform/single-server/scripts/deploy.sh

      - name: Bats — verify_workers_blocked regression suite
        run: bats terraform/single-server/scripts/tests/

      # #1500: the CI readiness gate is a script too — same bar.
      - name: ShellCheck wait-for-api.sh
        run: shellcheck .github/scripts/wait-for-api.sh

      # #2763: the image contents check that the images job runs.
      - name: ShellCheck check-image-contents.sh
        run: shellcheck .github/scripts/check-image-contents.sh

      # #2771: the tag/server.json version guard of publish-mcp-registry.yml.
      - name: ShellCheck check-server-json-version.sh
        run: shellcheck .github/scripts/check-server-json-version.sh

      - name: Bats — wait-for-api phase verdicts, image contents and server.json version verdicts
        run: bats .github/scripts/tests/

  backend-unit:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      # Redis is required at FastAPI lifespan startup (SessionManager eagerly
      # connects via auth.session._get_or_create_redis_client). Without it,
      # any test using TestClient(app) fails at app boot. DB/Qdrant are not
      # required because tests/conftest.py::async_engine skips gracefully.
      redis:
        image: redis:7-alpine
        ports:
          - 6379:6379
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "redis-cli ping"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0 # v7.1.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"

      # uv is pinned in lockstep with backend/pyproject.toml [tool.uv]
      # required-version, backend/Dockerfile and setup.sh (#1706);
      # tests/test_uv_version_lockstep.py enforces it. The cache is keyed on
      # backend/uv.lock, so a lock change is the only thing that refills it.
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          version: "0.11.19"
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: backend/uv.lock

      - name: Install dependencies
        # From the lock, never a fresh resolution: --locked fails when uv.lock
        # is out of date with pyproject.toml (#1706). The venv goes on PATH so
        # the pytest / alembic / python steps below run unchanged. `lite`
        # (lancedb, pyarrow) lets the real-table LanceDB tests run instead of
        # skipping (#1808).
        run: |
          cd backend
          uv sync --locked --extra dev --extra lite
          echo "$PWD/.venv/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run unit tests
        env:
          REDIS_URL: redis://localhost:6379
        # tests/smoke/test_all_routes.py is excluded here: it iterates every
        # route (including Postgres-backed public endpoints) and asserts no
        # 500s, which inherently requires a running DB + migrated schema.
        # It runs in the backend-integration job below alongside tests/integration/.
        run: cd backend && pytest --ignore=tests/e2e --ignore=tests/integration --ignore=tests/smoke/test_all_routes.py -v --maxfail=5 --timeout=300

  frontend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: "24"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: cd frontend && npm ci

      - name: Type check
        run: cd frontend && npx tsc --noEmit

      # ESLint flat config (frontend/eslint.config.mjs, #2202). Errors fail the
      # job; rule families with pre-existing hits are warn-only for now, and
      # `npm run lint` caps the warning count (--max-warnings) so new ones fail.
      - name: Lint
        run: cd frontend && npm run lint

      # CI builds with the webpack compiler (`--webpack`) instead of the
      # Next.js 16 default (Turbopack). Turbopack's `next build` hard-requires
      # the native @next/swc-* binding, which `npm ci` fails to provide on the
      # GitHub Actions runner (only the WASM fallback loads), aborting the
      # build on every PR. The prod Docker build (frontend/Dockerfile) still
      # uses Turbopack, so this flag is scoped to CI only — package.json's
      # shared `build` script is left as the canonical Turbopack build. See #855.
      - name: Build
        run: cd frontend && npm run build -- --webpack
        env:
          NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL: http://localhost:8080

  # Accessibility (color-contrast) checks via Playwright + @axe-core (#780).
  # Scoped to `e2e/a11y` only — the full `test:e2e` suite includes
  # admin-user-detail.spec.ts, whose admin-auth fixture hard-requires a live
  # backend + E2E_ADMIN_* secrets and would fail here. The a11y specs are
  # hermetic: playwright.config.ts auto-starts `next dev` and /login renders
  # without auth. Required-check promotion is deferred to #768 (after 5
  # consecutive green runs).
  frontend-a11y:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [frontend]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: "24"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: cd frontend && npm ci

      - name: Install Playwright browser
        run: cd frontend && npx playwright install chromium --with-deps

      - name: Run a11y tests
        run: cd frontend && npm run test:a11y
        env:
          NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL: http://localhost:8080

      - name: Upload Playwright report
        if: ${{ failure() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: playwright-report
          path: frontend/playwright-report/
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 7

  # Detect which paths changed so backend-integration only runs when
  # relevant. GHA does not expose `github.event.pull_request.changed_files`
  # — this is the standard monorepo path-gating pattern via
  # dorny/paths-filter outputs. Runs on all triggers (no `if:` guard) so
  # backend-integration's `needs:` dependency resolves on every event;
  # backend-integration's own `if:` gate decides whether to run.
  detect-changes:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # paths-filter lists the pull request's files through the API.
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      backend-integration: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.backend-integration }}
      frontend-a11y-authed: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.frontend-a11y-authed }}
      images: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.images }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dorny/paths-filter@ceb8a2b8f2d89434be7ff52d3de7ec3738c5cc9d # v4.0.3
        id: filter
        with:
          filters: |
            backend-integration:
              - 'backend/src/**'
              - 'backend/alembic/versions/**'
              # Every test directory: DB-backed tests live outside
              # tests/integration/ too and run in this job (#2297).
              - 'backend/tests/**'
              - 'backend/pyproject.toml'
              - 'backend/uv.lock'
              - '.github/workflows/ci.yml'
            frontend-a11y-authed:
              # Broad on purpose: this lane installs + runs the full stack, so any
              # file it consumes can break it. Cover the whole frontend source tree
              # (app + components + lib — the rendered /device, /invite, /workspace
              # pages pull in shared components), the e2e specs, the npm + backend
              # dependency/script manifests, and the backend it migrates/serves.
              - 'frontend/e2e/**'
              - 'frontend/src/**'
              - 'frontend/package.json'
              - 'frontend/package-lock.json'
              - 'frontend/playwright.config.ts'
              - 'backend/src/**'
              - 'backend/alembic/versions/**'
              - 'backend/pyproject.toml'
              - 'backend/uv.lock'
              - '.github/workflows/ci.yml'
              - '.github/scripts/**'
            images:
              # What goes into the api and web images (#2763). The application
              # code is left out on purpose: the images job checks the tools
              # and packages around it, and the web build takes minutes.
              - 'backend/Dockerfile'
              - 'backend/.dockerignore'
              - 'backend/pyproject.toml'
              - 'backend/uv.lock'
              - 'frontend/Dockerfile'
              # `output: "standalone"` decides whether the runner gets server.js.
              - 'frontend/next.config.ts'
              - 'frontend/package.json'
              - 'frontend/package-lock.json'
              - '.github/workflows/ci.yml'
              - '.github/scripts/check-image-contents.sh'

  # Integration tests + the all-routes smoke test — both require a live
  # DB and Redis. Gated by detect-changes path filter, `force-integration`
  # label or workflow_dispatch.
  #
  # Four parallel jobs (#3027), each with its own service containers and an
  # empty database: `db` runs the backend-unit suite again against Postgres;
  # `1`..`3` run the integration selection, split by test file
  # (.github/scripts/pytest_shard.py: every file lands in exactly one shard;
  # tests/ci/test_pytest_shard.py). It starts with backend-unit, not after it.
  backend-integration:
    name: backend-integration (${{ matrix.shard }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [detect-changes]
    strategy:
      # One shard's failure must not hide another's.
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: ["db", "1", "2", "3"]
    # The label-contains check is guarded by event-name so non-PR events
    # (workflow_dispatch) don't depend on PR-only context — GHA
    # treats undefined `pull_request` as null-coercible to an empty list, so
    # the bare contains() is safe in practice, but the explicit guard makes
    # the intent unambiguous to future readers.
    if: |
      needs.detect-changes.outputs.backend-integration == 'true' ||
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&
        contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'force-integration')) ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    services:
      postgres:
        # Literal pin (not a YAML anchor) in all three service blocks, and
        # postgres_pin_consistency.bats keeps them equal to the compose files.
        # Dependabot bumps only the compose files: update these on its PR (#2524).
        image: postgres:18.4-alpine@sha256:9a8afca54e7861fd90fab5fdf4c42477a6b1cb7d293595148e674e0a3181de15
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: kagura
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: kagura_dev_password
          POSTGRES_DB: kagura_test
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U kagura -d kagura_test"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
      redis:
        image: redis:7-alpine
        ports:
          - 6379:6379
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "redis-cli ping"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
      qdrant:
        # For the live vector-store tests (#1798). No --health-cmd: the image
        # ships no shell utilities usable for a container-side probe; the
        # "Wait for Qdrant" step below polls /readyz from the host. Same tag
        # as the compose files (qdrant_pin_consistency.bats).
        image: qdrant/qdrant:v1.19.1
        ports:
          - 6333:6333
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0 # v7.1.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"

      # uv is pinned in lockstep with backend/pyproject.toml [tool.uv]
      # required-version, backend/Dockerfile and setup.sh (#1706);
      # tests/test_uv_version_lockstep.py enforces it. The cache is keyed on
      # backend/uv.lock, so a lock change is the only thing that refills it.
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          version: "0.11.19"
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: backend/uv.lock

      - name: Install dependencies
        # From the lock, never a fresh resolution: --locked fails when uv.lock
        # is out of date with pyproject.toml (#1706). The venv goes on PATH so
        # the pytest / alembic / python steps below run unchanged. `lite`
        # matches the backend-unit job, so the DB-backed run below collects
        # the same suite.
        run: |
          cd backend
          uv sync --locked --extra dev --extra lite
          echo "$PWD/.venv/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      # MinIO for the #994 S3-compatible storage integration test. Started as a
      # plain container (not a GHA `services:` entry) so we control the
      # `server /data` command; the test creates its own bucket. The test
      # self-skips if MINIO_TEST_ENDPOINT is unreachable, so a MinIO hiccup
      # never fails the whole integration job spuriously.
      # Chainguard's MinIO build, pinned by digest (#1691): Docker Hub stopped
      # serving minio/minio on 2026-09-12 and quay.io/minio/minio started
      # requiring authentication on 2026-09-24, each failing every run at this
      # step. The digest is `latest` as of 2026-09-24 (RELEASE.2026-09-22T19-25-18Z).
      # Keep in sync with the `minio` service in docker-compose.yml.
      - name: Start MinIO
        run: |
          docker run -d --name minio -p 9000:9000 \
            -e MINIO_ROOT_USER=minioadmin -e MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD=minioadmin \
            cgr.dev/chainguard/minio@sha256:bd014394a80898e68c149f2311fdf8d5a2c2f3bb2c33b9327ae6d02b4b065ae1 \
            server /data
          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
            if curl -fs http://localhost:9000/minio/health/live >/dev/null; then
              echo "minio up"; exit 0
            fi
            sleep 2
          done
          # Hard-fail rather than let the test silently skip — the MinIO
          # round-trip is the #994 acceptance criterion, so "MinIO never came
          # up" must turn the job red, not green-by-skip.
          echo "MinIO did not become healthy within 60s" >&2
          docker logs minio 2>&1 | tail -30 || true
          exit 1

      # Hard-fail rather than let the Qdrant tests silently skip: they are the
      # only place the "never deletes a live memory's point" rule of the
      # orphan sweep meets a real vector store (#1798).
      - name: Wait for Qdrant
        run: |
          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
            if curl -fs http://localhost:6333/readyz >/dev/null; then
              echo "qdrant up"; exit 0
            fi
            sleep 2
          done
          echo "Qdrant did not become ready within 60s" >&2
          exit 1

      # The backend-unit suite again, now against Postgres: about 1,000 tests
      # outside tests/integration/ take the db_session fixture and skip in the
      # unit job, so this is the only place they run (#2297). The selection
      # matches backend-unit except tests/cli, which the integration step runs
      # (tests/ci/test_db_backed_tests_in_ci.py).
      - name: Run DB-backed tests outside tests/integration
        if: ${{ matrix.shard == 'db' }}
        env:
          TEST_DATABASE_URL: postgresql+asyncpg://kagura:kagura_dev_password@localhost:5432/kagura_test
          # The app's own engine (get_db, isolated sessions) reads DATABASE_URL;
          # point it at the same database the fixtures use.
          DATABASE_URL: postgresql+asyncpg://kagura:kagura_dev_password@localhost:5432/kagura_test
          # Fail instead of skipping every db_session test (#1885).
          REQUIRE_TEST_DATABASE: "1"
          REDIS_URL: redis://localhost:6379
          QDRANT_URL: http://localhost:6333
        run: >-
          cd backend && pytest --ignore=tests/e2e --ignore=tests/integration --ignore=tests/cli
          --ignore=tests/smoke/test_all_routes.py
          --timeout=300 --maxfail=5

      - name: Run integration tests
        # One of INTEGRATION_SHARDS shards; the shard list is printed first so
        # a log shows which files this job ran.
        if: ${{ matrix.shard != 'db' }}
        env:
          TEST_DATABASE_URL: postgresql+asyncpg://kagura:kagura_dev_password@localhost:5432/kagura_test
          # Hard-fail rather than let every db_session test silently skip: the
          # async_engine fixture (tests/conftest.py) turns a failed create_all
          # into a skip, which is right for the unit job but would leave this
          # job green with nothing run when Postgres is up and rejects the
          # schema (#1885).
          REQUIRE_TEST_DATABASE: "1"
          REDIS_URL: redis://localhost:6379
          QDRANT_URL: http://localhost:6333
          MINIO_TEST_ENDPOINT: http://localhost:9000
          MINIO_TEST_ACCESS_KEY: minioadmin
          MINIO_TEST_SECRET_KEY: minioadmin
          MINIO_TEST_BUCKET: kagura-files-test
          SHARD: ${{ matrix.shard }}
          INTEGRATION_SHARDS: "3"
        run: >-
          cd backend &&
          python ../.github/scripts/pytest_shard.py --shard "$SHARD" --total "$INTEGRATION_SHARDS"
          tests/integration/ tests/cli/ tests/smoke/test_all_routes.py > "$RUNNER_TEMP/shard-files.txt" &&
          cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/shard-files.txt" &&
          xargs -a "$RUNNER_TEMP/shard-files.txt" pytest
          -v --timeout=120 --maxfail=3

  # Authenticated a11y (color-contrast) lane (#840). Unlike the hermetic
  # frontend-a11y job (next dev only), the e2e/authed-a11y/ specs need a LIVE
  # backend + an authenticated admin, so this job provisions a full stack:
  # postgres + redis + migrated schema + a seeded admin, starts the API, then
  # runs Playwright (which auto-starts `next dev` via webServer). Boot needs
  # only postgres + redis (Qdrant is /readiness-only, not /health). Gated by
  # the detect-changes path filter (same pattern as backend-integration).
  #
  # Scope (#840, first slice): runs the 3 existing specs (device / invite
  # unknown-token / workspace-dashboard). Auth is deterministic via the
  # storageState `setup` project (#959): the admin logs in once, every spec
  # reuses the session cookie — no per-test re-login, so parallel workers can't
  # clobber each other's session (#114). The Pro-workspace/invitation
  # happy-path seed is still a deferred follow-up. This is a new CI-only lane —
  # boot env / port-wait timing may need tuning over the first runs; it is NOT
  # yet a Required check (#768).
  frontend-a11y-authed:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [detect-changes, frontend]
    if: |
      needs.detect-changes.outputs.frontend-a11y-authed == 'true' ||
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&
        contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'force-integration')) ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    env:
      # cd backend (cwd → resolves `src.api.main`) + PYTHONPATH=src (resolves the
      # bare `config`/`api` imports) mirrors how pytest (pythonpath=src) and the
      # docker CMD (uvicorn src.api.main:app) run.
      PYTHONPATH: src
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql+asyncpg://kagura:kagura_dev_password@localhost:5432/kagura_test
      REDIS_URL: redis://localhost:6379
      CORS_ORIGINS: http://localhost:3000
      E2E_ADMIN_LOGIN_ID: e2e-admin
      # #2918: the workspace management spec signs in as a second, separate
      # user whose allowance dropped to one of its three Free workspaces.
      # Slot suspension is enforced in this job only (enforce needs the
      # workspace cap enforced; the admin owns one Pro workspace, cap 3, so the
      # other specs see no change).
      E2E_SLOT_OWNER_LOGIN_ID: e2e-slot-owner
      WORKSPACE_SLOT_SUSPENSION: enforce
      ENFORCE_WORKSPACE_CAP: "true"
      E2E_API_URL: http://localhost:8080
      NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL: http://localhost:8080
      # #1500: wait-for-api.sh reads the boot-phase INFO lines from the API log.
      LOG_LEVEL: INFO
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:18.4-alpine@sha256:9a8afca54e7861fd90fab5fdf4c42477a6b1cb7d293595148e674e0a3181de15
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: kagura
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: kagura_dev_password
          POSTGRES_DB: kagura_test
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U kagura -d kagura_test"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
      redis:
        image: redis:7-alpine
        ports:
          - 6379:6379
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "redis-cli ping"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0 # v7.1.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"

      # uv is pinned in lockstep with backend/pyproject.toml [tool.uv]
      # required-version, backend/Dockerfile and setup.sh (#1706);
      # tests/test_uv_version_lockstep.py enforces it. The cache is keyed on
      # backend/uv.lock, so a lock change is the only thing that refills it.
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          version: "0.11.19"
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: backend/uv.lock

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: "24"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json

      - name: Install backend dependencies
        # From the lock, never a fresh resolution: --locked fails when uv.lock
        # is out of date with pyproject.toml (#1706). The venv goes on PATH so
        # the pytest / alembic / python steps below run unchanged.
        run: |
          cd backend
          uv sync --locked --extra dev
          echo "$PWD/.venv/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Install frontend dependencies
        run: cd frontend && npm ci

      - name: Install Playwright browser
        run: cd frontend && npx playwright install chromium --with-deps

      - name: Generate ephemeral secrets + admin password
        # Throwaway values for an ephemeral CI database — never reused. A valid
        # Fernet key is generated for API_KEY_SECRET in case the encryptor is
        # constructed at boot/import.
        run: |
          {
            echo "API_KEY_SECRET=$(python -c 'from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())')"
            echo "AUDIT_HMAC_KEY=$(python -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))')"
            echo "E2E_ADMIN_PASSWORD=Ci-$(python -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(18))')-9X"
          } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          # #2918: the slot owner's password, masked in the job log.
          SLOT_OWNER_PASSWORD="Ci-$(python -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(18))')-9X"
          echo "::add-mask::$SLOT_OWNER_PASSWORD"
          echo "E2E_SLOT_OWNER_PASSWORD=$SLOT_OWNER_PASSWORD" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Migrate schema
        run: cd backend && alembic upgrade head

      - name: Seed e2e admin
        run: cd backend && python -m src.cli.seed_e2e_admin

      - name: Seed e2e slot owner
        # #2918: three Free workspaces, two suspended, selection required.
        run: cd backend && python -m src.cli.seed_e2e_admin --slot-owner

      - name: Start API server
        # Logged to a file so the readiness gate can read the boot phases.
        run: |
          cd backend
          python -m uvicorn src.api.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 --log-level warning \
            > "$RUNNER_TEMP/api.log" 2>&1 &
          echo "API_PID=$!" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Wait for API readiness
        # #1500: a slow or crashed boot fails HERE, naming its phase — see
        # .github/scripts/wait-for-api.sh.
        id: wait_api
        run: .github/scripts/wait-for-api.sh "$API_PID" "$RUNNER_TEMP/api.log"

      - name: Run authed a11y tests
        run: cd frontend && npm run test:a11y:authed

      - name: Show API log
        # The readiness step already dumps the log when it is the one failing.
        if: ${{ failure() && steps.wait_api.outcome != 'failure' }}
        run: tail -n 100 "$RUNNER_TEMP/api.log" || true

      - name: Upload Playwright report
        if: ${{ failure() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: playwright-report-authed
          path: frontend/playwright-report/
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 7

  # OAuth account-linking E2E lane (#937). Like frontend-a11y-authed it needs a
  # live backend + authenticated admin, PLUS the OAuth endpoint overrides so the
  # server-side token/userinfo exchange hits the mock IdP (frontend/e2e/mock-idp)
  # instead of real Google/GitHub. The mock IdP is started by Playwright's
  # webServer (playwright.config.ts), so no separate start step is needed here.
  # Overrides are gated by OAUTH_ENDPOINT_OVERRIDE_ENABLED and hard-blocked in
  # production (auth/oauth_endpoints.py); ENVIRONMENT is left unset → development.
  # Reuses the frontend-a11y-authed path filter (its globs already cover every
  # file this lane consumes). New CI-only lane — NOT yet a Required check (#768);
  # boot/timing may need tuning over the first runs.
  frontend-e2e-oauth:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [detect-changes, frontend]
    if: |
      needs.detect-changes.outputs.frontend-a11y-authed == 'true' ||
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&
        contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'force-integration')) ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    env:
      PYTHONPATH: src
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql+asyncpg://kagura:kagura_dev_password@localhost:5432/kagura_test
      REDIS_URL: redis://localhost:6379
      CORS_ORIGINS: http://localhost:3000
      # The link callback redirects to {FRONTEND_URL}/profile?linked=1 — pin it to
      # the Playwright next-dev origin so the round-trip lands on the frontend (not
      # the API origin) and passes _safe_redirect_url's same-origin check.
      FRONTEND_URL: http://localhost:3000
      E2E_ADMIN_LOGIN_ID: e2e-admin
      E2E_API_URL: http://localhost:8080
      NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL: http://localhost:8080
      # #1500: wait-for-api.sh reads the boot-phase INFO lines from the API log.
      LOG_LEVEL: INFO
      # OAuth test-IdP harness (#937): redirect the server-side GitHub exchange
      # at the Playwright-managed mock IdP on :9100.
      OAUTH_ENDPOINT_OVERRIDE_ENABLED: "true"
      OAUTH_GITHUB_AUTH_URL: http://localhost:9100/github/login/oauth/authorize
      OAUTH_GITHUB_TOKEN_URL: http://localhost:9100/github/login/oauth/access_token
      OAUTH_GITHUB_USER_URL: http://localhost:9100/github/user
      OAUTH_GITHUB_EMAILS_URL: http://localhost:9100/github/user/emails
      GITHUB_CLIENT_ID: e2e-mock-client-id
      GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET: e2e-mock-client-secret
      GITHUB_REDIRECT_URI: http://localhost:8080/api/v1/auth/github/callback
      # The GitHub callback guards on `_oauth2_manager`, which main.py only
      # initializes when GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID is set — so the GitHub-only flow still
      # needs a (dummy) Google client id or the callback 500s "Auth managers not
      # initialized". Non-secret throwaway values for an ephemeral CI run.
      GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID: e2e-mock-google-client-id
      GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET: e2e-mock-google-client-secret
      # #1655: the beta-invite hand-off spec mints an invite and redeems it
      # through the gate (which the spec turns on in manual mode itself).
      ENABLE_BETA_INVITES: "true"
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:18.4-alpine@sha256:9a8afca54e7861fd90fab5fdf4c42477a6b1cb7d293595148e674e0a3181de15
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: kagura
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: kagura_dev_password
          POSTGRES_DB: kagura_test
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U kagura -d kagura_test"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
      redis:
        image: redis:7-alpine
        ports:
          - 6379:6379
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "redis-cli ping"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0 # v7.1.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"

      # uv is pinned in lockstep with backend/pyproject.toml [tool.uv]
      # required-version, backend/Dockerfile and setup.sh (#1706);
      # tests/test_uv_version_lockstep.py enforces it. The cache is keyed on
      # backend/uv.lock, so a lock change is the only thing that refills it.
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          version: "0.11.19"
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: backend/uv.lock

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: "24"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json

      - name: Install backend dependencies
        # From the lock, never a fresh resolution: --locked fails when uv.lock
        # is out of date with pyproject.toml (#1706). The venv goes on PATH so
        # the pytest / alembic / python steps below run unchanged.
        run: |
          cd backend
          uv sync --locked --extra dev
          echo "$PWD/.venv/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Install frontend dependencies
        run: cd frontend && npm ci

      - name: Install Playwright browser
        run: cd frontend && npx playwright install chromium --with-deps

      - name: Generate ephemeral secrets + admin password
        run: |
          {
            echo "API_KEY_SECRET=$(python -c 'from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())')"
            echo "AUDIT_HMAC_KEY=$(python -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))')"
            echo "E2E_ADMIN_PASSWORD=Ci-$(python -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(18))')-9X"
          } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Migrate schema
        run: cd backend && alembic upgrade head

      - name: Seed e2e admin
        run: cd backend && python -m src.cli.seed_e2e_admin

      - name: Start API server
        # Logged to a file so the readiness gate can read the boot phases.
        run: |
          cd backend
          python -m uvicorn src.api.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 --log-level warning \
            > "$RUNNER_TEMP/api.log" 2>&1 &
          echo "API_PID=$!" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Wait for API readiness
        # #1500: a slow or crashed boot fails HERE, naming its phase — see
        # .github/scripts/wait-for-api.sh.
        id: wait_api
        run: .github/scripts/wait-for-api.sh "$API_PID" "$RUNNER_TEMP/api.log"

      - name: Run OAuth E2E (account linking, beta invite hand-off)
        run: cd frontend && npm run test:e2e:oauth

      - name: Run passkey E2E with a Chromium virtual authenticator
        run: cd frontend && npx playwright test --project=passkey

      - name: Show API log
        # The readiness step already dumps the log when it is the one failing.
        if: ${{ failure() && steps.wait_api.outcome != 'failure' }}
        run: tail -n 100 "$RUNNER_TEMP/api.log" || true

      - name: Upload Playwright report
        if: ${{ failure() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: playwright-report-oauth
          path: frontend/playwright-report/
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 7

  # Builds the api and web images and checks what they carry (#2763).
  # backend/tests/ci/test_image_contents.py reads the Dockerfiles; this job runs
  # the built images, so a base image or a dependency that brings in a compiler,
  # the dev extra or a package manager fails here as well. Gated like
  # backend-integration: a change to what goes into the images, and
  # workflow_dispatch (a release pull request changes the lock files, so it
  # runs there). Nothing is pushed: publishing happens outside this
  # repository.
  images:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [detect-changes]
    if: |
      needs.detect-changes.outputs.images == 'true' ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # No --target: the production compose files build the api's last stage,
      # which test_image_contents.py keeps as `runtime`. No layer cache: the job
      # runs when the image inputs change, so a cache would rarely hit, and the
      # repository's cache budget is the other jobs'.
      - name: Build the api image
        id: build_api
        run: docker build --pull -t kagura-api:ci backend

      # Throwaway NEXT_PUBLIC_* values: they are compiled into the bundle and do
      # not change which tools and packages the image carries.
      - name: Build the web image
        id: build_web
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: >-
          docker build --pull -t kagura-web:ci
          --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:8080
          --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=http://localhost:3000
          frontend

      - name: Check what the api image carries
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && steps.build_api.outcome == 'success' }}
        run: .github/scripts/check-image-contents.sh api kagura-api:ci

      - name: Check what the web image carries
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && steps.build_web.outcome == 'success' }}
        run: .github/scripts/check-image-contents.sh web kagura-web:ci

sampled_files.README.md:
Kagura Memory Cloud

Your next AI conversation starts with what you already know.
Shared, persistent memory for people, teams, and AI agents.
Open source · Self-hostable · MCP + REST API

English · 日本語

Open in ChatGPT · Request a cloud invite · Self-host · Benchmarks · Documentation

## Keep the context. Change the conversation. > **DolphinBench: 455 of 600 tasks (75.8%), self-tested on November 23, 2026.** With Hermes and GPT 5.6 Luna, Kagura Memory Cloud passed more tasks than each memory system in the benchmark's published Hermes + Luna results (Mem0 424, Hindsight 417, Honcho 411). The run is self-reported and awaits the maintainers' review: [run record](https://github.com/mem0ai/dolphinbench/pull/16) · [evidence](https://github.com/kagura-ai/dolphinbench/releases/tag/kagura-memory-cloud-hermes-20261123) · [comparison](#dolphinbench-memory-for-an-agent-that-acts). > **OpenAI Plugin released:** [Kagura Memory Cloud is available in ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6adacc9eaf5481919a85fad2aaa7aade). Add the plugin and sign in to Kagura to save and recall memories in your conversations. See [supported platforms](#supported-platforms) for the other ways to connect. You explained the project yesterday. Today you open a new chat, switch AI tools, or hand work to a teammate. The decisions and their reasons should come with you. **Kagura Memory Cloud gives your assistants a shared place to remember and recall that knowledge.** Save a decision in one session; retrieve it in another client connected to the same workspace and context. Browse, edit, and organize the memories in the web UI. It works with **ChatGPT, Claude, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Muse, Grok, and Microsoft 365 Copilot**. Use the published ChatGPT plugin or connect a compatible client over MCP. Applications can also use the REST API or [Python SDK](https://github.com/kagura-ai/kagura-memory-python-sdk). | When you… | Use shared memory to… | |---|---| | Resume a project | Recover decisions, constraints, and unresolved work. | | Switch AI assistants | Reuse the same project knowledge across tools. | | Work with a team | Share knowledge through workspace and context roles. | | Change a decision | Replace an outdated memory and retain its history. | | Build an agent | Retrieve relevant context without sending the entire conversation log. |


See memory retrieval in action — watch the demo.

## Quick start ### Choose how to try it | | Start here | What you need | |---|---|---| | **Hosted Kagura AI** | [Request an invite](https://www.kagura-ai.com/waitlist/) · [Connect your AI client](https://www.kagura-ai.com/help/connect/) | An invited account and a compatible AI client. Cloud registration is currently invite-only. | | **Self-hosted Memory Cloud** | Run the setup below | Docker Compose, Python 3.11+, Bash, and an embedding provider. | ### Supported platforms | Client | Start here | |---|---| | **ChatGPT — released OpenAI Plugin** | [Add Kagura Memory Cloud](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6adacc9eaf5481919a85fad2aaa7aade), then sign in to your Kagura AI account. | | **Claude / Claude Desktop** | [Connect over remote MCP](docs/mcp-clients.md#claude-desktop--claude-chat-web) and sign in to Kagura. | | **Claude Code** | [Connect MCP](docs/mcp-clients.md#claude-code-recommended); add the optional plugin for session workflows. | | **Codex** | [Connect MCP and install the optional skill plugin](docs/getting-started.md#codex-cli). | | **Cursor** | [Add the MCP server in Cursor settings](docs/getting-started.md#cursor). | | **Gemini / Gemini CLI** | Use a [custom MCP connector](docs/mcp-clients.md#gemini-custom-mcp-connector) or the [CLI configuration](docs/mcp-clients.md#gemini-cli). | | **Muse** | [Add a remote MCP server](docs/mcp-clients.md#muse) and sign in to Kagura. | | **Grok / Grok Bot** | [Connect over remote MCP](docs/mcp-clients.md#grok--grok-bot) and sign in to Kagura. | | **Microsoft 365 Copilot** | [Connect through MCP and OAuth](docs/microsoft-365-copilot.md), with operator setup of the OAuth client and Microsoft registration. | | **Other MCP clients / your own apps** | Use [Streamable HTTP or the REST API](docs/mcp-clients.md#other-mcp-clients--rest-api). | The published ChatGPT plugin connects to hosted Kagura AI and requires an account. For your own Memory Cloud deployment, use the [custom MCP connection instructions](docs/mcp-clients.md#chatgpt-desktop). ### Run locally On Linux, macOS, or Windows with WSL2, with Docker running: ```bash git clone https://github.com/kagura-ai/memory-cloud.git cd memory-cloud bash setup.sh ``` The interactive setup generates configuration secrets, installs the pinned Python dependencies and Kagura CLI, starts the services, runs migrations, and creates an admin account and MCP configuration. It uses `curl` if it needs to install `uv`. Node.js runs inside Docker; a host Node.js installation is only needed for frontend development. **Memory search needs embeddings:** configure an OpenAI API key or a reachable self-hosted embedding server. Google/GitHub sign-in is optional; the local admin can use a password and MFA. See the [setup guide](docs/getting-started.md) for manual steps and provider configuration. | Open | Purpose | |---|---| | [localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) | Sign in and manage your memories. | | `http://localhost:8080/mcp` | Connect a local MCP client. | | [localhost:8080/redoc](http://localhost:8080/redoc) | Explore the running server's REST API. | The root Compose stack is for local development. For a public server, use the [deployment guide](docs/deployment.md). ### Try your first memory 1. In the web UI, create a context named **my-first-project**. A context groups memories for a project or topic. 2. Connect your AI client using [MCP Client Setup](docs/mcp-clients.md). For Claude Code, setup generates a local `.mcp.json`; restart the client to load it. Other clients have their own configuration. Web-based clients need a reachable HTTPS server, rather than your machine's `localhost`. 3. Ask the assistant: > In Kagura's my-first-project context, remember: we chose PostgreSQL because the app needs transactions and relational queries. 4. Open a **new conversation** with the connected client and ask: > Search Kagura's my-first-project context. Which database did we choose, and why? Look for the saved memory in the web UI and a recall tool call in the new conversation. Then repeat the question in another client with access to the same context. Kagura stores what you or an integration explicitly saves. Connecting a client does not automatically import all of its past chats. Keep credentials out of memories and version control. ## Benchmarks: accuracy and cost together How much history does an assistant need to answer well? Our [public benchmark report](https://www.kagura-ai.com/ja/benchmarks/) measures answer quality as well as cost. | LoCoMo, 472 questions across 3 conversations | KMC v0.152.0 | Full conversation input | |---|---:|---:| | Answer accuracy, strict grading | **84.2%** | 89.0% | | Memory tokens read at answer time | **80% fewer** | Baseline | | Answer-time model cost | **66% lower** | Baseline | These are developer-run, preregistered results from November 10, 2026, excluding adversarial questions. Costs exclude memory construction and service fees. The tradeoff includes lower accuracy than full-history input; these are not official full-dataset scores or a guarantee for your workload. A November 12 rerun of **v0.156.0** scored **91.3% with lenient grading / 83.7% with strict grading**. It reused the same conversations after tuning and was not preregistered. Keep it separate from the original run and its cost measurements. ### DolphinBench: memory for an agent that acts [DolphinBench](https://github.com/mem0ai/dolphinbench) gives an agent three people's histories (13,539 messages) and then 600 tasks in simulated apps; a task passes only if the agent acts correctly on what it should remember. We ran it with the benchmark's Hermes setup and GPT 5.6 Luna, with Kagura Memory Cloud as the memory. | Memory (Hermes + GPT 5.6 Luna) | Tasks passed, of 600 | Source | |---|---:|---| | **Kagura Memory Cloud v0.156.0** | **455 (75.8%)** | Self-tested, November 23, 2026; [under review](https://github.com/mem0ai/dolphinbench/pull/16) | | Mem0 | 424 (70.7%) | Published by the benchmark | | Hindsight | 417 (69.5%) | Published by the benchmark | | Honcho | 411 (68.5%) | Published by the benchmark | | Hermes built-in memory | 394 (65.7%) | Published by the benchmark | | Supermemory | 355 (59.2%) | Published by the benchmark | Read the comparison with these limits: - **Self-tested.** The benchmark's maintainers have not verified our run. The published rows are theirs. - **Not held out.** We chose the plugin's recall settings after reading failures on the public tasks. - **Judge route.** The judge is the benchmark's model, settings and prompts, sent through the OpenAI API instead of Azure. - **Cost.** $97.90 of agent tokens at the benchmark's prices. The memory server's own models ran self-hosted and are not included. - **Other self-tested runs** awaiting review report 451 to 504 tasks, most with a different harness. Everything needed to check the score is public: the [run record and method note](https://github.com/kagura-ai/dolphinbench/blob/kagura-memory-cloud-hermes-20261123/docs/submissions/kagura-memory-cloud-hermes-20261123.md), the [evidence ZIP](https://github.com/kagura-ai/dolphinbench/releases/tag/kagura-memory-cloud-hermes-20261123) with all 600 task conversations and saved judge answers, and the plugin and adapter source at the same tag. **Evaluation is ongoing.** We are running additional evaluations and working to improve memory retrieval and answer accuracy. The published results above reflect the tested versions and conditions. See the [benchmark reading guide](docs/benchmarks.md) for FC and LongMemEval results, comparison limits, and the distinction between answer accuracy and retrieval metrics. [English public report](https://www.kagura-ai.com/benchmarks/) · [日本語・LoCoMo詳細](https://www.kagura-ai.com/ja/benchmarks/) ## What you get | Capability | How it helps | |---|---| | **Hybrid retrieval** | Semantic search + BM25 keyword matching, with optional reranking. | | **Memory you can maintain** | Update, supersede, inspect revisions, and remove outdated knowledge. | | **Session continuity** | Bootstrap a session with context, pinned notes, upcoming items, and recent changes. | | **Related-memory discovery** | Explore a graph of related memories; supported searches can strengthen associations. | | **Team controls** | Workspaces, private/shared contexts, roles, and scoped credentials. | | **Web management** | Search and edit memories, inspect history, manage members and integrations. | | **Your deployment choice** | Self-host the Apache-licensed server and choose your embedding provider. Model and infrastructure costs depend on that choice. | ### MCP tools Start with `remember`, `recall`, and `reference`. Session tools such as `bootstrap` and `changes_since` help an agent pick up previous work. Use `update_memory` or supersession when a fact changes. The default `/mcp` endpoint lists the core tools. Add `?profile=full` for the full catalog, or `?add_tools=explore` for graph exploration. Tool visibility and access permissions are separate; workspace and context roles still apply. See [tool profiles and roles](docs/mcp-tools.md#tool-profiles). ### Getting started with Claude Code Once MCP is connected, the optional plugin adds guided session and memory workflows. In Claude Code: ```text /plugin marketplace add kagura-ai/memory-cloud /plugin install kagura-memory@kagura-memory-cloud ``` Use `/kagura-memory:session-start` when you return to a project and `/kagura-memory:session-summary` to save useful knowledge before leaving. `/kagura-memory:recall`, `:remember`, and `:maintain` support day-to-day use. Installation and hook configuration are covered in [MCP Client Setup](docs/mcp-clients.md); Codex users have a [separate plugin setup](docs/getting-started.md#codex-cli). ## How it works ```text People and AI clients ── MCP / REST ── Kagura Memory Cloud ├─ Workspace → contexts → memories ├─ PostgreSQL: records, keywords, graph ├─ Qdrant: semantic retrieval └─ Web UI: browse, edit, share ``` `recall` finds relevant memories through hybrid search. `explore` follows relationships for discovery. Keeping these paths separate lets you choose direct retrieval or related knowledge. Background [Sleep Maintenance](docs/sleep-maintenance.md) consolidates memory according to configuration. Built with **FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Qdrant, Redis, and Next.js**. Read the [architecture](docs/architecture.md) and [core concepts](docs/concepts.md) for the underlying design. ## Documentation | I want to… | Read | |---|---| | Install and save my first memory | [Getting Started](docs/getting-started.md) | | Connect an AI client | [MCP Client Setup](docs/mcp-clients.md) | | Build an integration | [MCP Tools](docs/mcp-tools.md) · [REST API](docs/api-reference.md) · [Python SDK](https://github.com/kagura-ai/kagura-memory-python-sdk) | | Write useful memories | [Chunking Guide](docs/chunking-guide.md) · [Core Concepts](docs/concepts.md) | | Evaluate quality | [Benchmarks](docs/benchmarks.md) | | Deploy and operate | [Deployment](docs/deployment.md) · [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md) | | Find a specialist guide | [Documentation index](docs/README.md) | | See what changed | [Releases](https://github.com/kagura-ai/memory-cloud/releases) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) | ## Contribute Bug reports, documentation improvements, and contributions are welcome. Start with [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Report vulnerabilities through [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## License [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE).

# Kagura Memory Cloud - Local Development
#
# Usage:
#   docker compose up -d
#
# Access:
#   API:      http://localhost:8080
#   Frontend: http://localhost:3000 (run separately: cd frontend && npm run dev)
#   MCP:      http://localhost:8080/mcp
#
# Data-store ports (postgres 5432, qdrant 6333/6334, redis 6379, minio
# 9000/9001, clamav 3310) are published on 127.0.0.1 only (#1626): Redis and
# Qdrant run without auth here, Postgres uses the .env.example default
# password, clamd's protocol has no auth at all, and a port Docker publishes
# bypasses host firewalls such as ufw. The localhost URLs
# in .env.example are unaffected. To let another machine reach them, prefer an
# SSH port-forward to this host's loopback; otherwise set COMPOSE_BIND_HOST
# (shell or the project `.env` — Compose interpolation does not read
# .env.local): COMPOSE_BIND_HOST=0.0.0.0 docker compose up -d
# Guarded by terraform/single-server/scripts/tests/compose_port_bind.bats.

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # Database Services
  # ==========================================================================
  # PostgreSQL (Primary DB + Graph memory)
  postgres:
    # Pinned by multi-arch manifest-list digest (#1302). The 18+ Docker image
    # moved PGDATA to /var/lib/postgresql/18/docker and the volume target to
    # /var/lib/postgresql — never mount a PG15-era data volume here.
    # Migration/rollback: docs/ops/postgres-18-migration-runbook.md
    image: postgres:18.4-alpine@sha256:9a8afca54e7861fd90fab5fdf4c42477a6b1cb7d293595148e674e0a3181de15
    container_name: kagura-postgres
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: kagura
      POSTGRES_USER: kagura
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD:-kagura_dev_password}
      # Pin UTC at the OS + Postgres session layer — see
      # .claude/rules/backend.md for the three-layer policy.
      TZ: UTC
      PGTZ: UTC
    ports:
      - "${COMPOSE_BIND_HOST:-127.0.0.1}:5432:5432"
    volumes:
      # PG18+ mounts the parent dir, not .../data. Fresh volume: local data
      # from the old postgres_data (PG15) volume is not carried over — after
      # first start, rebuild the schema with
      #   docker exec kagura-api alembic upgrade head
      # (`make migrate` needs a host venv) or restore a dump.
      - postgres_data_18:/var/lib/postgresql
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U kagura -d postgres"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 30s

  # Qdrant (Vector DB)
  qdrant:
    # Pinned together with qdrant-client in backend/pyproject.toml (#1535,
    # #1793). A volume from an older release cannot start on this image
    # directly: upgrade it one minor at a time — docs/ops/qdrant-upgrade-runbook.md
    image: qdrant/qdrant:v1.19.1
    container_name: kagura-qdrant
    # Qdrant opens many files per segment (seen on 1.15); under eval-scale ingest/delete
    # churn the default container nofile limit is exhausted (EMFILE crash-loop
    # at actix worker startup, os error 24 — observed 2026-07-08 on a GB10 rig
    # after the collection grew to 8 segments). 65536 gives ample headroom.
    ulimits:
      nofile:
        soft: 65536
        hard: 65536
    ports:
      - "${COMPOSE_BIND_HOST:-127.0.0.1}:6333:6333"
      - "${COMPOSE_BIND_HOST:-127.0.0.1}:6334:6334"
    volumes:
      - qdrant_data:/qdrant/storage
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "timeout 10s bash -c ':> /dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/6333' || exit 1"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 10s

  # Redis (Cache)
  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    container_name: kagura-redis
    ports:
      - "${COMPOSE_BIND_HOST:-127.0.0.1}:6379:6379"
    volumes:
      - redis_data:/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 5

  # Backend API
  api:
    build:
      context: ./backend
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
      # The dev extra (pytest for `make test`) is only in this stage (#2620).
      target: dev
    container_name: kagura-api
    env_file:
      - .env.local
    environment:
      # Database (local docker postgres - async driver)
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql+asyncpg://kagura:${DB_PASSWORD:-kagura_dev_password}@postgres:5432/kagura

      # Qdrant (Vector DB)
      QDRANT_URL: http://qdrant:6333

      # Redis (Cache)
      REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379

      # OAuth2 - Let .env.local handle these
      # GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET are read from .env.local
      GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI: http://localhost:8080/api/v1/auth/google/callback

      # Security — values from .env.local (via env_file above)
      # API_KEY_SECRET, AUDIT_HMAC_KEY, AUDIT_PSEUDO_SALT are read from .env.local

      # API Settings
      API_HOST: 0.0.0.0
      API_PORT: 8080
      LOG_LEVEL: ${LOG_LEVEL:-info}
      LOG_COLORIZE: "true"
      PYTHONUNBUFFERED: "1"

      # CORS
      CORS_ORIGINS: ${CORS_ORIGINS:-http://localhost:3000,http://localhost:8080}
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      qdrant:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
    volumes:
      - ./backend/src:/app/src  # Hot reload
      - ./backend/tests:/app/tests
    command: uvicorn src.api.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 --reload --log-level info --use-colors

  # Frontend (Next.js dev server)
  web:
    image: node:24-alpine
    container_name: kagura-web-dev
    working_dir: /app
    environment:
      NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL: http://localhost:8080
      NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED: "1"
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    volumes:
      - ./frontend:/app
      - frontend_node_modules:/app/node_modules
    command: sh -c "npm install && npx next dev --hostname 0.0.0.0"
    depends_on:
      - api

  # MinIO — S3-compatible object storage for self-host / local BYO-storage
  # testing (Issue #994). Opt-in via the `minio` profile so it does NOT start
  # with a default `docker compose up`:
  #   docker compose --profile minio up -d minio
  # Then point the API at it with STORAGE_BACKEND_TYPE=minio,
  # STORAGE_ENDPOINT_URL=http://minio:9000, STORAGE_ACCESS_KEY_ID/SECRET=minioadmin,
  # STORAGE_BUCKET=kagura-files-dev. The legacy R2_* names still work as aliases.
  #
  # ⚠ SECURITY — DEV DEFAULTS ONLY. The minioadmin/minioadmin credentials and the
  # loopback-published 9000/9001 ports below are for LOCAL development only. For
  # a real self-host deployment you MUST: (1) set strong unique MINIO_ROOT_USER /
  # MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD (or, better, per-app access keys with bucket-scoped
  # policy), and (2) NOT expose these ports publicly — front MinIO with TLS and
  # keep it on the private network. Copying this block to production unchanged
  # (or with COMPOSE_BIND_HOST=0.0.0.0) leaves an open, default-credentialed
  # object store (OWASP A05).
  minio:
    # Chainguard's MinIO build, pinned by digest (#1691): the minio/minio images
    # on Docker Hub and quay.io are no longer pullable anonymously. Keep in sync
    # with the "Start MinIO" step in .github/workflows/ci.yml.
    image: cgr.dev/chainguard/minio@sha256:bd014394a80898e68c149f2311fdf8d5a2c2f3bb2c33b9327ae6d02b4b065ae1
    container_name: kagura-minio
    profiles: ["minio"]
    # The image runs as a non-root user by default. The previous image ran as
    # root, so an existing minio_data volume is root-owned; run as root to keep
    # those volumes writable.
    user: "0:0"
    command: server /data --console-address ":9001"
    environment:
      MINIO_ROOT_USER: minioadmin
      MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD: minioadmin
    ports:
      - "${COMPOSE_BIND_HOST:-127.0.0.1}:9000:9000"
      - "${COMPOSE_BIND_HOST:-127.0.0.1}:9001:9001"
    volumes:
      - minio_data:/data
    healthcheck:
      # The image ships bash but no curl, wget or grep: probe the liveness
      # endpoint over bash's /dev/tcp and require an HTTP 200 status line.
      test:
        - "CMD"
        - "bash"
        - "-c"
        - "exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/9000 && printf 'GET /minio/health/live HTTP/1.1\\r\\nHost: localhost\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\\r\\n' >&3 && read -r status <&3 && [[ $$status == *' 200 '* ]]"
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 10s

  # ClamAV (clamd + freshclam) for the upload malware scan (Issue #565). Opt-in
  # via the `clamav` profile, like minio:
  #   docker compose --profile clamav up -d clamav
  # It needs about 3-4 GiB of RAM (ClamAV's documented minimum / preferred)
  # and outbound HTTPS for signature updates. Then set FILE_SCAN_ENABLED=true
  # and CLAMD_HOST=clamav in .env.local (CLAMD_HOST=localhost for an API run
  # on the host). Same image and clamd.conf as the production overlay
  # (terraform/single-server/docker-compose.clamav.yml); see
  # docs/deployment.md "Upload malware scanning (ClamAV)".
  clamav:
    image: clamav/clamav:1.4.6-debian@sha256:aedee9daad6b069b26adad61af7ec50a41efe33fd8eff7f985c1f31e3a6ae9de
    container_name: kagura-clamav
    profiles: ["clamav"]
    ports:
      - "${COMPOSE_BIND_HOST:-127.0.0.1}:3310:3310"
    volumes:
      - clamav_data:/var/lib/clamav
      - ./terraform/single-server/clamav/clamd.conf:/etc/clamav/clamd.conf:ro
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "clamdcheck.sh"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10m

volumes:
  postgres_data_18:
  qdrant_data:
  redis_data:
  frontend_node_modules:
  minio_data:
  clamav_data:

decision_reasons: High-severity capability requires manual security review
