repository.description: Rapid-MLX is an open-source (Apache 2.0) OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible LLM inference server for Apple Silicon, built on MLX, focused on reliable tool calling for coding agents. Up to 4× faster than Apple's MLX (mlx-lm) on the same weights.
repository.name: Rapid-MLX
repository.readme:
Rapid-MLX

Run Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Pi, Hermes, Crush or Goose with a local model on Mac:
rapid-mlx launch <agent>

**1. Install** — the guided installer handles Python and picks a model for your Mac: ```bash curl -fsSL https://rapidmlx.com/install.sh | bash ``` Restart your terminal or run `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"`. Prefer [pip (Python 3.12+)](#alternative-install-methods) or Homebrew (`brew install rapid-mlx`)? Both install the same CLI. **2. Launch your coding agent** — install your chosen agent, then run one of: Using an SDK instead? [Jump to the Python quickstart](#python-quickstart). ```bash rapid-mlx launch claude-code rapid-mlx launch opencode rapid-mlx launch codex ``` `rapid-mlx launch ` creates a private profile, starts the server, and launches the agent. Run the same command tomorrow; `rapid-mlx launch claude-code --remove` removes Rapid's private profile without changing your existing Claude Code settings. [One-command guides for each agent](https://rapidmlx.com/docs/agents/). A first reply can take longer while a model downloads, loads, or processes the agent's opening prompt. For other tools, use `rapid-mlx agents --setup`, for example `rapid-mlx agents cline --setup`.

Rapid-MLX is an open-source (Apache 2.0) OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible LLM inference server for Apple Silicon, built on MLX, focused on reliable tool calling for coding agents.
Up to 4× faster than Apple's MLX (mlx-lm), 1.5× on a typical task — same model, same weights.
Decode speed, Qwen3.5-9B 4-bit on a Mac mini M4 Pro, greedy decoding, both servers at their defaults — per-task results, method, and raw data.

**Faster decode than oMLX and LM Studio on Qwen3.5-9B, Qwen3.8-27B, and Qwen3.6-35B** Measured speed on a Mac Studio M5 Max (36 GB) — Rapid-MLX 0.16.1 vs oMLX 0.7.0 and LM Studio, using the same base 4-bit weights for each model. | Model | Metric | Rapid-MLX | oMLX | LM Studio | |---|---|---:|---:|---:| | Qwen3.5-9B | Decode (tok/s) | **115.5** | 77.9 | 81.0 | | Qwen3.5-9B | 4 streams (tok/s) | **248.2** | 224.6 | 230.0 | | Qwen3.8-27B | Decode (tok/s) | **37.9** | 25.3 | 26.0 | | Qwen3.8-27B | 4 streams (tok/s) | **82.8** | 75.3 | 69.7 | | Qwen3.6-35B | Decode (tok/s) | **173.4** | 145.8 | 124.5 | | Qwen3.6-35B | 4 streams (tok/s) | **293.9** | 281.9 | 265.6 | | Qwen3.6-35B | 2K-prompt first token (s, lower is better) | **0.55** | 1.14 | 1.49 | Single run per engine; default serving modes with Rapid's MTP text mode, oMLX's SSD cache, and LM Studio's configured context and four parallel slots. [Full results and raw data](https://rapidmlx.com/compare). **Or use the OpenAI / Anthropic SDK** Start a local server, then run the Python examples below from a separate terminal: ```bash rapid-mlx serve qwen3.5-4b-4bit --port 8000 ``` On first run, this command downloads a ~3 GB 4B model if it is not already cached. Without `--port`, the server picks the first free port in `8000`–`8009`; these examples pin `8000`. Install your SDK with `pip install openai` or `pip install anthropic`. OpenAI Python — base URL includes `/v1`: ```python from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1", api_key="not-needed") print(client.chat.completions.create( model="default", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello"}], ).choices[0].message.content) ``` Anthropic Python — base URL is the host; the SDK calls `/v1/messages`: ```python from anthropic import Anthropic client = Anthropic(base_url="http://localhost:8000", api_key="not-needed") msg = client.messages.create( model="default", max_tokens=256, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello"}], ) print("".join(b.text for b in msg.content if b.type == "text")) ```

rapidmlx.com · Docs · Model mirror · Desktop app · Discord

--- ## How it compares Feature facts only, taken mostly from each project's own documentation as of 2026-09-26 (sources below). For speed, see the measured results above. | | Rapid-MLX | [oMLX](https://github.com/jundot/omlx) | [Ollama](https://github.com/ollama/ollama) | [LM Studio](https://lmstudio.ai) | [mlx-lm](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm) (`mlx_lm.server`) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | **License** | Apache-2.0 | Apache-2.0 | MIT | Closed-source app; its MLX engine and `lms` CLI are MIT | MIT | | **Inference engine on a Mac** | MLX | MLX | GGML/GGUF engine, plus an MLX engine for safetensors models | llama.cpp (GGUF) and MLX engines | MLX | | **Local API** | OpenAI (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`) and Anthropic Messages (`/v1/messages`) | OpenAI and Anthropic Messages | Ollama API, OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic-compatible (subset) | OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic-compatible, LM Studio REST API | OpenAI-style chat API | | **GUI** | Rapid-MLX Desktop (macOS app) | macOS menu-bar app and web admin panel | Desktop app (macOS, Windows) | Desktop app | None (CLI / Python) | | **Concurrent requests** | Continuous batching | Continuous batching (mlx-lm `BatchGenerator`) | Parallel requests per model (`OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL`, default 1) | Continuous batching (llama.cpp engine; MLX engine since 0.4.2) | Continuous batching (`BatchGenerator`); one request at a time with a quantized KV cache | | **Prompt / KV cache** | Radix prefix cache in memory (with state snapshots for hybrid models), saved to disk on shutdown and restored at startup; quantized KV cache | Tiered KV cache: in-memory hot tier plus SSD cold tier, reused across restarts | Reuses the previous request's prompt KV cache; KV cache quantization (`OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE`) | — | In-memory prompt cache; quantized KV cache (`--kv-bits`) | | **Tool-call parsing** | 27 parser modules, including an auto-detect fallback ([`rapid_mlx/tool_parsers`](https://github.com/raullenchai/Rapid-MLX/tree/main/rapid_mlx/tool_parsers)) | mlx-lm formats plus the auto-detected families listed in its README | [Tool calling](https://docs.ollama.com/capabilities/tool-calling) | [Tool use](https://lmstudio.ai/docs/developer/openai-compat/tools) via the OpenAI-compatible API | Tool calls for models whose tokenizer declares tool-calling support | Sources: [oMLX README](https://github.com/jundot/omlx#readme) · Ollama [OpenAI](https://docs.ollama.com/api/openai-compatibility) and [Anthropic](https://docs.ollama.com/api/anthropic-compatibility) compatibility, [FAQ](https://docs.ollama.com/faq), [MLX engine](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/development.md#mlx-engine-optional) · LM Studio [Anthropic compatibility](https://lmstudio.ai/docs/developer/anthropic-compat), [parallel requests](https://lmstudio.ai/docs/app/advanced/parallel-requests), [0.4.2 changelog](https://lmstudio.ai/changelog/lmstudio-v0.4.2), [app terms](https://lmstudio.ai/app-terms), [mlx-engine](https://github.com/lmstudio-ai/mlx-engine) · [mlx-lm server docs](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm/blob/main/mlx_lm/SERVER.md) and [`server.py`](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm/blob/main/mlx_lm/server.py). Ollama prompt-cache reuse is from our [benchmark notes](https://rapidmlx.com/blog/assets/engine-bench-2026-08/results.json). — = not verified for this table. Spot an error? Please [open an issue](https://github.com/raullenchai/Rapid-MLX/issues). vs Apple's mlx-lm: per-task results and raw data at https://rapidmlx.com/compare/mlx-lm. --- ## Works with your AI stack Use Rapid-MLX as a local backend for agents, apps, or your own code. If a client accepts an OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible endpoint, it can usually use Rapid-MLX without an adapter. For Claude Desktop, [set up its in-app Gateway](https://rapidmlx.com/docs/claude-desktop/).

Five Tier-1 agents are exercised end-to-end on real weights before release. See the [tested compatibility matrix](https://rapidmlx.com/docs/matrix.html) for exact API coverage and setup status. Docker Agent documents Rapid-MLX as a local provider; see the [Docker Agent setup page](https://docker.github.io/docker-agent/providers/rapid-mlx/) for the provider definition. --- ## Install ### Desktop — macOS (Apple Silicon) The easiest way to chat locally, manage models, and use vision, files, voice, and image generation from one app. - [Download Rapid-MLX Desktop](https://rapidmlx.com/desktop) - [Browse signed Desktop releases](https://github.com/raullenchai/Rapid-MLX/releases?q=rapid-mac-v) - Requires an M-series Mac; Windows and Linux desktop builds are not available yet - [Share Compute setup and credit ledger](https://github.com/raullenchai/Rapid-MLX/blob/main/docs/guides/share-compute.md) In **Settings → Performance**, inspect system memory, engine Metal allocations, prefix-cache usage, running and waiting requests, and a recent memory trend. Engine allocations overlap system totals; do not add them together. Missing measurements appear as a dash. After a chat reply, expand **Generation details** for saved execution facts and timing. Model recommendations, `rapid-mlx models`, and `rapid-mlx doctor` show measured speed references when a matching chip, RAM, and configuration are available. These references describe measured workloads, not guaranteed speed. ### CLI and server — macOS (Apple Silicon) ```bash # Homebrew — prebuilt bottle from homebrew-core brew install rapid-mlx # Or the guided installer — detects RAM and offers to start a chat (RAPID_INSTALL_NO_CHAT=1 skips) curl -fsSL https://rapidmlx.com/install.sh | bash ``` Both install the same `rapid-mlx` CLI. Prefer `uv` or `pip`, or want to verify the installer before running it? See [alternative install methods](#alternative-install-methods) and [install security](https://github.com/raullenchai/Rapid-MLX/blob/main/SECURITY.md). The guided installer prefers a runnable model already cached on this Mac when it fits the RAM tier. Otherwise its quick first-chat download is `lfm2.5-2.6b-4bit` at 8 GB or above, with `lfm2.5-1b-4bit` for smaller or unknown RAM. Larger quality picks remain available through `rapid-mlx recipe` and the model picker. --- ## Submit a Community Benchmark Help other Mac users choose a model by sharing a standardized result from your own Apple Silicon Mac. Runs stay local until you explicitly choose to publish; you do not need a GitHub account or a benchmark JSON pull request. - **Desktop:** Open the **Benchmark** tab in the sidebar, choose a model, run it, review the result in **My Results**, and select **Publish** if you want to share it. - **CLI:** Run `rapid-mlx benchmark catalog`, then `rapid-mlx benchmark run `. Review the saved result and publish it with `rapid-mlx benchmark share ` only if you choose to. Explore the [Community Benchmark leaderboard](https://rapidmlx.com/leaderboard) or read the [protocol and privacy details](https://github.com/raullenchai/Rapid-MLX/blob/main/community-benchmarks/README.md). --- ## Quick Start (60 seconds) **1. Chat with a model right now:** ```bash rapid-mlx chat ``` With no model named, `rapid-mlx chat` uses a chat model already on this Mac — the `lfm2.5-2.6b-4bit` starter if present, otherwise the best fit for this Mac's memory — without another download. If none is downloaded yet, it downloads the `lfm2.5-2.6b-4bit` starter (~1.6 GB) before opening the REPL. Type `/help` for slash commands, `/exit` to quit. **2. Or serve it for use from other apps:** ```bash rapid-mlx serve qwen3.5-4b-4bit ``` Starts an OpenAI-compatible HTTP server on the first free port in `8000`–`8009` when `--port` is omitted. An explicit `--port` never falls back. The examples below assume port `8000` was selected. Point any client that supports a local custom endpoint (Aider, LangChain, OpenCode, PydanticAI, your own scripts) at **`http://localhost:8000/v1`**; Claude Code / Anthropic SDK uses **`http://localhost:8000`** (the Anthropic messages route lives at `/v1/messages` under the same host). ```bash curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"default","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello"}]}' ``` ```python from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1", api_key="not-needed") print(client.chat.completions.create( model="default", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello"}], ).choices[0].message.content) ``` **3. Or wire up your coding agent — one command:** ```bash rapid-mlx launch claude-code ``` This saves a private Claude Code profile, starts a local server if needed, and launches Claude Code without editing `~/.claude/settings.json`. The same command works after a restart. Swap in `codex`, `opencode`, `pi`, `hermes`, `crush`, or `goose`. For the original config-writing behavior, use `--legacy-config`; `cline` and `continue-dev` keep their existing setup flow. [Agent setup details](docs/guides/ai-clients.md#coding-agents). > **Cursor:** Cursor currently routes BYOK requests through its own servers, so its servers cannot reach a Rapid-MLX endpoint on `localhost`. Rapid-MLX therefore does not generate a Cursor localhost config. If you intentionally expose the server through a public HTTPS tunnel, set `RAPID_MLX_API_KEY=your-secret` for both `rapid-mlx serve ...` and `rapid-mlx launch cursor --server-url https://your-public-host`. This is no longer a fully local connection; never expose an unauthenticated server. Rapid-MLX rejects explicit local/private addresses but cannot verify reachability from Cursor's network, whose DNS view may differ from your Mac. > **Vision / image / video models?** They work out of the box with the official installer above (and Rapid-MLX Desktop), which include the vision, image-generation and video-generation runtimes. Audio (TTS, STT, voice cloning) and embeddings ship as opt-in extras. → [Optional extras](https://rapidmlx.com/docs/extras.html) > **Not into the terminal?** [**Rapid-MLX Desktop**](https://rapidmlx.com/desktop) bundles the same engine inside a one-click Mac app. ## See it in action

Real session on a Mac mini (M2 Pro, 32 GB), idle waits shortened. Recording: docs/assets/demo.cast. --- ## Fine-tune a model on your Mac `rapid-mlx finetune` trains a LoRA adapter on your own JSONL data, and `rapid-mlx serve --adapter` serves the result through the same OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible API. ```bash rapid-mlx finetune qwen3.5-9b-4bit --data ./examples.jsonl --out ./my-adapter rapid-mlx serve qwen3.5-9b-4bit --adapter ./my-adapter ``` Qwen3.5 trains through MLX's native gated-delta kernel. Measured on an M3 Ultra with 4-bit weights, batch size 1, 16 adapted layers and a 1,024-token maximum sequence length: | Checkpoint | Path | Peak memory | Steps/s | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | | Qwen3.5-9B | Stock mlx-lm 0.31.3 | 70.3 GB | 0.05 | | Qwen3.5-9B | Rapid-MLX | 13.8 GB | 0.55 | | Qwen3.5-27B | Rapid-MLX | 26.2 GB | 0.28 | Adapters are text only: image inputs return HTTP 400 while an adapter is loaded. See the [fine-tuning guide](https://github.com/raullenchai/Rapid-MLX/blob/main/docs/guides/finetune.md) for data formats, defaults and limits. --- ## Image generation Generate images locally from the Desktop **Images** tab or the OpenAI-compatible Images API. The image runtime ships with the base install: ```bash rapid-mlx serve flux2-klein-4b ``` ```bash curl http://localhost:8000/v1/images/generations \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"flux2-klein-4b","prompt":"A red sailboat on an alpine lake","size":"1024x1024","seed":42}' ``` Edit an existing PNG or JPEG with the edit-specialized model: In one terminal: ```bash rapid-mlx serve qwen-image-edit ``` In another terminal: ```bash curl http://localhost:8000/v1/images/edits \ -F image=@input.png \ -F model=qwen-image-edit \ -F 'prompt=Change the sky to a warm sunset' \ -F response_format=b64_json ``` `flux2-klein-4b` is the recommended starting point. Download sizes are the currently cataloged model payloads; minimum unified memory includes practical headroom for macOS and the serving process. Omit `steps` to use the validated family default shown below. | Alias or HF repo ID | Best fit | Modes | Download | Minimum unified memory | Default steps | | --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | `flux3-klein` | FLUX 3 Klein, gated (next release) | Generate + edit (1–10 references) | 18.9 GiB | 24 GB (provisional) | 16 | | `flux3-klein-base` | FLUX 3 Klein base, gated (next release) | Generate + edit (1–10 references) | 18.9 GiB | 24 GB (provisional) | 50 | | `flux2-klein-4b` | Recommended; fast everyday images | Generate + edit | 4.3 GiB | 16 GB | 4 | | `bonsai-image-4b-2bit` | Smallest download | Generate | 3.6 GiB | 12 GB | 4 | | `z-image-turbo` | Photorealistic images | Generate | 5.5 GiB | 16 GB | 8 | | `flux-schnell` | FLUX.1 compatibility | Generate | 9.0 GiB | 32 GB | 4 | | `sdxl-base` | SDXL compatibility | Generate | 6.5 GiB | 16 GB | 30 | | `hidream-o1-dev` | Complex compositions | Generate | 16.4 GiB | 32 GB | 28 | | `sd35-large-4bit` | Stable Diffusion 3.5 | Generate | 15.3 GiB | 32 GB | 28 | | `minimax-h3-image` | MiniMax-H3-Image, 4-bit at load | Generate + edit (up to 16 references) | 126.1 GiB | 64 GB | 6 | | `minimax-h3-image-8bit` | MiniMax-H3-Image, 8-bit at load | Generate + edit (up to 16 references) | 126.1 GiB | 96 GB | 6 | | `qwen-image-2.1` | Text-rich images on low-memory Macs | Generate + edit | 8.9 GiB | 8 GB | 40 | | `qwen-image` | Same model as `qwen-image-2.1` | Generate + edit | 8.9 GiB | 8 GB | 40 | | `qwen-image-2.1-bf16` | Higher-precision Qwen Image 2.1 path | Generate + edit | 30.9 GiB | 32 GB | 40 | | `qwen-image-2.1-turbo` | Eight-step distilled Qwen Image 2.1 | Generate | 30.2 GiB | 32 GB | 8 | | `qwen-image-edit` | Precise instruction edits and text changes | Edit | 34.9 GiB | 96 GB | 20 | [MiniMax-H3-Image](docs/models/families/minimax-h3-image.md) uses the MiniMax-H3-Image Community License, which excludes use in the European Union, the United Kingdom, the Republic of Korea and the United States. Commercial use is permitted under the license; organizations above US$1M annual revenue and providers of hosted services to third parties need separate written authorization from MiniMax. Products must prominently display **MiniMax-H3-Image**. Desktop currently accepts up to 10 references. For the next release, `flux3-klein` and `flux3-klein-base` require mflux 0.23 or later and gated Hugging Face access under the FLUX Kommunity License. Both accept 1–10 reference images for editing. Their 24 GB memory floor is provisional pending real-peak measurement; download sizes use estimated component totals. See the [FLUX 3 Klein guide](docs/models/families/flux3-klein.md) for setup. `qwen-image-2.1` uses mflux 0.20 with a native MLX q4 transformer and q4 text encoder. `qwen-image-2.1-bf16` preserves the previous 8-bit-on-load transformer and bf16 encoder path. `qwen-image-2.1-turbo` loads the official distilled checkpoint the same way and samples its published eight-step schedule without classifier-free guidance; it is text-to-image only. The other two aliases' edit endpoint performs single-image img2img conditioning; the separate instruction-edit variant is not yet available upstream. See the [family guide](https://github.com/raullenchai/Rapid-MLX/blob/main/docs/models/families/qwen-image-2.1.md) for request and memory behavior. At 1024×1024 with the four-step Klein default, measured warm generation was about **9.2 seconds per image on an M3 Ultra**. On a 32 GB M2 Pro, the q4 path measured a 52.7-second median; explicitly selecting `mflux-community/flux2-klein-4b-mflux-bf16` reduced that median to 41.8 seconds (1.26× throughput). The eight-step `z-image-turbo` baseline was about 34 seconds on the M3 Ultra and 150 seconds on the M2 Pro. The q4 alias remains the predictable default; on the measured 32 GB M2 Pro, use the larger 14.9 GiB BF16 alias when latency matters. Exact results depend on resolution, power/thermal state, and other workloads. The server completion log reports total time and, when the backend exposes exact loop boundaries, measured denoise `s/step`. For the qualified 1024-square Klein shape it also reports estimated achieved TFLOPS; unavailable or unqualified values are never fabricated. → [Reproducible precision benchmark and methodology](https://github.com/raullenchai/Rapid-MLX/blob/main/docs/engineering/performance/2026-09-04-image-weight-precision.md) Image work is single-flight: one generation runs at a time so two diffusion pipelines cannot exhaust unified memory. Model weights retain their own licenses and use restrictions; review the upstream model card before commercial deployment. → [Release dogfood coverage and reproducible acceptance contract](https://github.com/raullenchai/Rapid-MLX/blob/main/docs/engineering/operations/image-release-dogfood-matrix.md) --- ## Video generation Run text-to-video or image-to-video locally through the OpenAI-compatible Videos API. Three backends ship — **Wan 2.1 / 2.2**, **CogVideoX-Fun** and **LTX-2.3** — across 8 registered checkpoints. `wan2.2-ti2v-5b-q8` is the recommended starting point: smallest of the Wan set, and TI2V means one checkpoint does both text-to-video and image-to-video. The video runtime ships with the base install. Install `ffmpeg` for the final MP4 mux. ```bash brew install ffmpeg rapid-mlx serve wan2.2-ti2v-5b-q8 ``` Create and download a clip: ```bash curl http://localhost:8000/v1/videos \ -F model=wan2.2-ti2v-5b-q8 \ -F 'prompt=A fox running through fresh snow, cinematic tracking shot' \ -F seconds=1 \ -F size=832x512 # Poll until GET /v1/videos/VIDEO_ID reports "status": "completed", then: curl http://localhost:8000/v1/videos/VIDEO_ID/content -o output.mp4 ``` The create call returns a job immediately. Poll `GET /v1/videos/VIDEO_ID` until `status` is `completed`. Add `-F input_reference=@start.png` for image-to-video. Generation is serialized — one clip at a time — because two diffusion pipelines resident at once will exhaust unified memory. Expect minutes of compute per second of footage, not real time. → [Every checkpoint, RAM requirement and tuning knob](https://rapidmlx.com/docs/models/families/video.html) --- ## Audio: speech, transcription, voice cloning The dependency commands below use the official `install.sh` environment. For Homebrew or another install method, follow [optional extras](https://rapidmlx.com/docs/extras.html). Audio aliases behind the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/audio/*` endpoints — any OpenAI SDK works unchanged. `tts-1`, `tts-1-hd`, and `gpt-4o-mini-tts` select the default TTS model (served TTS model, otherwise Kokoro). ```bash ~/.rapid-mlx/bin/python -m pip install 'rapid-mlx[audio]' # Text to speech rapid-mlx serve kokoro curl --fail http://localhost:8000/v1/audio/speech \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"kokoro","input":"hello from rapid-mlx"}' --output hello.wav # Transcription (Whisper / Parakeet / SenseVoice) rapid-mlx serve whisper-large-v3-turbo curl http://localhost:8000/v1/audio/transcriptions \ -F file=@hello.wav -F model=whisper-large-v3-turbo ``` Beyond the basics, three things you may not expect to run locally: - **Zero-shot voice cloning** from a reference clip. `indextts` is the only one that takes the clip alone; `qwen3-tts-clone`, `f5-tts-zh` and `chatterbox` all require `ref_text` (the clip's exact transcript) paired with `ref_audio`, and the request is rejected before generation if it is missing. - **Voice design** — `qwen3-tts-voicedesign` has no named speakers at all. Describe the voice you want in natural language via `instructions` (timbre, gender, age, accent, emotion, prosody) and it synthesises it. - **Forced alignment** — `qwen3-aligner` takes audio *plus the transcript you already have* and returns per-character timings. It never guesses at the words, so it cannot mis-hear them; that is what karaoke captions and beat-synced editing need. Also: word-level timestamps on transcription, and local text-to-music at `/v1/audio/music`. → [All 53 aliases across 17 families](https://rapidmlx.com/docs/models/families/audio.html) --- ## Typed decisions with System One Serve fast `noul`, `choice`, and `score` decisions through a TypeSafe-compatible `/v1/systemone` API. Laya-MLX is the compact default; CLM-8B uses a native MLX Qwen3-8B encoder and cached state/action projections. Cloudflare Clef adds joint-schema decisions from text, images, and video frames, on native MLX or with its official head on Torch/Metal. Decider-2b and OpenJev (27B, non-commercial weights) run on native MLX with no extra install. For the official `install.sh` environment, use the commands below. All three rows target an 8K prompt and 256-token decode; after chat templating the Qwen prompts contain 8,156 tokens and the GLM prompt contains 8,192. | Model | Shape | Median TTFT | Prefill | Decode | MLX memory observed through 32K | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | `qwen3.8-27b-4bit` | 27B dense | 24.66s | 330.8 tok/s | **43.4 tok/s** | 26.7 GB active / 27.1 GB peak | | `qwen3.8-flash-next-4bit` | 180B total / 6B active¹ | **9.40s** | **867.9 tok/s** | 23.0 tok/s | 102.8 GB active / 148.1 GB peak | | `glm5.3-flash-4bit` | 320B total / 18B active | 22.78s | 359.6 tok/s | **27.8 tok/s** | 180.6 GB active / 195.6 GB peak | ¹ Flash-Next comprises a 125B language model, 51B n-gram embedding, and 4B MTP head. Speculative decoding modes remain workload-dependent. Flash-Next prefill reaches 262 / 875 / 868 / 716 tok/s at 128 / 2K / 8K / 32K; median TTFT is 0.35 / 2.30 / 9.40 / 45.73s. GLM-5.3-Flash reached 27.2 tok/s decode at 32K, but its TTFT was 118.34s and its 195.6 GB allocator peak leaves no safe system headroom on a 192 GB Mac. Use a 256 GB Mac for this measured 32K workload; 192 GB remains the catalog floor for shorter contexts. Measured rows use the standard ~8K prompt peak of the complete `rapid-mlx serve` process tree on an M2 Pro 32 GB Mac mini (the 32 GB+ row: M3 Ultra, 2026-08-18 — footprint is config-bound, speed reads lower on smaller chips). | RAM | Recommended | Peak RSS | One-shot | |---|---|---:|---| | **8–15 GB** MacBook Air / base Mini | `lfm2.5-2.6b-4bit` | 3.0 GB | `rapid-mlx serve lfm2.5-2.6b-4bit` | | **16–17 GB** MacBook Air / Pro | `qwen3.5-4b-4bit` | 6.0 GB | `rapid-mlx serve qwen3.5-4b-4bit` | | **18–23 GB** MacBook Pro | `qwen3.5-9b-4bit` | 8.7 GB | `rapid-mlx serve qwen3.5-9b-4bit` | | **24–31 GB** Mac Mini / MacBook Pro | `bonsai-27b-2bit` | 13.0 GB | `rapid-mlx serve bonsai-27b-2bit` | | **32 GB+** Mac Studio / MacBook Pro | `qwen3.8-27b-4bit` | 20.0 GB | `rapid-mlx serve qwen3.8-27b-4bit` | The experimental `deepseek-v41-flash-reap-2bit` alias is a separate 256 GB Mac Studio lane, not a recommendation for the table above. It pins the 199 GiB REAP checkpoint and its separate 4.62 GB mixed-precision DSpark sidecar, refuses to start below 224 GiB unified memory, and serves deterministic greedy K4 decoding through a serial OpenAI-compatible endpoint: ```bash rapid-mlx pull deepseek-v41-flash-reap-2bit rapid-mlx serve deepseek-v41-flash-reap-2bit ``` The mixed head keeps routed experts at 2-bit and raises the smaller dense paths to 4-bit. Sustained four-workload qualification measured **19.39 tok/s** overall at K4 versus 9.58 tok/s autoregressive (**2.02x**), with a 218.23 GB peak. This is approximately 20 tok/s for the measured configuration, not a per-prompt guarantee. This lane remains experimental and text-only, caps input at 8,192 tokens and output at 4,096, and does not claim sampling, tool calling, MCP, or continuous batching. Every Mac from 32 GB up gets the same pick, and that is the point: Qwen3.8-27B scores 52 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (2026-08-18) — GPT-5.6-class, the highest of any open-weights model we serve, ahead of the much larger 122B (33) and 35B (32) it replaces (the index scores the full-precision release; our 4-bit build's deltas are unmeasured — the standing caveat for every quantized pick here). On the measured 8K workload it prefills at 330.8 tok/s and decodes at 43.4 tok/s, with zero new swap. The verified 4-bit artifact automatically enables its MTP path when the selected cache and serving lane are compatible; `--no-spec-decode` remains the explicit opt-out. The 32 GB recommendation is based on the approximately 8K qualification (about 20 GB for the complete process tree). The 32K Studio run reached a 27.1 GB MLX allocator peak before non-MLX process and macOS memory; on a 32 GB Mac, reduce context/cache use or choose a larger-memory machine. M1 and M2 Macs can explicitly select `qwen3.8-27b-4bit-fp16`. It carries the same 4-bit target and native MTP layout, but stores the checkpoint's non-quantized tensors as FP16 for chips without accelerated BF16 matrix multiplication. The regular `qwen3.8-27b-4bit` alias remains unchanged for M3 and newer Macs; Rapid does not silently swap checkpoint precision. The pinned `ornith-1.5-122b-a10b-4bit` alias offers the publisher’s 122B hybrid MoE checkpoint on Macs with at least 96 GB unified memory. Install the `[vision]` runtime for its checkpoint loader; this alias qualifies text chat, streaming, tools, and thinking controls. Its download is about 69.6 GB. Homebrew — Mac-native, one command, prebuilt bottle from homebrew/core ```bash brew install rapid-mlx ``` Available in homebrew-core. Upgrade with `brew upgrade rapid-mlx`.
uv — isolated tool install, auto-manages Python ```bash uv tool install rapid-mlx@latest ``` Don't have uv yet? `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh`. Upgrade with `uv tool upgrade rapid-mlx`. On a Python 3.10/3.11 tool environment use `uv tool upgrade --python 3.12 rapid-mlx`.
pip — requires Python 3.12+ (macOS ships 3.9) ```bash python3.12 -m venv ~/.venvs/rapid-mlx ~/.venvs/rapid-mlx/bin/pip install rapid-mlx ``` Add `~/.venvs/rapid-mlx/bin` to your PATH or call the executable directly. If `python3.12` is missing, use the official installer above or install Python 3.12 with Homebrew first. Upgrade with the pip of the environment that holds Rapid-MLX, e.g. `~/.venvs/rapid-mlx/bin/pip install -U rapid-mlx` for the environment above (an existing install made with an earlier Python 3.12 pip command upgrades with that same Python's pip). An install on Python 3.10/3.11 stays on 1.0.0 (`Requirement already satisfied`); reinstall it with Python 3.12 — see [Upgrading from Python 3.10 or 3.11](https://rapidmlx.com/docs/getting-started/installation.html#upgrading-from-python-310-or-311). Image-input / VLM models (Qwen-VL, Gemma 4, true multimodal) need no extra step — the vision runtime ships with the base install. See [Optional extras](https://rapidmlx.com/docs/extras.html) for audio and embeddings. For the complete feature set — chat, embeddings, audio, and System One on top of the base install — install the `[all]` extra: `~/.venvs/rapid-mlx/bin/pip install 'rapid-mlx[all]'`. Audio alone is `~/.venvs/rapid-mlx/bin/pip install 'rapid-mlx[audio]'`; see [Optional extras](https://rapidmlx.com/docs/extras.html).

Most of Rapid-MLX is built this way, and we review AI-written PRs the same as hand-written ones. What we ask in return: 1. **Say how AI helped.** The PR template has a short disclosure section, such as "Claude wrote it, I ran the tests". No prompt transcripts needed. 2. **Prove it works.** Include the test you added or the command you ran and its output. A real reproduction beats a long description. 3. **Keep it focused.** One fix or feature per PR is easier to review and merge. 4. **Understand what you submit.** Be ready to explain why the change is needed and what it touches. It stands on Apple's MLX stack and the runtimes built around it: - **[MLX](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx)** — Apple's array framework for Apple Silicon - **[mlx-lm](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm)** — LLM inference, KV cache, quantization - **[mlx-vlm](https://github.com/Blaizzy/mlx-vlm)** — vision-language models - **[mlx-audio](https://github.com/Blaizzy/mlx-audio)** — speech and audio models Vendored third-party components and their licenses are listed in [NOTICE](https://github.com/raullenchai/Rapid-MLX/blob/main/NOTICE); what the macOS app ships is enumerated in [apps/rapid-mac/THIRD_PARTY.md](https://github.com/raullenchai/Rapid-MLX/blob/main/apps/rapid-mac/THIRD_PARTY.md). ## License Apache 2.0 — see [LICENSE](https://github.com/raullenchai/Rapid-MLX/blob/main/LICENSE) and [NOTICE](https://github.com/raullenchai/Rapid-MLX/blob/main/NOTICE). ### Experimental persistent chat The harness is included in the base install. Try it with a local inference server: ```bash python -m pip install rapid-mlx rapid-mlx serve mlx-community/Qwen3.5-4B-MLX-4bit --port 18800 # Model page URLs work too: rapid-mlx serve https://huggingface.co/mlx-community/Qwen3.5-4B-MLX-4bit --port 18800 # In another terminal: rapid-mlx chat --harness --base-url http://127.0.0.1:18800 --profile dogfood rapid-mlx chat --harness --base-url http://127.0.0.1:18800 --profile dogfood --resume last ``` The usual model selection and startup also work with `rapid-mlx chat --harness`. The existing chat experience remains the default; `RAPID_MLX_CHAT_HARNESS=1` enables the experimental harness for subsequent chat commands. The harness reads the selected model's native context and effective serving limit from `/v1/models` before each turn. Its default context budget is the smaller of those limits and 32,768 tokens. Newly spawned harness chat servers use the same default, bounded by locally cached model metadata. A server started with `--context-length` remains authoritative; set that flag on `serve` when attaching to an existing server. An explicit chat startup context can exceed the default budget, but cannot exceed the model or serving limit or the harness ceiling of 131,072 tokens. The runtime counts tokens using the inference server when available and falls back to a conservative text estimate. It reserves room for the answer, compacts older tool outputs, and saves summary checkpoints to keep longer conversations usable. Use `/context` for the system/tools, conversation, tool-output, and free-token breakdown; `/compact [instructions]` saves a summary checkpoint manually. A dim context indicator appears at 50% usage, with a warning at 90%. Automatic compaction announces itself in the transcript. Responses stream as Markdown. Ctrl-C stops the current response. Use `/history` to list and resume conversations, `/new` to start fresh, `/edit` and `/regen` to create branches, and `/branch` to switch between them. `/think on` turns thinking on; `/think off` turns it off. The prompt is `› `, or `Thinking › ` while thinking is on (`> ` replaces `› ` on non-UTF-8 output). Thinking is collapsed by default and `/show-thinking` expands it for the current session; it is never saved. The folder where you start a new conversation becomes its workspace and stays fixed when you resume it. Ask Rapid to read files, search code with a regex, or list matching paths using its built-in `read_file`, `grep`, and `glob` tools. Reads support text/code, PDF text, DOCX, XLSX/CSV, PPTX, JSON/YAML, and HTML. Results include line numbers and paging hints; searches honor `.gitignore` and skip binaries and dependency folders. These three read tools need no approval. Paths outside the workspace and secrets-like paths are refused, including symlink escapes. Use `/attach PATH` to explicitly share a file from another folder (or a sensitive file you choose to share). Attachments accept the same formats up to 20 MiB and save an extracted text snapshot capped at 1 MiB. Spreadsheet extraction caps each sheet at 1,000 rows/10,000 cells and reads cached formula values; it does not calculate formulas. PNG, JPEG, WebP, and GIF images work with vision models. Only the current message’s images are sent; earlier images become placeholders. Scanned PDFs without text are unsupported. `/regen` reruns workspace reads, so it can see file changes; attached snapshots stay fixed. `/export [PATH]` exports the selected branch as Markdown; `/help` lists commands. New conversations show `New chat · Type / for commands`; resuming shows the conversation title. Type `/` to browse commands in the completion menu. History is stored under `~/Library/Application Support/Rapid/chat//` (`RAPID_MLX_CHAT_HOME` overrides the root). A separate local owner starts automatically, survives client exits, and stops after five idle minutes. An owner restart preserves history and marks an in-flight answer interrupted; you can continue or regenerate. Only local HTTP inference targets are supported. New conversations use the CLI's launch directory (resolved to its real path) as an immutable workspace, including after resume. `write_file` and `patch` edit UTF-8 files up to 1 MiB with durable pre-images; `/undo` restores the last file edit, refusing to overwrite subsequent changes. Repeat `/undo` for earlier edits. It does not undo shell commands or Python effects. Older conversations without a workspace can bind one explicitly supplied client directory on their next turn; that directory then remains immutable. The owner never chooses its own cwd. Workspace edits and commands without dangerous patterns run immediately. Outside-workspace and secrets-like file reads/edits are refused, even with approval. Explicit attachments grant access only to their extracted snapshot. Destructive commands, privilege changes, remote execution/uploads, and side effects on regenerated or edited branches require approval once each. Approvals show a command or diff: `y` allows once, `a` allows the exact tool/arguments for this conversation when offered, and `n` denies (`N` adds an optional denial reason). Dangerous actions never offer `a`. Ctrl-C cancels a pending approval or kills the running command's process group. Unanswered approvals expire after 120 seconds; noninteractive input denies them. `terminal` and `execute_code(language="python", code=...)` run noninteractively in the workspace, with a 120-second default timeout (maximum 600) and 8 KiB of head/tail output. Python uses `python3` on PATH, falling back to the bundled interpreter. Terminal processes inherit only PATH, HOME, USER, LOGNAME, LANG, LC_*, TERM, SHELL and TMPDIR; PWD is set to the workspace. To pass other non-secret variables, set `RAPID_MLX_HARNESS_TERMINAL_ENV` in the owner environment to a comma-separated list of exact names before starting the owner. Names containing KEY, SECRET, TOKEN, PASSWORD, PASSWD, CREDENTIAL or AUTH, AWS_* and DATABASE_URL are always excluded, as are values containing URL userinfo. This limits accidental inheritance; commands can still access files and resources available to the user. Pattern checks are heuristics, **not an OS sandbox**; scripts and programs run with your local account's access. Use `RAPID_MLX_CHAT_APPROVALS=always` or `--approvals always` to approve every action; `RAPID_MLX_CHAT_ACTION_TOOLS=0` or `--no-action-tools` disables all four tools. These client settings also apply when attaching to an existing owner; an owner's stricter environment policy cannot be relaxed by a client. The operation ledger commits authorization and dispatch before effects. Restart marks unfinished dispatches `outcome_unknown`, shows them when resuming history, and never automatically replays them. Regeneration shows matching prior receipts as “Previously executed … — run again?” and requires fresh approval. Inspect unknown effects before approving another attempt. Weather, web search and `web_fetch(url)` are available to tool-capable models by default. The CLI shows tool progress and numbered sources after the answer; `/export` retains those sources. Weather uses Open-Meteo without a key. Search uses Keenable's public tier without a key. Set `KEENABLE_API_KEY`, `RAPID_MLX_TAVILY_API_KEY` or `RAPID_MLX_BRAVE_API_KEY` in the owner's environment to use a keyed provider. `RAPID_MLX_WEB_SEARCH_PROVIDER=tavily|brave|keenable` selects explicitly; otherwise configured keyed providers precede public Keenable. Rate limits, server errors and timeouts fail over to the next available provider. Keys stay in memory and are never saved in chat history. Providers can throttle or return no useful results. Each turn carries local date, weekday, time, timezone and coarse locale beside its user message, preserving the stable system/tool prefix. Search results keep provider dates when available and label missing dates. Explicitly current queries are anchored to the full local date unless they already specify a date or a historical period. Explicit "today" searches omit known older results, retaining unknown dates for verification; provider publication dates are not event dates. For article summaries, the assistant is instructed to follow the story link and cite the evidence. Web calls are limited to four per run. All tools share a 16,000-byte model-return allowance per run, including file and terminal output; older tool results may be compacted for the model while original evidence remains in the local event journal. At the limit, the runtime makes one tools-disabled answer attempt. An empty recovery produces a visible failure message, without claiming a verified answer. The built-in `delegate_task(task, context?, tools?)` tool is available by default inside the harness. It gives a helper a fresh history containing only its task and supplied context. Helpers use the same local model, workspace, and approval policy. Optional tool names narrow the parent's available tools; helpers cannot delegate again. Up to three helpers run concurrently in the owner, using the inference server's batching. Each helper has a 120-second deadline, six model requests, eight tool calls, and a 12,000-token usage budget; its web/result limits are independent of the parent's. Exhausted or timed-out helpers return an explicit partial summary. The parent combines their summaries and sources. The CLI shows compact nested helper progress. Child actions use the normal approval prompt with helper attribution; Ctrl-C stops the parent and all its helpers. Child transcripts stay out of visible branch messages but are retained locally without reasoning and included as collapsed details in `/export`. Chat stores use schema 4. Earlier experimental schemas require a new profile; existing schema 4 profiles reopen unchanged, and incompatible stores are refused. For offline use, set `RAPID_MLX_CHAT_WEB_TOOLS=0` before starting a new profile owner, for example `RAPID_MLX_CHAT_WEB_TOOLS=0 rapid-mlx chat --harness --profile offline`. An already-running owner keeps its startup environment. Weather and search have a 10-second total timeout. Fetch has a 20-second total timeout, allowing up to 10 seconds for Keenable before trying the direct fallback; Ctrl-C cancels an in-flight request. Editing or regenerating a turn runs read-only tools again for fresh information. Search returns snippets; `web_fetch` reads a page using Keenable, with a direct HTTP(S) fallback that rejects private network addresses, pins validated IPs and checks every redirect. Responses are size- and content-type-bounded; extracted page text is capped at 8,000 UTF-8 bytes and may be shortened further to fit the remaining tool-output allowance, with a truncation marker. Fetching needs no per-domain prompt. MCP, custom system prompts, and Desktop integration remain outside this experimental slice. See the [chat owner decision](docs/engineering/decisions/2026-10-25-chat-owner-topology.md) for lifecycle and durability details.

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, release/0.16.0]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 9 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' && '-nightly' || '' }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# Every job in this workflow runs product code (engine, CLI, Desktop app) on
# shared or self-hosted machines. None of that is a user: keep it out of the
# production telemetry store. The engine and the Desktop app both honour this
# kill switch; the golden-flow harness lifts it only for the flows that turn
# telemetry on against a loopback sink (fresh-install, fresh-install-share,
# no-dead-controls). The Desktop unit tests pin their own environment, so the
# switch stays on while they run.
env:
  RAPID_MLX_TELEMETRY: "0"

# Linux runner routing (JSON runner specs: a string or a label array; unset uses ubuntu-latest):
# - CI_LINUX_RUNNER routes the heavy test-matrix shards.
# - CI_LINUX_LIGHT_RUNNER routes every other (seconds-long) Linux job, so
#   control-plane work never queues behind test shards on a small pool.
# Fork heads (pull_request, pull_request_target, workflow_run) always use ubuntu-latest.
# Rollback: gh variable delete CI_LINUX_RUNNER (heavy); gh variable delete CI_LINUX_LIGHT_RUNNER (light)

jobs:
  changes:
    permissions:
      contents: read
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    runs-on: ${{ fromJSON((vars.CI_LINUX_LIGHT_RUNNER != '' && (!github.event.pull_request || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository) && (!github.event.workflow_run || github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository)) && vars.CI_LINUX_LIGHT_RUNNER || '"ubuntu-latest"') }}
    outputs:
      engine: ${{ steps.policy.outputs.engine }}
      desktop: ${{ steps.policy.outputs.desktop }}
      docs_only: ${{ steps.policy.outputs.docs_only }}
      full_gate: ${{ steps.policy.outputs.full_gate }}
      l1_matrix: ${{ steps.policy.outputs.l1_matrix }}
      linux_matrix_mode: ${{ steps.policy.outputs.linux_matrix_mode }}
      linux_matrix_reason: ${{ steps.policy.outputs.linux_matrix_reason }}
      test_matrix: ${{ steps.policy.outputs.test_matrix }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Classify validation lanes
        id: policy
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.head_ref }}
          HEAD_REPO: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name }}
          PR_BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "pull_request" ]; then
            # Classify the actual diff before integration promotion. Promotion
            # broadens coverage inside the affected lane; it must not turn an
            # engine-only PR into a full Desktop run (or vice versa).
            # Disable rename folding so both the removed source path and the
            # new destination participate in classification.
            git diff --no-renames --name-only "$PR_BASE_SHA" "$GITHUB_SHA" > /tmp/changed-paths
            full_gate=false
            if [ "$HEAD_REPO" = "$REPO" ] && \
              [[ "$HEAD_REF" == train/* ]]; then
              full_gate=true
            fi
            echo "full_gate=$full_gate" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            if [ "$full_gate" = true ]; then
              python scripts/classify_ci_changes.py \
                --paths-file /tmp/changed-paths \
                --force-full \
                --force-reason promoted-head \
                --github-output "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo 'l1_matrix={"include":[{"model":"qwen3.5-4b-4bit","contract_only":"0"},{"model":"llama3-3b-4bit","contract_only":"0"},{"model":"gemma3-4b-qat-4bit","contract_only":"1"},{"model":"qwen3-4b-instruct-2507-4bit","contract_only":"1"},{"model":"qwen3-4b-thinking-2507-4bit","contract_only":"1"}]}' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            else
              python scripts/classify_ci_changes.py \
                --paths-file /tmp/changed-paths \
                --github-output "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo 'l1_matrix={"include":[{"model":"qwen3.5-4b-4bit","contract_only":"0"}]}' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            fi
          else
            # Non-PR events run the complete engine gate.
            {
              echo 'engine=true'
              echo 'desktop=true'
              echo 'docs_only=false'
              echo 'full_gate=true'
              echo 'linux_matrix_mode=full'
              echo 'linux_matrix_reason=non-pr-full'
              echo 'test_matrix={"include":[{"python-version":"3.12","shard":1},{"python-version":"3.12","shard":2},{"python-version":"3.12","shard":3},{"python-version":"3.13","shard":1},{"python-version":"3.13","shard":2},{"python-version":"3.13","shard":3}]}'
              echo 'l1_matrix={"include":[{"model":"qwen3.5-4b-4bit","contract_only":"0"},{"model":"llama3-3b-4bit","contract_only":"0"},{"model":"gemma3-4b-qat-4bit","contract_only":"1"},{"model":"qwen3-4b-instruct-2507-4bit","contract_only":"1"},{"model":"qwen3-4b-thinking-2507-4bit","contract_only":"1"}]}'
            } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - name: Explain Linux matrix route
        env:
          MATRIX_MODE: ${{ steps.policy.outputs.linux_matrix_mode }}
          MATRIX_REASON: ${{ steps.policy.outputs.linux_matrix_reason }}
        run: |
          echo "Linux matrix: ${MATRIX_MODE} (${MATRIX_REASON})"
          {
            echo '### Linux test matrix'
            echo "- Mode: \`${MATRIX_MODE}\`"
            echo "- Reason: \`${MATRIX_REASON}\`"
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  merge-lane-no-mac:
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      !cancelled() &&
      needs.changes.result == 'success' &&
      needs.changes.outputs.engine != 'true' &&
      needs.changes.outputs.desktop != 'true'
    runs-on: ${{ fromJSON((vars.CI_LINUX_LIGHT_RUNNER != '' && (!github.event.pull_request || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository) && (!github.event.workflow_run || github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository)) && vars.CI_LINUX_LIGHT_RUNNER || '"ubuntu-latest"') }}
    steps:
      - name: Mark no-Mac merge lane
        run: echo "This head requires neither the engine nor Desktop lane."

  merge-lane-mac:
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      !cancelled() &&
      needs.changes.result == 'success' &&
      (needs.changes.outputs.engine == 'true' ||
       needs.changes.outputs.desktop == 'true')
    runs-on: ${{ fromJSON((vars.CI_LINUX_LIGHT_RUNNER != '' && (!github.event.pull_request || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository) && (!github.event.workflow_run || github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository)) && vars.CI_LINUX_LIGHT_RUNNER || '"ubuntu-latest"') }}
    steps:
      - name: Mark Mac-required merge lane
        run: echo "This head requires the engine, Desktop, or both lanes."

  lint:
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      !cancelled() &&
      needs.changes.result == 'success'
    runs-on: ${{ fromJSON((vars.CI_LINUX_LIGHT_RUNNER != '' && (!github.event.pull_request || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository) && (!github.event.workflow_run || github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository)) && vars.CI_LINUX_LIGHT_RUNNER || '"ubuntu-latest"') }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97  # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          # pyyaml: check_gha_pinning.py parses workflow YAML (so quoted
          # `uses` forms cannot bypass the SHA-pin gate).
          pip install ruff pyyaml

      - name: Run ruff lint
        run: ruff check .

      - name: Run ruff format check
        run: ruff format --check .

      - name: Check packaged model digest coverage offline
        run: python scripts/build_model_digests.py --check

      # PF-3 — all GitHub Actions are immutable 40-char commit SHA pins.
      # Dependabot or a reviewed PR is required to advance an action.

      # is not a PR check it never shows up as red on the PR that

      - name: Workflow expression sanity
        run: python scripts/check_workflow_expressions.py

      # The model-management diagram and status tables are generated from one
      # reviewed YAML manifest. Fail if a PR edits status/relationships without
      # regenerating the GitHub-facing Mermaid/SVG views.
      - name: Model-management architecture SSOT
        run: python scripts/render_model_management_architecture.py --check

      # The engine and the desktop app ship ONE version number. Keep this

      - name: Engine ↔ desktop app version sync
        run: python scripts/check_version_sync.py

  engine-contracts:
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      !cancelled() &&
      needs.changes.result == 'success' &&
      needs.changes.outputs.engine == 'true'
    runs-on: ${{ fromJSON((vars.CI_LINUX_LIGHT_RUNNER != '' && (!github.event.pull_request || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository) && (!github.event.workflow_run || github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository)) && vars.CI_LINUX_LIGHT_RUNNER || '"ubuntu-latest"') }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97  # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"

      # Structural check — catches "silent flag drop" bugs where a CLI
      # arg is defined but never plumbed to its target config (#400).
      # Pure stdlib + AST — no mlx import required, runs on Linux.
      - name: CLI ↔ Config fidelity audit
        run: python scripts/audit_cli_config_fidelity.py

      # The release scripts cannot be exercised without cutting a release, so
      # their tag-claim, recovery and refuse-to-move paths are covered offline
      # against a mock ``gh``. These existed but nothing ran them, which is how
      # a release-path regression stays invisible until release day. Pure bash,
      # no network/gh/git.
      - name: Release-script offline tests
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          for t in tests/release/test_*.sh; do
            echo "── $t"
            bash "$t"
          done

      # install.sh picks the interpreter and builds ~/.rapid-mlx, but it only
      # runs end-to-end on Apple Silicon, so its arch-selection and venv-repair
      # logic (see #1953) is covered offline against fake interpreters. Pure
      # bash, no network/Python/real install — runs on the Linux CI leg.
      - name: Installer offline tests
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          for t in tests/install/test_*.sh; do
            echo "── $t"
            bash "$t"
          done

      # Parser microbench — reports order-of-magnitude (>12x) regressions in
      # tool-call extraction. Pure Python (parsers don't import mlx). The
      # relative budget scales parser μs/call by a same-run control workload;
      # interleaved rounds and a median reduce uniform machine-speed noise and
      # isolated scheduler pauses. Different operations do not necessarily
      # scale together across hosted architectures, so this shared-runner lane
      # is intentionally ADVISORY (#2344). The serial M3 release check runs the
      # same script without `--report` and remains the enforced timing gate.
      #
      # PYTHONPATH=. so `from rapid_mlx.tool_parsers...` resolves
      # without installing the package — pytest auto-adds rootdir but
      # bare `python` doesn't, and we don't want a full `pip install -e .`
      # here just for the parser module.
      - name: Parser microbench
        env:
          PYTHONPATH: ${{ github.workspace }}
        run: |
          pip install pydantic transformers jsonschema openai-harmony
          python scripts/microbench_parsers.py --report

  mlx-bound-guard:
    # #1248 — a change to an mlx / mlx-lm / mlx-vlm version bound can re-open the
    # upstream-heuristic break that shipped garbage (#1234). It must be gated on a
    # full-family output-coherence sweep (#1247), attested via the
    # `mlx-coherence-swept` label or a `Coherence-Sweep:` PR-body trailer. No-op
    # unless a guarded specifier actually changes. PR-only: it diffs the head
    # against the PR base, which a push-to-main event has no meaningful analogue
    # for (origin/main == the pushed commit).
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      !cancelled() &&
      needs.changes.result == 'success' &&
      github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&
      needs.changes.outputs.engine == 'true'
    runs-on: ${{ fromJSON((vars.CI_LINUX_LIGHT_RUNNER != '' && (!github.event.pull_request || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository) && (!github.event.workflow_run || github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository)) && vars.CI_LINUX_LIGHT_RUNNER || '"ubuntu-latest"') }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97  # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Install packaging
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install packaging

      - name: Fetch base branch
        env:
          BASE_BRANCH: ${{ github.base_ref || 'main' }}
        run: git fetch --no-tags origin "${BASE_BRANCH}:refs/remotes/origin/${BASE_BRANCH}"

      - name: Guard mlx/mlx-lm/mlx-vlm version bounds

          MLX_BOUND_BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          PR_BODY: ${{ github.event.pull_request.body }}
          PR_LABELS: ${{ join(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, ',') }}

    needs: changes
    if: >-
      !cancelled() &&
      needs.changes.result == 'success' &&
      needs.changes.outputs.engine == 'true'
    runs-on: ${{ fromJSON((vars.CI_LINUX_LIGHT_RUNNER != '' && (!github.event.pull_request || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository) && (!github.event.workflow_run || github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository)) && vars.CI_LINUX_LIGHT_RUNNER || '"ubuntu-latest"') }}

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1

        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          # The checked-in budget belongs to this fully pinned type surface.
          pip install --requirement config/mypy-requirements.txt

      - name: Enforce shrink-only mypy error budget
        run: python scripts/check_mypy_error_budget.py

  test-matrix:
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      !cancelled() &&
      needs.changes.result == 'success' &&
      needs.changes.outputs.engine == 'true'
    runs-on: ${{ fromJSON((vars.CI_LINUX_RUNNER != '' && (!github.event.pull_request || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository) && (!github.event.workflow_run || github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository)) && vars.CI_LINUX_RUNNER || '"ubuntu-latest"') }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      # Ordinary PRs run all three shards on Python 3.12, the coverage
      # interpreter. Promoted heads and non-PR events retain all supported
      # Python versions; missing or invalid diffs also fail safe to full.
      matrix: ${{ fromJSON(needs.changes.outputs.test_matrix) }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          # diff-cover compares the PR head with the immutable base SHA. A
          # shallow checkout can make that commit unavailable.
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Python ${{ matrix.python-version }}
        uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97  # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}

      - name: Install dependencies
        # The lane's test surface is declared in pyproject.toml as the
        # `ci-linux` extra (see its comment for why jinja2 lives there —
        # reasoning-template tests #2445/#2446 render chat templates with it).
        # This lane MUST stay no-MLX (Apple-Silicon-only), so `--no-deps`
        # installs the package without pulling mlx/mlx-lm. The synced
        # requirements file supplies the complete cross-platform unit-test
        # surface without `-e ".[ci-linux]"` dragging MLX onto Linux.
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -e . --no-deps
          pip install --requirement config/requirements-ci-linux.txt

      - name: Run unit tests (no MLX required)
        env:
          COVERAGE_FILE: coverage-linux-${{ matrix.python-version }}-${{ matrix.shard }}.data
          CI_TEST_SHARD: ${{ matrix.shard }}
        # Ordinary unit tests are discovered by directory. MLX-bound modules
        # own a requires_mlx marker + collection guard. Tests that deliberately
        # consume a real HF cache or network are non-hermetic and stay outside
        # this hosted lane; live/integration tests and the isolated fake-MLX
        # process have stable directory boundaries.
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          ordinary_plan="$RUNNER_TEMP/ordinary-ignores.txt"
          python scripts/ci_test_shard.py \
            --suite ordinary \
            --shard-index "$CI_TEST_SHARD" \
            --shard-count 3 > "$ordinary_plan"
          mapfile -t ordinary_ignores < "$ordinary_plan"
          pytest \
            tests \
            "${ordinary_ignores[@]}" \
            --ignore=tests/integrations \
            --ignore=tests/headless_mlx \
            -m "not requires_mlx and not real_hf_cache and not requires_network and not slow and not integration and not needle" \
            -o faulthandler_timeout=180 \
            -v --tb=short --durations=30 \
            --cov=rapid_mlx \
            --cov=scripts.sidecar_macho_inventory \
            --cov=scripts.pr_validate.steps.stress_e2e_bench \
            --cov=scripts.pr_validate.queue_ready \
            --cov=scripts.pr_validate.runner \
            --cov=scripts.pr_validate.pr_validate \
            --cov=scripts.merge_on_green \
            --cov=scripts.main_guard \
            --cov=scripts.check_release_source_ref \
            --cov=scripts.check_release_environment \
            --cov=scripts.upload_release_r2 \
            --cov=scripts.release_prepare \
            --cov=scripts.release_control \
            --cov=scripts.classify_ci_changes \
            --cov-report=term-missing

          # These lifecycle contracts install inert MLX modules before import.
          # A separate process prevents those fakes from contaminating normal
          # no-MLX discovery while preserving automatic enrollment by folder.
          headless_plan="$RUNNER_TEMP/headless-ignores.txt"
          python scripts/ci_test_shard.py \
            --suite headless \
            --shard-index "$CI_TEST_SHARD" \
            --shard-count 3 > "$headless_plan"
          mapfile -t headless_ignores < "$headless_plan"
          pytest \
            tests/headless_mlx \
            "${headless_ignores[@]}" \
            -v --tb=short --durations=30 \
            --cov=rapid_mlx \
            --cov-append \
            --cov-report=term-missing

      - name: Install package builder for release-stamp integration test
        if: matrix.python-version == '3.12' && matrix.shard == 1
        run: python -m pip install build

      - name: Run real release-stamp package build
        if: matrix.python-version == '3.12' && matrix.shard == 1
        run: |
          pytest \
            tests/test_release_stamp_scripts.py::test_real_build_ships_the_stamp_in_wheel_and_sdist \
            --run-slow -m slow \
            -v --tb=short

      - name: Run real license-file package build
        if: matrix.python-version == '3.12' && matrix.shard == 1
        run: |
          python -m pip install "setuptools>=61.0" wheel
          pytest \
            tests/test_license_files_packaged.py::test_real_distributions_ship_every_tracked_license_file \
            --run-slow -m slow \
            -v --tb=short

      - name: Upload Linux shard coverage data
        if: matrix.python-version == '3.12'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a  # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: linux-coverage-${{ github.sha }}-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage-linux-3.12-${{ matrix.shard }}.data
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 1

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1

        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c  # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: linux-coverage-${{ github.sha }}-*
          path: coverage-data/linux-shards
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Combine Linux shard coverage
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          python -m pip install coverage
          python -m coverage combine coverage-data/linux-shards/coverage-linux-3.12-*.data
          mv .coverage coverage-linux-3.12.data
          COVERAGE_FILE=coverage-linux-3.12.data python -m coverage xml -o coverage.xml

      - name: Upload combined coverage to Codecov
        # The external report is advisory. Keep action bootstrap failures from
        # masking the mandatory local coverage artifact and changed-lines gate.
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@b9fd7d16f6d7d1b5d2bec1a2887e65ceed900238  # v4
        with:
          file: ./coverage.xml
          fail_ci_if_error: false

      - name: Upload combined Linux coverage data
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a  # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: linux-coverage-${{ github.sha }}

          retention-days: 1

              f"tensorfold @ git+{SUPPORTED_RUNTIME_URL}@{SUPPORTED_REVISION}",
          ], check=True)
          PYTHON
          pytest tests/test_tensorfold_qwen27_retention.py \
            -q --tb=short --cov=rapid_mlx --cov-append --cov-report=

      - name: Upload Apple Silicon coverage data
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a  # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: apple-coverage-${{ github.sha }}
          path: coverage-apple.data
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 1

  test-apple-silicon-mac-only:
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      !cancelled() &&
      needs.changes.result == 'success' &&
      needs.changes.outputs.engine == 'true'
    runs-on: macos-15
    # One job, not a shard matrix: hosted macOS arm64 capacity is scarce and
    # queued jobs that are never acquired are cancelled, failing `tests`.
    # The whole selection runs in about 15-20 minutes on one runner.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97  # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Install project and dependencies
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          # The mac-only roster runs in the same .[test] environment that pr_validate validates against.
          pip install -e ".[vision,image,test]"

      - name: Run mac-only tests
        run: |
          files=$(python -m scripts.pr_validate.steps.mac_only_tests --list)
          test -n "$files"
          # Hosted exclusions are maintained in mac_only_tests.HOSTED_DESELECT.
          deselect=$(python -m scripts.pr_validate.steps.mac_only_tests --deselect-args)
          pytest $files $deselect -m "not slow and not integration and not needle and not real_hf_cache and not requires_network" -q --tb=short -p no:cacheprovider -n 3 --dist loadfile

  changed-lines-coverage:
    needs:
      - changes
      - linux-coverage
      - test-apple-silicon
    if: >-
      !cancelled() &&
      needs.changes.result == 'success' &&
      github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&
      needs.changes.outputs.engine == 'true' &&
      needs.linux-coverage.result == 'success' &&
      needs.test-apple-silicon.result == 'success'
    runs-on: ${{ fromJSON((vars.CI_LINUX_LIGHT_RUNNER != '' && (!github.event.pull_request || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository) && (!github.event.workflow_run || github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository)) && vars.CI_LINUX_LIGHT_RUNNER || '"ubuntu-latest"') }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97  # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Install coverage tools
        run: pip install coverage "diff-cover==8.0.3"

      - name: Download Linux coverage data
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c  # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: linux-coverage-${{ github.sha }}
          path: coverage-data/linux

      - name: Download Apple Silicon coverage data
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c  # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: apple-coverage-${{ github.sha }}
          path: coverage-data/apple

      - name: Combine coverage and enforce changed lines
        env:
          PR_BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          python -m coverage combine \
            coverage-data/linux/coverage-linux-3.12.data \
            coverage-data/apple/coverage-apple.data
          python -m coverage xml -o coverage.xml
          python -m diff_cover.diff_cover_tool \
            coverage.xml \
            --compare-branch "$PR_BASE_SHA" \
            --show-uncovered \
            --fail-under 100

  l1-smoke:
    # L1 release-flow gate — a small-model GPU coherence + tool-call format
    # smoke on the FREE macos-15 hosted runner. That runner HAS a real Metal GPU
    # (``mx.default_device()`` -> ``Device(gpu, 0)``), so MLX runs on the GPU
    # there for $0; its ~7GB RAM caps it at small models, not the 35B self-hosted
    # Studio (L2) tier. Runs on promoted and integration heads to catch GROSS
    # engine breakage before landing: garbage-from-first-token (#1234
    # doubled-norm class, via the #1247 GOLDEN gate) and tool-call parser
    # regressions. Ordinary PRs retain Linux + Apple-Silicon coverage without
    # queueing these model downloads.
    #
    # GOLDEN models run coherence + the engine contract. The 4B
    # aliases run contract-only: forcing a zero-argument call factors model
    # competence out while still covering multi-turn replay, streaming channel
    # routing, and native-marker leaks (#1677).
    # Each model runs on its own runner (parallel) so lanes do not share RAM.
    # The Qwen3.5-9B (#2419 top-telemetry cover) was tried here and relocated off
    # L1: its runtime footprint is ~8.7 GB (rapid_mlx/model_recommendations.json,
    # SSOT — bucketed at the 18 GB floor) vs this runner's ~7 GB, and the
    # coherence serve OOMs (server unreachable, 503) under the gate. It, like the
    # 26-35B top-telemetry lanes (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Qwen3.8/3.6-27B, Gemma-4-26B,
    # Bonsai-27B, 15-38GB), exceeds this free runner's ~7GB budget — they stay on
    # the self-hosted 35B Studio tier-1 gate (L2), not on L1.
    #
    # Gemma3 is multimodal but this contract is text/tool-only, so the smoke
    # script forces ``--no-mllm`` and exercises its LM backbone without pulling
    # the vision extra. Ministral remains out after its text lane hung (#1367).
    #
    # The aggregate ``tests`` job requires this matrix, so a contract failure is
    # release-blocking rather than an informational red check.
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      !cancelled() &&
      needs.changes.result == 'success' &&
      needs.changes.outputs.engine == 'true' &&
      needs.changes.outputs.full_gate == 'true'
    runs-on: macos-15
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      # Don't cancel the other legs when one family fails — we want to see
      # which families regressed, not just the first failure.
      fail-fast: false
      matrix: ${{ fromJSON(needs.changes.outputs.l1_matrix) }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97  # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Install project
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          # Lean base install — NO ``[vision]`` extra. Both matrix models are
          # text-only, and ``l1_smoke.sh`` serves with ``--no-mllm`` anyway, so
          # the vision/mlx-vlm deps are never needed and the install stays fast.
          pip install -e .
          # coherence_gate.py + l1_toolcall_check.py drive the server over HTTP;
          # httpx is not a runtime dependency of rapid-mlx itself.
          pip install httpx

      - name: Verify Metal GPU
        # macos-15 hosted runners expose a paravirtualized Metal GPU and MLX
        # defaults to it. A CPU-only default here means a broken toolchain, so
        # assert the GPU device rather than silently smoke-testing on CPU.
        run: |
          python -c "import platform; assert platform.machine() == 'arm64', platform.machine()"
          python -c "import mlx.core as mx; d=str(mx.default_device()); assert 'gpu' in d.lower(), d; print('GPU OK:', d)"

      - name: Prefetch model (${{ matrix.model }})
        # rapid-mlx pull uses the R2 mirror (fast — ~40MB/s), so weights are on
        # disk before the serve boot; no actions/cache needed.
        run: rapid-mlx pull "${{ matrix.model }}"

      - name: L1 smoke (coherence + tool-loop contract)
        env:
          RAPID_MLX_PORT: "8123"
          L1_CONTRACT_ONLY: ${{ matrix.contract_only }}
        run: bash scripts/l1_smoke.sh "${{ matrix.model }}"

  tests:
    needs:
      - changes
      - lint
      - engine-contracts
      - mlx-bound-guard
      - type-check
      - test-matrix
      - linux-coverage
      - test-apple-silicon
      - test-apple-silicon-mac-only
      - changed-lines-coverage
      - l1-smoke
    runs-on: ${{ fromJSON((vars.CI_LINUX_LIGHT_RUNNER != '' && (!github.event.pull_request || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository) && (!github.event.workflow_run || github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository)) && vars.CI_LINUX_LIGHT_RUNNER || '"ubuntu-latest"') }}
    # Keep the required verdict terminal after failure or cancellation;
    # classifier and workload jobs above stop when their source is superseded.
    if: always()
    steps:
      - name: Check test results
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: |
          if [ "${{ needs.changes.result }}" != success ]; then
            echo "CI change classifier failed"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "${{ needs.lint.result }}" != success ]; then
            echo "Universal repository guards failed"
            exit 1
          fi
          expected="${{ needs.changes.outputs.engine }}"
          if [ "$expected" != "true" ]; then
            echo "Engine lanes not required for this change"
            exit 0
          fi
          if [ "${{ needs.engine-contracts.result }}" != success ]; then
            echo "Engine lint and static contracts failed"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "${{ needs.type-check.result }}" != success ]; then
            echo "Type-check job failed"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = pull_request ] \
            && [ "${{ needs.mlx-bound-guard.result }}" != success ]; then
            echo "MLX dependency-bound guard failed"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "${{ needs.test-matrix.result }}" != "success" ]; then
            echo "Unit tests failed"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "${{ needs.linux-coverage.result }}" != "success" ]; then
            echo "Linux shard coverage merge failed"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "${{ needs.test-apple-silicon.result }}" != "success" ]; then
            echo "Apple Silicon tests failed"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "${{ needs.test-apple-silicon-mac-only.result }}" != "success" ]; then
            echo "Apple Silicon mac-only tests failed"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = pull_request ] \
            && [ "${{ needs.changed-lines-coverage.result }}" != "success" ]; then
            echo "Changed-lines coverage union failed"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "${{ needs.changes.outputs.full_gate }}" = "true" ]; then
            if [ "${{ needs.l1-smoke.result }}" != "success" ]; then
              echo "Small-model tool-loop contract failed"
              exit 1
            fi
          elif [ "${{ needs.l1-smoke.result }}" != "skipped" ]; then
            echo "Unpromoted head unexpectedly allocated the L1 smoke lane"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Reject cancelled workflow
        if: ${{ cancelled() }}
        run: |
          echo "CI workflow was cancelled"
          exit 1
