sampled_files.README.md:
Rapid-MLX

Run Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Pi, Hermes, Crush or Goose with a local model on Mac:
rapid-mlx launch <agent>

**1. Install** — the guided installer handles Python and picks a model for your Mac: ```bash curl -fsSL https://rapidmlx.com/install.sh | bash ``` Restart your terminal or run `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"`. Prefer [pip (Python 3.12+)](#alternative-install-methods) or Homebrew (`brew install rapid-mlx`)? Both install the same CLI. **2. Launch your coding agent** — install your chosen agent, then run one of: Using an SDK instead? [Jump to the Python quickstart](#python-quickstart). ```bash rapid-mlx launch claude-code rapid-mlx launch opencode rapid-mlx launch codex ``` `rapid-mlx launch ` creates a private profile, starts the server, and launches the agent. Run the same command tomorrow; `rapid-mlx launch claude-code --remove` removes Rapid's private profile without changing your existing Claude Code settings. [One-command guides for each agent](https://rapidmlx.com/docs/agents/). A first reply can take longer while a model downloads, loads, or processes the agent's opening prompt. For other tools, use `rapid-mlx agents --setup`, for example `rapid-mlx agents cline --setup`.

Rapid-MLX is an open-source (Apache 2.0) OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible LLM inference server for Apple Silicon, built on MLX, focused on reliable tool calling for coding agents.
Up to 4× faster than Apple's MLX (mlx-lm), 1.5× on a typical task — same model, same weights.
Decode speed, Qwen3.5-9B 4-bit on a Mac mini M4 Pro, greedy decoding, both servers at their defaults — per-task results, method, and raw data.

**Faster decode than oMLX and LM Studio on Qwen3.5-9B, Qwen3.8-27B, and Qwen3.6-35B** Measured speed on a Mac Studio M5 Max (36 GB) — Rapid-MLX 0.16.1 vs oMLX 0.7.0 and LM Studio, using the same base 4-bit weights for each model. | Model | Metric | Rapid-MLX | oMLX | LM Studio | |---|---|---:|---:|---:| | Qwen3.5-9B | Decode (tok/s) | **115.5** | 77.9 | 81.0 | | Qwen3.5-9B | 4 streams (tok/s) | **248.2** | 224.6 | 230.0 | | Qwen3.8-27B | Decode (tok/s) | **37.9** | 25.3 | 26.0 | | Qwen3.8-27B | 4 streams (tok/s) | **82.8** | 75.3 | 69.7 | | Qwen3.6-35B | Decode (tok/s) | **173.4** | 145.8 | 124.5 | | Qwen3.6-35B | 4 streams (tok/s) | **293.9** | 281.9 | 265.6 | | Qwen3.6-35B | 2K-prompt first token (s, lower is better) | **0.55** | 1.14 | 1.49 | Single run per engine; default serving modes with Rapid's MTP text mode, oMLX's SSD cache, and LM Studio's configured context and four parallel slots. [Full results and raw data](https://rapidmlx.com/compare). **Or use the OpenAI / Anthropic SDK** Start a local server, then run the Python examples below from a separate terminal: ```bash rapid-mlx serve qwen3.5-4b-4bit --port 8000 ``` On first run, this command downloads a ~3 GB 4B model if it is not already cached. Without `--port`, the server picks the first free port in `8000`–`8009`; these examples pin `8000`. Install your SDK with `pip install openai` or `pip install anthropic`. OpenAI Python — base URL includes `/v1`: ```python from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1", api_key="not-needed") print(client.chat.completions.create( model="default", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello"}], ).choices[0].message.content) ``` Anthropic Python — base URL is the host; the SDK calls `/v1/messages`: ```python from anthropic import Anthropic client = Anthropic(base_url="http://localhost:8000", api_key="not-needed") msg = client.messages.create( model="default", max_tokens=256, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello"}], ) print("".join(b.text for b in msg.content if b.type == "text")) ```

rapidmlx.com · Docs · Model mirror · Desktop app · Discord

--- ## How it compares Feature facts only, taken mostly from each project's own documentation as of 2026-09-26 (sources below). For speed, see the measured results above. | | Rapid-MLX | [oMLX](https://github.com/jundot/omlx) | [Ollama](https://github.com/ollama/ollama) | [LM Studio](https://lmstudio.ai) | [mlx-lm](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm) (`mlx_lm.server`) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | **License** | Apache-2.0 | Apache-2.0 | MIT | Closed-source app; its MLX engine and `lms` CLI are MIT | MIT | | **Inference engine on a Mac** | MLX | MLX | GGML/GGUF engine, plus an MLX engine for safetensors models | llama.cpp (GGUF) and MLX engines | MLX | | **Local API** | OpenAI (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`) and Anthropic Messages (`/v1/messages`) | OpenAI and Anthropic Messages | Ollama API, OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic-compatible (subset) | OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic-compatible, LM Studio REST API | OpenAI-style chat API | | **GUI** | Rapid-MLX Desktop (macOS app) | macOS menu-bar app and web admin panel | Desktop app (macOS, Windows) | Desktop app | None (CLI / Python) | | **Concurrent requests** | Continuous batching | Continuous batching (mlx-lm `BatchGenerator`) | Parallel requests per model (`OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL`, default 1) | Continuous batching (llama.cpp engine; Chat with a model right now:** ```bash rapid-mlx chat ``` With no model named, `rapid-mlx chat` uses a chat model already on this Mac — the `lfm2.5-2.6b-4bit` starter if present, otherwise the best fit for this Mac's memory — without another download. If none is downloaded yet, it downloads the `lfm2.5-2.6b-4bit` starter (~1.6 GB) before opening the REPL. Type `/help` for slash commands, `/exit` to quit. **2. Or serve it for use from other apps:** ```bash rapid-mlx serve qwen3.5-4b-4bit ``` Starts an OpenAI-compatible HTTP server on the first free port in `8000`–`8009` when `--port` is omitted. An explicit `--port` never falls back. The examples below assume port `8000` was selected. Point any client that supports a local custom endpoint (Aider, LangChain, OpenCode, PydanticAI, your own scripts) at **`http://localhost:8000/v1`**; Claude Code / Anthropic SDK uses **`http://localhost:8000`** (the Anthropic messages route lives at `/v1/messages` under the same host). ```bash curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"default","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello"}]}' ``` ```python from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1", api_key="not-needed") print(client.chat.completions.create( model="default", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello"}], ).choices[0].message.content) ``` **3. Or wire up your coding agent — one command:** ```bash rapid-mlx launch claude-code ``` This saves a private Claude Code profile, starts a local server if needed, and launches Claude Code without editing `~/.claude/settings.json`. The same command works after a restart. Swap in `codex`, `opencode`, `pi`, `hermes`, `crush`, or `goose`. For the original config-writing behavior, use `--legacy-config`; `cline` and `continue-dev` keep their existing setup flow. [Agent setup details](docs/guides/ai-clients.md#coding-agents). > **Cursor:** Cursor currently routes BYOK requests through its own servers, so its servers cannot reach a Rapid-MLX endpoint on `localhost`. Rapid-MLX therefore does not generate a Cursor localhost config. If you intentionally expose the server through a public HTTPS tunnel, set `RAPID_MLX_API_KEY=your-secret` for both `rapid-mlx serve ...` and `rapid-mlx launch cursor --server-url https://your-public-host`. This is no longer a fully local connection; never expose an unauthenticated server. Rapid-MLX rejects explicit local/private addresses but cannot verify reachability from Cursor's network, whose DNS view may differ from your Mac. > **Vision / image / video models?** They work out of the box with the official installer above (and Rapid-MLX Desktop), which include the vision, image-generation and video-generation runtimes. Three backends ship — **Wan 2.1 / 2.2**, **CogVideoX-Fun** and **LTX-2.3** — across 8 registered checkpoints. `wan2.2-ti2v-5b-q8` is the recommended starting point: smallest of the Wan set, and TI2V means one checkpoint does both text-to-video and image-to-video. The video runtime ships with the base install. Install `ffmpeg` for the final MP4 mux. ```bash brew install ffmpeg rapid-mlx serve wan2.2-ti2v-5b-q8 ``` Create and download a clip: ```bash curl http://localhost:8000/v1/videos \ -F model=wan2.2-ti2v-5b-q8 \ -F 'prompt=A fox running through fresh snow, cinematic tracking shot' \ -F seconds=1 \ -F size=832x512 # Poll until GET /v1/videos/VIDEO_ID reports "status": "completed", then: curl http://localhost:8000/v1/videos/VIDEO_ID/content -o output.mp4 ``` The create call returns a job immediately. Poll `GET /v1/videos/VIDEO_ID` until `status` is `completed`. Add `-F input_reference=@start.png` for image-to-video. Generation is serialized — one clip at a time — because two diffusion pipelines resident at once will exhaust unified memory. Expect minutes of compute per second of footage, not real time. → [Every checkpoint, RAM requirement and tuning knob](https://rapidmlx.com/docs/models/families/video.html) --- ## Audio: speech, transcription, voice cloning The dependency commands below use the official `install.sh` environment. For Homebrew or another install method, follow [optional extras](https://rapidmlx.com/docs/extras.html). Audio aliases behind the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/audio/*` endpoints — any OpenAI SDK works unchanged. `tts-1`, `tts-1-hd`, and `gpt-4o-mini-tts` select the default TTS model (served TTS model, otherwise Kokoro). ```bash ~/.rapid-mlx/bin/python -m pip install 'rapid-mlx[audio]' # Text to speech rapid-mlx serve kokoro curl --fail http://localhost:8000/v1/audio/speech \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"kokoro","input":"hello from rapid-mlx"}' --output hello.wav # Transcription (Whisper / Parakeet / SenseVoice) rapid-mlx serve whisper-large-v3-turbo curl http://localhost:8000/v1/audio/transcriptions \ -F file=@hello.wav -F model=whisper-large-v3-turbo ``` Beyond the basics, three things you may not expect to run locally: - **Zero-shot voice cloning** from a reference clip. `indextts` is the only one that takes the clip alone; `qwen3-tts-clone`, `f5-tts-zh` and `chatterbox` all require `ref_text` (the clip's exact transcript) paired with `ref_audio`, and the request is rejected before generation if it is missing. - **Voice design** — `qwen3-tts-voicedesign` has no named speakers at all. Describe the voice you want in natural language via `instructions` (timbre, gender, age, accent, emotion, prosody) and it synthesises it. - **Forced alignment** — `qwen3-aligner` takes audio *plus the transcript you already have* and returns per-character timings. It never guesses at the words, so it cannot mis-hear them; that is what karaoke captions and beat-synced editing need. Also: word-level timestamps on transcription, and local text-to-music at `/v1/audio/music`. → [All 53 aliases across 17 families](https://rapidmlx.com/docs/models/families/audio.html) --- ## Typed decisions with System One Serve fast `noul`, `choice`, and `score` decisions through a TypeSafe-compatible `/v1/systemone` API. Homebrew — Mac-native, one command, prebuilt bottle from homebrew/core ```bash brew install rapid-mlx ``` Available in homebrew-core. Upgrade with `brew upgrade rapid-mlx`.
uv — isolated tool install, auto-manages Python ```bash uv tool install rapid-mlx@latest ``` Don't have uv yet? `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh`. Upgrade with `uv tool upgrade rapid-mlx`. On a Python 3.10/3.11 tool environment use `uv tool upgrade --python 3.12 rapid-mlx`.
pip — requires Python 3.12+ (macOS ships 3.9) ```bash python3.12 -m venv ~/.venvs/rapid-mlx ~/.venvs/rapid-mlx/bin/pip install rapid-mlx ``` Add `~/.venvs/rapid-mlx/bin` to your PATH or call the executable directly. If `python3.12` is missing, use the official installer above or install Python 3.12 with Homebrew first. Upgrade with the pip of the environment that holds Rapid-MLX, e.g. `~/.venvs/rapid-mlx/bin/pip install -U rapid-mlx` for the environment above (an existing install made with an earlier Python 3.12 pip command upgrades with that same Python's pip). An install on Python 3.10/3.11 stays on 1.0.0 (`Requirement already satisfied`); reinstall it with Python 3.12 — see [Upgrading from Python 3.10 or 3.11](https://rapidmlx.com/docs/getting-started/installation.html#upgrading-from-python-310-or-311). Image-input / VLM models (Qwen-VL, Gemma 4, true multimodal) need no extra step — the vision runtime ships with the base install. See [Optional extras](https://rapidmlx.com/docs/extras.html) for audio and embeddings. For the complete feature set — chat, embeddings, audio, and System One on top of the base install — install the `[all]` extra: `~/.venvs/rapid-mlx/bin/pip install 'rapid-mlx[all]'`. Audio alone is `~/.venvs/rapid-mlx/bin/pip install 'rapid-mlx[audio]'`; see [Optional extras](https://rapidmlx.com/docs/extras.html).

Weather, web search and `web_fetch(url)` are available to tool-capable models by default. The CLI shows tool progress and numbered sources after the answer; `/export` retains those sources. Weather uses Open-Meteo without a key. Search uses Keenable's public tier without a key. Set `KEENABLE_API_KEY`, `RAPID_MLX_TAVILY_API_KEY` or `RAPID_MLX_BRAVE_API_KEY` in the owner's environment to use a keyed provider. `RAPID_MLX_WEB_SEARCH_PROVIDER=tavily|brave|keenable` selects explicitly; otherwise configured keyed providers precede public Keenable. Rate limits, server errors and timeouts fail over to the next available provider. Keys stay in memory and are never saved in chat history. Providers can throttle or return no useful results. Each turn carries local date, weekday, time, timezone and coarse locale beside its user message, preserving the stable system/tool prefix. Search results keep provider dates when available and label missing dates. Explicitly current queries are anchored to the full local date unless they already specify a date or a historical period. Explicit "today" searches omit known older results, retaining unknown dates for verification; provider publication dates are not event dates. For article summaries, the assistant is instructed to follow the story link and cite the evidence. Web calls are limited to four per run. All tools share a 16,000-byte model-return allowance per run, including file and terminal output; older tool results may be compacted for the model while original evidence remains in the local event journal. At the limit, the runtime makes one tools-disabled answer attempt. An empty recovery produces a visible failure message, without claiming a verified answer. The built-in `delegate_task(task, context?, tools?)` tool is available by default inside the harness. It gives a helper a fresh history containing only its task and supplied context. Helpers use the same local model, workspace, and approval policy. Optional tool names narrow the parent's available tools; helpers cannot delegate again. Up to three helpers run concurrently in the owner, using the inference server's batching. Each helper has a 120-second deadline, six model requests, eight tool calls, and a 12,000-token usage budget; its web/result limits are independent of the parent's. Exhausted or timed-out helpers return an explicit partial summary. The parent combines their summaries and sources. The CLI shows compact nested helper progress. Child actions use the normal approval prompt with helper attribution; Ctrl-C stops the parent and all its helpers. Child transcripts stay out of visible branch messages but are retained locally without reasoning and included as collapsed details in `/export`. Chat stores use schema 4. Earlier experimental schemas require a new profile; existing schema 4 profiles reopen unchanged, and incompatible stores are refused. For offline use, set `RAPID_MLX_CHAT_WEB_TOOLS=0` before starting a new profile owner, for example `RAPID_MLX_CHAT_WEB_TOOLS=0 rapid-mlx chat --harness --profile offline`. An already-running owner keeps its startup environment. Weather and search have a 10-second total timeout. Fetch has a 20-second total timeout, allowing up to 10 seconds for Keenable before trying the direct fallback; Ctrl-C cancels an in-flight request. Editing or regenerating a turn runs read-only tools again for fresh information. Search returns snippets; `web_fetch` reads a page using Keenable, with a direct HTTP(S) fallback that rejects private network addresses, pins validated IPs and checks every redirect. Responses are size- and content-type-bounded; extracted page text is capped at 8,000 UTF-8 bytes and may be shortened further to fit the remaining tool-output allowance, with a truncation marker. Fetching needs no per-domain prompt. MCP, custom system prompts, and Desktop integration remain outside this experimental slice. See the [chat owner decision](docs/engineering/decisions/2026-10-25-chat-owner-topology.md) for lifecycle and durability details.

]

    # architecture used by Rapid's Whisper silence guard and also contains
    # the fix for the 0.4.4 Kokoro istftnet length regression. Keep a minor
    # cap so audio runtime/API changes are adopted deliberately.
    "mlx-audio>=0.5.3,<0.6",
    # F5-TTS (pure-MLX, no torch): EN+ZH multilingual + zero-shot voice cloning.
    # Fills the Chinese expressive/cloneable TTS gap. Standalone package (not an
    # mlx_audio family) — wired directly in audio/tts.py's `f5` branch.
    "f5-tts-mlx==0.2.6",
    "sounddevice>=0.4.0",
    "soundfile>=0.12.0,<0.15",
    "scipy>=1.10.0",
    "numba>=0.57.0",
    "tiktoken>=0.5.0,<0.14",
    "misaki[zh,ja]>=0.5.0",  # Chinese (zh) and Japanese (ja) support
    "spacy>=3.7.0",
    "num2words>=0.5.0",
    "loguru>=0.7.0",
    # R6-H1 (Eva 0.8.7 dogfood): Kokoro TTS imports ``misaki.espeak`` which
    # calls ``EspeakWrapper.set_data_path(...)`` (the legacy 3.2-era API).
    # Two things need to line up for that call to succeed on a fresh
    # ``pip install rapid-mlx[audio]``:
    #
    #   1. ``espeakng-loader`` provides the bundled libespeak-ng binary
    #      and ``espeak-ng-data/`` directory misaki passes to
    #      ``set_data_path``. Without it, the import crashes inside
    #      ``misaki/espeak.py`` with ``ModuleNotFoundError`` before any
    #      TTS request reaches the engine.
    #   2. ``phonemizer-fork`` (NOT vanilla ``phonemizer``) is the only
    #      package that still exposes ``EspeakWrapper.set_data_path``.
    #      Vanilla ``phonemizer>=3.3.0`` removed it in favour of a
    #      property-only ``data_path`` accessor — so the legacy API
    #      misaki uses raises ``AttributeError: type object
    #      'EspeakWrapper' has no attribute 'set_data_path'`` and the
    #      Kokoro TTS route 500s on first request.
    #
    # Pin ``phonemizer-fork`` BEFORE the vanilla ``phonemizer`` line and
    # drop the vanilla pin — pip installs the first one wins and they
    # claim the same import name, so leaving both in produces a
    # non-deterministic resolution depending on resolver order.
    # ``test_audio_extras_lockin.py`` asserts both packages are
    # importable and that ``EspeakWrapper.set_data_path`` exists so we
    # catch a future drift back to vanilla phonemizer in CI.
    "espeakng-loader>=0.2.0",
    "phonemizer-fork>=3.3.0",
    # Additional multilingual dependencies
    "cn2an>=0.5.0",          # Chinese number conversion
]

audio-desktop = [

]
# Image-generation runtime. Already part of the base install on macOS; kept as

image = [

    "mflux>=0.23.0,<0.24; platform_system == 'Darwin'",

    "pillow>=12.3.0,<13; platform_system == 'Darwin'",
    "sentencepiece>=0.2.0,<0.3; platform_system == 'Darwin'",
]

    "rapid_mlx/models/deepseek_v4*.py",

    "E402",   # module-level import not at top
    "E501",   # line too long
    "E731",   # lambda assignment
    "B004",   # unreliable callable check
    "B008",   # function call in default arg
    "B011",   # assert false
    "B017",   # assert raises exception
    "B905",   # zip without strict
    "N801",   # class name casing
    "N806",   # variable in function casing
    "SIM103", # needless bool
    "SIM108", # ternary instead of if-else
    "SIM110", # reimplemented builtin
    "SIM222", # expr or true
    "UP028",  # yield in for loop
    "SIM102", # collapsible if
    "SIM105", # suppressible exception
    "SIM115", # open file with context handler

repository.readme:
# NotebookLM REST API + MCP server **Automate Google Gemini Notebook — formerly, and still widely known as, NotebookLM — at scale. 62-endpoint HTTP REST API for n8n / Zapier / Make / curl, an MCP server for Claude Code / Cursor / Codex, a UTCP interface for clients that call the API natively, and Rust and Ruby clients. Citation-backed Q&A, full Studio generation (audio · video · infographic · report · presentation · data table), multi-account rotation with auto-reauth across personal and Google Workspace accounts.** > v4.12.0 — **Node 22 is now the floor, and the last four open advisories are gone with it.** The declared floor of Node 18 had quietly become fiction: three production dependencies already required Node 20 or newer, and the test matrix kept passing on 18 without exercising them. Raising it also let the third-party file globber go — its dependency chain carried four advisories with no fix upstream — replaced by Node's built-in search, now actually under test. Builds on **4.0.0**, where the HTTP API stopped being open to the network and to any web page ([GHSA-p69m-c5rf-g2c3](https://github.com/roomi-fields/gemini-notebook-mcp/security/advisories/GHSA-p69m-c5rf-g2c3)): it binds loopback, refuses unlisted origins, and takes a bearer token — **remote access and Docker require `NOTEBOOKLM_API_KEY`**, see [Securing the HTTP API](./deployment/docs/15-SECURITY.md). Built on a **dual transport** — the internal `batchexecute` RPC API (10-100× faster than scraping, immune to UI rebrands) with the Playwright browser as an automatic fallback. See the [changelog](./CHANGELOG.md). > **Note (July 2026):** Google rebranded **NotebookLM** to **Gemini Notebook**. It is the same product, existing links redirect, and this project drives the same underlying service — the browser path was updated for the new DOM in v2.3.0 and the RPC path in v3.0.0. Package and repository keep the `notebooklm` name. --- > **Unofficial project — good to know before you start** > > This is not affiliated with Google. It talks to the same `batchexecute` > endpoints the NotebookLM web app uses, with a browser fallback when they move. > They are undocumented, so they can change without notice — when that happens we > ship a fix, as we have for every change so far. > > Two practical notes: use a **dedicated Google account** for automation, and > expect NotebookLM's own quotas to apply at high volume. See > [Disclaimer](#disclaimer) for the full text. --- ## What You Can Build 🔗 **No-code automation pipelines** — The 62-endpoint REST API means NotebookLM becomes a step in n8n, Zapier, Make, or a plain `curl` in cron. No agent, no MCP client, no Node in your stack — just HTTP. This is the half most NotebookLM libraries don't have. 🤖 **Agent tooling** — The same engine over MCP for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex, with a bundled skill that primes the agent on citation formats, the daily-quota-aware batch pattern, and transport selection. 📚 **Research at volume** — Multi-account rotation with automatic re-authentication, built for overnight runs of 1 000+ questions across several notebooks without babysitting. 🎙️ **Full Studio generation** — Audio overviews, video, infographics, reports, presentations, data tables, plus flashcards, quizzes and mind maps — generated and downloaded programmatically. ## Use Cases & Recipes NotebookLM is a **grounded** engine: Gemini reads your sources and answers _from them_, with citations. The winning pattern is to let it do the expensive reading while your own stack handles orchestration and the last mile. **Spend fewer tokens — offload the reading** - **🪙 Zero-token synthesis layer** — Drop 30 documents in a notebook, let Gemini do the heavy analysis, and spend your agent's context only on the final polish. The reasoning happens server-side; your agent just orchestrates (`add_notebook` → `source_add` → `notebook_ask`). - **💾 Answer cache you can re-read offline** — `vault_batch` writes every answer to disk as structured JSON against a published [schema](https://schemas.roomi-fields.com/nblm-answer-v1.json), so a batch run becomes a corpus you can grep, diff, re-index, or feed to a retrieval layer — without re-querying and re-spending quota. **Wire it into things that aren't agents** - **⚙️ NotebookLM as an n8n / Zapier / Make step** — Because it speaks plain HTTP, a citation-backed answer becomes one node in a workflow: a form submission triggers a question, the cited answer lands in a sheet, a Slack message, or a database. No agent runtime involved. - **📄 Document intake pipeline** — Watch a folder or an inbox, push new PDFs and URLs in as sources, and ask a standing set of questions against them on every arrival. **Grounded answers with a paper trail** - **🔍 Citations with the actual source text** — Answers come back with source names _and the quoted excerpts_ they rest on, extracted from the citation panel — so a claim can be checked, not just attributed. - **🎓 Literature review at thesis scale** — Batch 100+ research questions across multiple notebooks, rotate accounts as daily quotas run out, and resume where it stopped. Built for, and tested on, exactly this. **Get artifacts back out** - **🔁 One source set, every format** — Fan a single notebook out to a podcast, a video, a slide deck, a report, a quiz and a mind map, then download them all locally. --- ## In the Wild Real deployments, not hypotheticals. - **📚 A doctoral literature review at batch scale** — The project was built for, and is continuously tested on, overnight runs of **1 000+ research questions** spread across several notebooks: multi-account rotation picks up when a daily quota runs out, every answer is written to disk with its citations, and an interrupted run resumes instead of starting over. The batch pattern in [`vault_batch`](#features) exists because a thesis needed it. - **🔌 Replacing a RAG engine with the REST API** — [`musnymubarak/Calim_Doc`](https://github.com/musnymubarak/Calim_Doc) swapped a Gemini-based retrieval engine for this project's HTTP API, running it as a Docker service (`notebooklm:3000`) behind a full client and worker layer. A good illustration of the REST half: no agent runtime, no MCP client — NotebookLM simply became a backend service their Python app calls. Built something with it? Open an issue — this section is for other people's work. ## Features ### Q&A with Citations - **Ask questions** to NotebookLM and get accurate, citation-backed answers - **Source citation extraction** with 5 formats: none, inline, footnotes, json, expanded (97% excerpt success rate) - **Session management** for multi-turn conversations with auto-reauth on session expiry ### Content Generation Generate multiple content types from your notebook sources: | Content Type | Formats | Options | | ------------------ | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- | | **Audio Overview** | Podcast-style discussion | Language (80+), custom instructions | | **Video** | Brief, Explainer | 6 visual styles, language, custom instructions | | **Infographic** | Horizontal, Vertical | Language, custom instructions | | **Report** | Summary, Detailed | Language, custom instructions | | **Presentation** | Overview, Detailed | Language, custom instructions | | **Data Table** | Simple, Detailed | Language, custom instructions | | **Flashcards** | Study cards | Language, custom instructions | | **Quiz** | Assessment questions | Language, custom instructions | | **Mind Map** | Interactive node graph | Saved to the notebook | **Video Visual Styles**: classroom, documentary, animated, corporate, cinematic, minimalist **Language of generated content**: pass `language` to any generator — a BCP-47 code (`es`, `ja`, `pt_BR`, `zh_Hans`) or a name in English or in the language itself (`"Spanish"`, `"Español"`). 81 languages are accepted, and an unrecognised one is refused rather than quietly swapped for another. Set a default with `NOTEBOOKLM_CONTENT_LANGUAGE`; it is deliberately independent of `NOTEBOOKLM_UI_LOCALE`, which only picks the interface language the browser fallback reads. Flashcards and quizzes are generated via `generate_study_aid`; mind maps via `generate_mind_map`. v3 also adds `share_notebook`, `manage_labels`, and `research_sources` (web/Drive source discovery) — see the [changelog](./CHANGELOG.md). ### Content Download - **Download Audio** — WAV audio files - **Download Video** — MP4 video files - **Download Infographic** — PNG image files - Text-based content (report, presentation, data_table) is returned in the API response - **Delete generated content** (`content_delete`) — until now a notebook accumulated every draft anyone ever asked for, with no way to remove one short of the web UI ### Source Management - **Add sources**: Files (PDF, TXT, DOCX, audio, images), URLs, Text, YouTube videos, Google Drive - **List sources**: Every source with its ID and title (`source_list`) - **Rename a source** (`rename_source`): fix a title in place, by id or by name - **Check freshness** (`check_source_freshness`): which URL / Drive sources have drifted from what they point at — the whole notebook in one call. An unanswered source is reported as unknown, never as current - **Read a source's guide** (`get_source_guide`): NotebookLM's own summary and key topics for one source - **Read a source in full** (`source_read`): the exact text NotebookLM indexed — what it actually reasons over, which the web UI only shows in fragments. Quote a source verbatim, check what a PDF really yielded, or hand the raw material to another tool. Name the source instead of its ID if you prefer; an ambiguous name is refused rather than guessed. Long sources arrive **one page at a time**, with an explicit instruction for fetching the next — or `paginate: false` for the whole document at once. ### Notebook Summary and Chat History - **What is in this notebook?** (`get_notebook_summary`) — NotebookLM's own summary of its sources plus the questions it suggests asking, without spending a question to find out - **What was already asked?** (`get_chat_history`) — read back the recorded questions and answers, newest first. An agent resuming work stops paying to ask what it already asked. NotebookLM exposes only the most recent conversation per notebook - **Clear the history** (`delete_chat_history`) — the web UI's "Delete history". There is no per-turn delete: the whole conversation goes ### Artifact Export and Revision - **Export to Drive** (`export_artifact`) — send a finished artifact to Google Docs or Google Sheets - **Revise one slide** (`revise_slide`) — change a single slide from a prompt instead of regenerating the whole deck ### Notebook Library - **Multi-notebook management** with validation and smart selection - **Auto-discovery**: Automatically generate metadata via NotebookLM queries - **Search notebooks** by keyword in name, description, or topics - **Scrape notebooks**: List all notebooks from NotebookLM with IDs and names - **Bulk delete**: Delete multiple notebooks at once ### Accounts & Localization - **Personal _and_ Google Workspace accounts** — recognizes both NotebookLM hosts (`notebooklm.google.com` and the `notebook.google.com` Workspace alias), so Workspace sessions authenticate cleanly instead of looping on "session expired" - **UI-language-aware** — drives NotebookLM whether its interface is in English, French, German, or Japanese (`en` · `fr` · `de` · `ja`); [add a language](./docs/ADDING_A_LANGUAGE.md) in a single JSON file ### UTCP Interface [UTCP](https://www.utcp.io/) — the Universal Tool Calling Protocol — is the inverse of MCP: **there is no protocol server and no wrapper process**. A client reads a tool manual once, then calls this REST API directly, so nothing sits between the agent and the endpoint. ```bash # The manual. 56 tools, named the same as the MCP tools. curl -H "X-API-Key: $NOTEBOOKLM_API_KEY" http://localhost:3000/utcp ``` - **`GET /utcp`** — the manual for a running server, with every call address rebased on the address the request arrived at, so one document serves a loopback install and a reverse-proxied one alike. - **Also published statically** at [notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/utcp.json](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/utcp.json), for a client configured before the server is up. - **62 named tools** — the manual reuses the MCP tool names, so `search_passages` is `search_passages` on both sides rather than something synthesised from a URL path. Every operation in the [OpenAPI 3.1 spec](./deployment/docs/openapi.yaml) carries a matching `operationId`, which also means a client pointed straight at the specification converts it correctly on its own. - **Authentication is declared the way UTCP clients implement it** — as an `api_key` in the `X-API-Key` header, which this server accepts alongside the bearer form. The key itself is never in the manual, only the literal `${NOTEBOOKLM_API_KEY}`, which is how a client asks for a value from its own environment. (A client that converts the specification instead will not pick up authentication at all, since the converter does not map bearer schemes — one reason to prefer the manual.) Generated from the specification on every release and held in step by a build guard, so the manual cannot describe a version that is not the one you are running. Details: [REST API reference → `GET /utcp`](./deployment/docs/03-API.md). ### Rust client A typed async client lives in this repository at [`crates/notebooklm-client`](./crates/notebooklm-client) and is published as [**`notebooklm`**](https://crates.io/crates/notebooklm) on crates.io ([docs](https://docs.rs/notebooklm)), one version per release. It covers **all 62 operations** — generated from the specification, with a synchronous twin behind one feature flag. ```rust let client = notebooklm::Client::local()?; let answer = client.ask_question(&AskRequest::new(&id, "What is ikigai?")).await?; println!("{}", answer.answer); ``` It deliberately **does not own a browser**: the Google session is bound to the machine it was made on, expires server-side while local cookies still look valid, and needs a driver kept patched against detection. The crate talks to this server, which already does all three. The reasoning in full: [driving it from Rust](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/blog/notebooklm-rust). ### Ruby client The same surface as a gem, in this repository at [`gems/notebooklm`](./gems/notebooklm) and published as [**`notebooklm`**](https://rubygems.org/gems/notebooklm) on RubyGems, also one version per release. All 62 operations, generated from the same specification, every response shape documented field by field — and no runtime dependencies. ```ruby client = NotebookLM.local answer = client.ask(notebook.id, 'What is ikigai?') answer.citations.each { |c| puts "[#{c.number}] #{c.source_text}" } ``` Why a gem at all, and why it owns no browser either: [driving it from Ruby](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/blog/notebooklm-ruby). ### Integration Options - **MCP Protocol** — Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, any MCP client - **[UTCP](https://www.utcp.io/)** — a tool manual at `/utcp`, for clients that call the REST API natively with no protocol server in between ([see above](#utcp-interface)) - **Agent Skill** — ships a bundled [`notebooklm` skill](./skills/notebooklm/SKILL.md) (also standalone: [`roomi-fields/notebooklm-skill`](https://github.com/roomi-fields/notebooklm-skill)) that teaches the agent citation formats, the batch-to-cache pattern, and when to use which transport - **HTTP REST API** — n8n, Zapier, Make.com, custom integrations - **Docker** — Isolated deployment with Docker or Docker Compose - **[RTFM](https://github.com/roomi-fields/rtfm) retrieval layer** — `/batch-to-vault` writes citation-backed answers as markdown + JSON sidecars (`nblm-answer-v1` schema), indexable by [RTFM](https://github.com/roomi-fields/rtfm) (FTS5 + semantic) for unlimited offline queries. Ideal for academic / SOTA workflows. [Guide](./deployment/docs/14-RTFM-INTEGRATION.md). --- ## Quick Start ### Option 0 — Claude Code marketplace (one-liner, recommended for Claude Code users) The fastest way to get NotebookLM into Claude Code. Distributed via the [`roomi-fields/claude-plugins`](https://github.com/roomi-fields/claude-plugins) marketplace alongside [RTFM](https://github.com/roomi-fields/rtfm) (the retrieval companion — see [RTFM integration guide](./deployment/docs/14-RTFM-INTEGRATION.md)): ```text /plugin marketplace add roomi-fields/claude-plugins /plugin install notebooklm@roomi-fields ``` That registers the MCP server **and the `notebooklm` agent skill**, runs `npx -y @roomi-fields/notebooklm-mcp@` automatically (Node ≥ 22 required), and lets you upgrade with two commands when a new release ships: `/plugin marketplace update roomi-fields` then `/reload-plugins`. Then run `npx -y -p @roomi-fields/notebooklm-mcp notebooklm-mcp-setup-auth` once in a terminal to log into Google (a visible Chrome opens). To install RTFM at the same time: `/plugin install rtfm@roomi-fields`. ### Option 1 — HTTP REST API (n8n, Zapier, Make, curl, any HTTP client) ```bash git clone https://github.com/roomi-fields/gemini-notebook-mcp.git cd gemini-notebook-mcp npm install && npm run build npm run setup-auth # One-time Google login npm run start:http # Start REST API on port 3000 ``` ```bash # Citation-backed Q&A, single curl, JSON response curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/ask \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"question": "Summarize chapter 3", "notebook_id": "your-id", "source_format": "json"}' ``` The full surface is **62 documented endpoints** — see the [REST API reference](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/notebooklm-rest-api). For overnight batches of 1 000+ questions, see the [batch pattern](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/batch-1000-questions). ### Option 2 — MCP Mode (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, VS Code…) One command finds the MCP clients installed on your machine and registers the server with each of them (Node ≥ 22 required): ```bash npx -y @roomi-fields/notebooklm-mcp setup ``` It covers Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini CLI, VS Code (Copilot) and Cline. It shows what it found and asks before changing anything, backs each config file up next to itself, never rewrites a file it cannot parse (it prints the snippet to paste instead), and keeps an existing `notebooklm` entry of yours unless you pass `--force`. `--dry-run` shows the changes without making them, `--client cursor,vscode` limits it to some clients, and `--remove` takes the entry out again. By hand, the entry every client expects is: ```json { "mcpServers": { "notebooklm": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@roomi-fields/notebooklm-mcp@latest"] } } } ``` From a clone instead, point the client at `node /path/to/gemini-notebook-mcp/dist/index.js` after `npm install && npm run build`. **Log in once — in a terminal, not through the assistant.** Run the interactive Google login as a command; a visible Chrome window opens, you sign in, and the saved session is then reused by the MCP server: ```bash npx -y -p @roomi-fields/notebooklm-mcp notebooklm-mcp-setup-auth # after `setup` above npm run setup-auth # from a clone ``` Do the login in a terminal rather than by asking the assistant _"log me in"_: some stdio MCP clients (e.g. Claude Desktop) cap tool-call duration and cut off the up-to-10-minute interactive login before you can finish signing in (see [issue #27](https://github.com/roomi-fields/gemini-notebook-mcp/issues/27)). ### Option 2b — MCP over HTTP (containers, remote clients) Clients that cannot spawn a local process — an AI in **another Docker container**, a hosted agent, a workflow runner — reach the **same MCP tools** over streamable HTTP. Start the HTTP server (Option 1) and point the client at `/mcp`: ```json { "mcpServers": { "notebooklm": { "type": "http", "url": "http://localhost:3000/mcp" } } } ``` Stateless, and behind the same auth as the REST API: set `NOTEBOOKLM_API_KEY` and the client sends `Authorization: Bearer `; leave it unset on a trusted container network and it works without one ([issue #42](https://github.com/roomi-fields/gemini-notebook-mcp/issues/42)). ### Option 3 — Docker (NAS, server, headless) ```bash # Build and run docker build -t notebooklm-mcp . export NOTEBOOKLM_API_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 32) docker run -d --name notebooklm-mcp -p 3000:3000 -p 127.0.0.1:6080:6080 \ -e NOTEBOOKLM_API_KEY -v notebooklm-data:/data notebooklm-mcp # Authenticate via noVNC (loopback only; from another machine: ssh -L 6080:localhost:6080 host) # 1. Open http://localhost:6080/vnc.html, password: docker logs notebooklm-mcp | grep Password # 2. Run: curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/setup-auth -H "Authorization: Bearer $NOTEBOOKLM_API_KEY" \ # -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"show_browser":true}' # 3. Login to Google in the VNC window ``` See [Docker Guide](./deployment/docs/08-DOCKER.md) for NAS deployment (Synology, QNAP). --- ## Documentation Full docs site: **** · [OpenAPI 3.1 name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  quality:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    strategy:
      matrix:
        node-version: [22.x, 24.x]

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Node.js ${{ matrix.node-version }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run ESLint
        run: npx eslint . --ext .ts,.tsx,.js,.jsx

      - name: Run TypeScript type check
        run: npx tsc --noEmit

      - name: Run Prettier check
        run: npx prettier --check "**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx,json,md}"

      - name: Run tests with coverage
        run: npm run test:ci

      - name: Run type coverage
        run: npx type-coverage --at-least 95

      # The published specification is what an AI client fetches and what a
      # code generator reads. Ours was invalid for months and nothing noticed:
      # three response descriptions contained an unquoted comma inside a flow
      # mapping, so YAML split them into a second, meaningless key and every
      # generator refused the document outright. Our own guards only ever
      # counted routes.
      - name: Validate the OpenAPI specification
        run: npx --yes @redocly/cli@1.34.3 lint deployment/docs/openapi.yaml --format=stylish

      # Bundled skills are published twice on purpose (standalone repo for
      # discovery + bundled copy so plugin installs ship them). Fail loudly if
      # the copies drift. One node version is enough — it is a network check.
      # Version strings and countable claims (endpoint count, Node floor) plus
      # doc coverage. These drifted silently for six releases and an AI answer
      # engine ended up quoting a stale figure back at a user.
      - name: Check versions and documented facts are in step with the code
        if: matrix.node-version == '22.x'
        run: |
          npm run version:check
          npm run facts:check
          npm run utcp:check

      - name: Check bundled skills match their canonical repos
        if: matrix.node-version == '22.x'
        run: npm run skill:check
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        if: matrix.node-version == '22.x'
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v4
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          files: ./coverage/lcov.info
          flags: unittests
          name: codecov-umbrella
          fail_ci_if_error: false
          verbose: true

  # The Rust client ships from this repository too, so it is held to the same
  # bar as the server: formatted, pedantic-clippy clean, and tested against a
  # stubbed server. It is a separate job because nothing it needs is in
  # node_modules.
  rust:
    name: Rust client
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install the toolchain
        run: rustup toolchain install stable --profile minimal --component rustfmt,clippy

      - name: Cache cargo
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            crates/notebooklm-client/target
          key: cargo-${{ hashFiles('crates/notebooklm-client/Cargo.toml') }}
          restore-keys: cargo-

      # The typed surface is generated from the specification. A hand edit
      # would be silently overwritten on the next release, so it fails here
      # instead.
      - name: Check the client matches the specification
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts && npm run rust:check

      - name: Check formatting
        working-directory: crates/notebooklm-client
        run: cargo fmt --check

      - name: Lint
        working-directory: crates/notebooklm-client
        run: cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings

      - name: Test
        working-directory: crates/notebooklm-client
        run: cargo test --all-features

      # A crate that cannot be packaged cannot be published, and finding that
      # out during a release is finding out too late.
      # No lock file is committed — it is a library, and a pinned lock would
      # only hide what a caller's own resolution does.
      - name: Check the package
        working-directory: crates/notebooklm-client
        run: cargo package

  # The Ruby gem ships from this repository too, and is held to the same bar:
  # its surface matches the specification, and it is tested against a stub
  # server built out of the standard library — the gem has no runtime
  # dependencies and its tests have none either.
  ruby:
    name: Ruby client
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install Ruby
        uses: ruby/setup-ruby@v1
        with:
          ruby-version: '3.1'

      # The surface is generated from the specification. A hand edit would be
      # silently overwritten on the next release, so it fails here instead.
      - name: Check the client matches the specification
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts && npm run ruby:check

      - name: Test
        working-directory: gems/notebooklm
        run: rake test

      # A gem that cannot be built cannot be published, and finding that out
      # during a release is finding out too late.
      - name: Check the package
        working-directory: gems/notebooklm
        run: gem build notebooklm.gemspec

  # The n8n community node ships from this repository too. n8n's verification
  # rules are strict about the package — the `n8n-community-node-package`
  # keyword, no runtime dependency, one service per package — so the package is
  # checked here rather than at submission time.
  n8n:
    name: n8n community node
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'

      # The node's surface is generated from the specification. A hand edit
      # would be silently overwritten on the next release, so it fails here
      # instead.
      - name: Check the node matches the specification
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts && npm run n8n:check

      - name: Build
        working-directory: nodes/n8n-nodes-gemini-notebook
        run: npm install && npm run build

      # A node n8n cannot load is a node nobody can install, and finding that
      # out during a release is finding out too late.
      - name: Check the package n8n will load
        working-directory: nodes/n8n-nodes-gemini-notebook
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          node -e "
            const assert = require('node:assert');
            const pkg = require('./package.json');
            assert(pkg.keywords.includes('n8n-community-node-package'), 'the community keyword is required');
            assert(pkg.name.startsWith('n8n-nodes-'), 'the package name must start with n8n-nodes-');
            assert(pkg.n8n.n8nNodesApiVersion === 1, 'n8nNodesApiVersion must be 1');
            assert(!pkg.dependencies, 'a verified node carries no runtime dependency');
            for (const f of [...pkg.n8n.nodes, ...pkg.n8n.credentials]) require('fs').accessSync(f);
            const { NotebookLm } = require('./dist/nodes/NotebookLm/NotebookLm.node.js');
            const node = new NotebookLm();
            const ops = node.description.properties.filter((p) => p.name === 'operation');
            const total = ops.reduce((n, p) => n + p.options.length, 0);
            assert.equal(total, 62, 'expected 62 operations, found ' + total);
            console.log('the node declares ' + total + ' operations across ' + ops.length + ' resources');
          "

      - name: Pack
        working-directory: nodes/n8n-nodes-gemini-notebook
        run: npm pack --dry-run

  security:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22.x'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run security audit (production deps only)
        # Same moderate bar, but advisories with no upstream fix must be named
        # and justified in the script rather than silently tolerated.
        run: node scripts/audit-check.mjs

FROM node:22-bookworm-slim

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    libnss3 libnspr4 libatk1.0-0 libatk-bridge2.0-0 libcups2 libdrm2 \
    libdbus-1-3 libxkbcommon0 libatspi2.0-0 libxcomposite1 libxdamage1 \
    libxfixes3 libxrandr2 libgbm1 libasound2 libpango-1.0-0 libcairo2 \
    xvfb x11vnc novnc websockify fluxbox \
    fonts-liberation fonts-noto-color-emoji wget ca-certificates procps \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

RUN groupadd -r notebooklm && useradd -r -g notebooklm -d /home/notebooklm notebooklm \
    && mkdir -p /home/notebooklm /app /data \
    && chown -R notebooklm:notebooklm /home/notebooklm /app /data \
    && mkdir -p /tmp/.X11-unix \
    && chmod 1777 /tmp/.X11-unix

WORKDIR /app

# Copier package files
COPY --chown=notebooklm:notebooklm package*.json ./

USER notebooklm

# Installer TOUTES les dépendances (avec devDependencies pour TypeScript)
RUN npm ci --ignore-scripts

# Copier les sources AVANT de builder
COPY --chown=notebooklm:notebooklm src/ ./src/
COPY --chown=notebooklm:notebooklm tsconfig*.json ./

# Builder
RUN npm run build

# Copier scripts
COPY --chown=notebooklm:notebooklm scripts/ ./scripts/

# Supprimer les devDependencies après le build
RUN npm prune --omit=dev

# Installer le browser
RUN npx patchright install chromium

USER root
RUN chmod +x /app/scripts/*.sh
USER notebooklm

ENV NODE_ENV=production \
    HTTP_PORT=3000 \
    HTTP_HOST=0.0.0.0 \
    HEADLESS=true \
    NOTEBOOKLM_DATA_DIR=/data \
    PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/home/notebooklm/.cache/ms-playwright \
    DISPLAY=:99 \
    NOVNC_PORT=6080

EXPOSE 3000 6080

HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=10s --start-period=10s --retries=3 \
    CMD wget --no-verbose --tries=1 --spider http://localhost:3000/health || exit 1

VOLUME ["/data"]

CMD ["/app/scripts/docker-entrypoint.sh"]

sampled_files.README.md:
# NotebookLM REST API + MCP server **Automate Google Gemini Notebook — formerly, and still widely known as, NotebookLM — at scale. 62-endpoint HTTP REST API for n8n / Zapier / Make / curl, an MCP server for Claude Code / Cursor / Codex, a UTCP interface for clients that call the API natively, and Rust and Ruby clients. Citation-backed Q&A, full Studio generation (audio · video · infographic · report · presentation · data table), multi-account rotation with auto-reauth across personal and Google Workspace accounts.** > v4.12.0 — **Node 22 is now the floor, and the last four open advisories are gone with it.** The declared floor of Node 18 had quietly become fiction: three production dependencies already required Node 20 or newer, and the test matrix kept passing on 18 without exercising them. Raising it also let the third-party file globber go — its dependency chain carried four advisories with no fix upstream — replaced by Node's built-in search, now actually under test. Builds on **4.0.0**, where the HTTP API stopped being open to the network and to any web page ([GHSA-p69m-c5rf-g2c3](https://github.com/roomi-fields/gemini-notebook-mcp/security/advisories/GHSA-p69m-c5rf-g2c3)): it binds loopback, refuses unlisted origins, and takes a bearer token — **remote access and Docker require `NOTEBOOKLM_API_KEY`**, see [Securing the HTTP API](./deployment/docs/15-SECURITY.md). Built on a **dual transport** — the internal `batchexecute` RPC API (10-100× faster than scraping, immune to UI rebrands) with the Playwright browser as an automatic fallback. See the [changelog](./CHANGELOG.md). > **Note (July 2026):** Google rebranded **NotebookLM** to **Gemini Notebook**. It is the same product, existing links redirect, and this project drives the same underlying service — the browser path was updated for the new DOM in v2.3.0 and the RPC path in v3.0.0. Package and repository keep the `notebooklm` name. --- > **Unofficial project — good to know before you start** > > This is not affiliated with Google. It talks to the same `batchexecute` > endpoints the NotebookLM web app uses, with a browser fallback when they move. > They are undocumented, so they can change without notice — when that happens we > ship a fix, as we have for every change so far. > > Two practical notes: use a **dedicated Google account** for automation, and > expect NotebookLM's own quotas to apply at high volume. See > [Disclaimer](#disclaimer) for the full text. --- ## What You Can Build 🔗 **No-code automation pipelines** — The 62-endpoint REST API means NotebookLM becomes a step in n8n, Zapier, Make, or a plain `curl` in cron. No agent, no MCP client, no Node in your stack — just HTTP. This is the half most NotebookLM libraries don't have. 🤖 **Agent tooling** — The same engine over MCP for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex, with a bundled skill that primes the agent on citation formats, the daily-quota-aware batch pattern, and transport selection. 📚 **Research at volume** — Multi-account rotation with automatic re-authentication, built for overnight runs of 1 000+ questions across several notebooks without babysitting. 🎙️ **Full Studio generation** — Audio overviews, video, infographics, reports, presentations, data tables, plus flashcards, quizzes and mind maps — generated and downloaded programmatically. ## Use Cases & Recipes NotebookLM is a **grounded** engine: Gemini reads your sources and answers _from them_, with citations. The winning pattern is to let it do the expensive reading while your own stack handles orchestration and the last mile. **Spend fewer tokens — offload the reading** - **🪙 Zero-token synthesis layer** — Drop 30 documents in a notebook, let Gemini do the heavy analysis, and spend your agent's context only on the final polish. The reasoning happens server-side; your agent just orchestrates (`add_notebook` → `source_add` → `notebook_ask`). - **💾 Answer cache you can re-read offline** — `vault_batch` writes every answer to disk as structured JSON against a published [schema](https://schemas.roomi-fields.com/nblm-answer-v1.json), so a batch run becomes a corpus you can grep, diff, re-index, or feed to a retrieval layer — without re-querying and re-spending quota. **Wire it into things that aren't agents** - **⚙️ NotebookLM as an n8n / Zapier / Make step** — Because it speaks plain HTTP, a citation-backed answer becomes one node in a workflow: a form submission triggers a question, the cited answer lands in a sheet, a Slack message, or a database. No agent runtime involved. - **📄 Document intake pipeline** — Watch a folder or an inbox, push new PDFs and URLs in as sources, and ask a standing set of questions against them on every arrival. **Grounded answers with a paper trail** - **🔍 Citations with the actual source text** — Answers come back with source names _and the quoted excerpts_ they rest on, extracted from the citation panel — so a claim can be checked, not just attributed. - **🎓 Literature review at thesis scale** — Batch 100+ research questions across multiple notebooks, rotate accounts as daily quotas run out, and resume where it stopped. Built for, and tested on, exactly this. **Get artifacts back out** - **🔁 One source set, every format** — Fan a single notebook out to a podcast, a video, a slide deck, a report, a quiz and a mind map, then download them all locally. --- ## In the Wild Real deployments, not hypotheticals. - **📚 A doctoral literature review at batch scale** — The project was built for, and is continuously tested on, overnight runs of **1 000+ research questions** spread across several notebooks: multi-account rotation picks up when a daily quota runs out, every answer is written to disk with its citations, and an interrupted run resumes instead of starting over. The batch pattern in [`vault_batch`](#features) exists because a thesis needed it. - **🔌 Replacing a RAG engine with the REST API** — [`musnymubarak/Calim_Doc`](https://github.com/musnymubarak/Calim_Doc) swapped a Gemini-based retrieval engine for this project's HTTP API, running it as a Docker service (`notebooklm:3000`) behind a full client and worker layer. A good illustration of the REST half: no agent runtime, no MCP client — NotebookLM simply became a backend service their Python app calls. Built something with it? Open an issue — this section is for other people's work. ## Features ### Q&A with Citations - **Ask questions** to NotebookLM and get accurate, citation-backed answers - **Source citation extraction** with 5 formats: none, inline, footnotes, json, expanded (97% excerpt success rate) - **Session management** for multi-turn conversations with auto-reauth on session expiry ### Content Generation Generate multiple content types from your notebook sources: | Content Type | Formats | Options | | ------------------ | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- | | **Audio Overview** | Podcast-style discussion | Language (80+), custom instructions | | **Video** | Brief, Explainer | 6 visual styles, language, custom instructions | | **Infographic** | Horizontal, Vertical | Language, custom instructions | | **Report** | Summary, Detailed | Language, custom instructions | | **Presentation** | Overview, Detailed | Language, custom instructions | | **Data Table** | Simple, Detailed | Language, custom instructions | | **Flashcards** | Study cards | Language, custom instructions | | **Quiz** | Assessment questions | Language, custom instructions | | **Mind Map** | Interactive node graph | Saved to the notebook | **Video Visual Styles**: classroom, documentary, animated, corporate, cinematic, minimalist **Language of generated content**: pass `language` to any generator — a BCP-47 code (`es`, `ja`, `pt_BR`, `zh_Hans`) or a name in English or in the language itself (`"Spanish"`, `"Español"`). 81 languages are accepted, and an unrecognised one is refused rather than quietly swapped for another. Set a default with `NOTEBOOKLM_CONTENT_LANGUAGE`; it is deliberately independent of `NOTEBOOKLM_UI_LOCALE`, which only picks the interface language the browser fallback reads. Flashcards and quizzes are generated via `generate_study_aid`; mind maps via `generate_mind_map`. v3 also adds `share_notebook`, `manage_labels`, and `research_sources` (web/Drive source discovery) — see the [changelog](./CHANGELOG.md). ### Content Download - **Download Audio** — WAV audio files - **Download Video** — MP4 video files - **Download Infographic** — PNG image files - Text-based content (report, presentation, data_table) is returned in the API response - **Delete generated content** (`content_delete`) — until now a notebook accumulated every draft anyone ever asked for, with no way to remove one short of the web UI ### Source Management - **Add sources**: Files (PDF, TXT, DOCX, audio, images), URLs, Text, YouTube videos, Google Drive - **List sources**: Every source with its ID and title (`source_list`) - **Rename a source** (`rename_source`): fix a title in place, by id or by name - **Check freshness** (`check_source_freshness`): which URL / Drive sources have drifted from what they point at — the whole notebook in one call. An unanswered source is reported as unknown, never as current - **Read a source's guide** (`get_source_guide`): NotebookLM's own summary and key topics for one source - **Read a source in full** (`source_read`): the exact text NotebookLM indexed — what it actually reasons over, which the web UI only shows in fragments. Quote a source verbatim, check what a PDF really yielded, or hand the raw material to another tool. Name the source instead of its ID if you prefer; an ambiguous name is refused rather than guessed. Long sources arrive **one page at a time**, with an explicit instruction for fetching the next — or `paginate: false` for the whole document at once. ### Notebook Summary and Chat History - **What is in this notebook?** (`get_notebook_summary`) — NotebookLM's own summary of its sources plus the questions it suggests asking, without spending a question to find out - **What was already asked?** (`get_chat_history`) — read back the recorded questions and answers, newest first. An agent resuming work stops paying to ask what it already asked. NotebookLM exposes only the most recent conversation per notebook - **Clear the history** (`delete_chat_history`) — the web UI's "Delete history". There is no per-turn delete: the whole conversation goes ### Artifact Export and Revision - **Export to Drive** (`export_artifact`) — send a finished artifact to Google Docs or Google Sheets - **Revise one slide** (`revise_slide`) — change a single slide from a prompt instead of regenerating the whole deck ### Notebook Library - **Multi-notebook management** with validation and smart selection - **Auto-discovery**: Automatically generate metadata via NotebookLM queries - **Search notebooks** by keyword in name, description, or topics - **Scrape notebooks**: List all notebooks from NotebookLM with IDs and names - **Bulk delete**: Delete multiple notebooks at once ### Accounts & Localization - **Personal _and_ Google Workspace accounts** — recognizes both NotebookLM hosts (`notebooklm.google.com` and the `notebook.google.com` Workspace alias), so Workspace sessions authenticate cleanly instead of looping on "session expired" - **UI-language-aware** — drives NotebookLM whether its interface is in English, French, German, or Japanese (`en` · `fr` · `de` · `ja`); [add a language](./docs/ADDING_A_LANGUAGE.md) in a single JSON file ### UTCP Interface [UTCP](https://www.utcp.io/) — the Universal Tool Calling Protocol — is the inverse of MCP: **there is no protocol server and no wrapper process**. A client reads a tool manual once, then calls this REST API directly, so nothing sits between the agent and the endpoint. ```bash # The manual. 56 tools, named the same as the MCP tools. curl -H "X-API-Key: $NOTEBOOKLM_API_KEY" http://localhost:3000/utcp ``` - **`GET /utcp`** — the manual for a running server, with every call address rebased on the address the request arrived at, so one document serves a loopback install and a reverse-proxied one alike. - **Also published statically** at [notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/utcp.json](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/utcp.json), for a client configured before the server is up. - **62 named tools** — the manual reuses the MCP tool names, so `search_passages` is `search_passages` on both sides rather than something synthesised from a URL path. Every operation in the [OpenAPI 3.1 spec](./deployment/docs/openapi.yaml) carries a matching `operationId`, which also means a client pointed straight at the specification converts it correctly on its own. - **Authentication is declared the way UTCP clients implement it** — as an `api_key` in the `X-API-Key` header, which this server accepts alongside the bearer form. The key itself is never in the manual, only the literal `${NOTEBOOKLM_API_KEY}`, which is how a client asks for a value from its own environment. (A client that converts the specification instead will not pick up authentication at all, since the converter does not map bearer schemes — one reason to prefer the manual.) Generated from the specification on every release and held in step by a build guard, so the manual cannot describe a version that is not the one you are running. Details: [REST API reference → `GET /utcp`](./deployment/docs/03-API.md). ### Rust client A typed async client lives in this repository at [`crates/notebooklm-client`](./crates/notebooklm-client) and is published as [**`notebooklm`**](https://crates.io/crates/notebooklm) on crates.io ([docs](https://docs.rs/notebooklm)), one version per release. It covers **all 62 operations** — generated from the specification, with a synchronous twin behind one feature flag. ```rust let client = notebooklm::Client::local()?; let answer = client.ask_question(&AskRequest::new(&id, "What is ikigai?")).await?; println!("{}", answer.answer); ``` It deliberately **does not own a browser**: the Google session is bound to the machine it was made on, expires server-side while local cookies still look valid, and needs a driver kept patched against detection. The crate talks to this server, which already does all three. The reasoning in full: [driving it from Rust](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/blog/notebooklm-rust). ### Ruby client The same surface as a gem, in this repository at [`gems/notebooklm`](./gems/notebooklm) and published as [**`notebooklm`**](https://rubygems.org/gems/notebooklm) on RubyGems, also one version per release. All 62 operations, generated from the same specification, every response shape documented field by field — and no runtime dependencies. ```ruby client = NotebookLM.local answer = client.ask(notebook.id, 'What is ikigai?') answer.citations.each { |c| puts "[#{c.number}] #{c.source_text}" } ``` Why a gem at all, and why it owns no browser either: [driving it from Ruby](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/blog/notebooklm-ruby). ### Integration Options - **MCP Protocol** — Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, any MCP client - **[UTCP](https://www.utcp.io/)** — a tool manual at `/utcp`, for clients that call the REST API natively with no protocol server in between ([see above](#utcp-interface)) - **Agent Skill** — ships a bundled [`notebooklm` skill](./skills/notebooklm/SKILL.md) (also standalone: [`roomi-fields/notebooklm-skill`](https://github.com/roomi-fields/notebooklm-skill)) that teaches the agent citation formats, the batch-to-cache pattern, and when to use which transport - **HTTP REST API** — n8n, Zapier, Make.com, custom integrations - **Docker** — Isolated deployment with Docker or Docker Compose - **[RTFM](https://github.com/roomi-fields/rtfm) retrieval layer** — `/batch-to-vault` writes citation-backed answers as markdown + JSON sidecars (`nblm-answer-v1` schema), indexable by [RTFM](https://github.com/roomi-fields/rtfm) (FTS5 + semantic) for unlimited offline queries. Ideal for academic / SOTA workflows. [Guide](./deployment/docs/14-RTFM-INTEGRATION.md). --- ## Quick Start ### Option 0 — Claude Code marketplace (one-liner, recommended for Claude Code users) The fastest way to get NotebookLM into Claude Code. Distributed via the [`roomi-fields/claude-plugins`](https://github.com/roomi-fields/claude-plugins) marketplace alongside [RTFM](https://github.com/roomi-fields/rtfm) (the retrieval companion — see [RTFM integration guide](./deployment/docs/14-RTFM-INTEGRATION.md)): ```text /plugin marketplace add roomi-fields/claude-plugins /plugin install notebooklm@roomi-fields ``` That registers the MCP server **and the `notebooklm` agent skill**, runs `npx -y @roomi-fields/notebooklm-mcp@` automatically (Node ≥ 22 required), and lets you upgrade with two commands when a new release ships: `/plugin marketplace update roomi-fields` then `/reload-plugins`. Then run `npx -y -p @roomi-fields/notebooklm-mcp notebooklm-mcp-setup-auth` once in a terminal to log into Google (a visible Chrome opens). To install RTFM at the same time: `/plugin install rtfm@roomi-fields`. ### Option 1 — HTTP REST API (n8n, Zapier, Make, curl, any HTTP client) ```bash git clone https://github.com/roomi-fields/gemini-notebook-mcp.git cd gemini-notebook-mcp npm install && npm run build npm run setup-auth # One-time Google login npm run start:http # Start REST API on port 3000 ``` ```bash # Citation-backed Q&A, single curl, JSON response curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/ask \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"question": "Summarize chapter 3", "notebook_id": "your-id", "source_format": "json"}' ``` The full surface is **62 documented endpoints** — see the [REST API reference](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/notebooklm-rest-api). For overnight batches of 1 000+ questions, see the [batch pattern](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/batch-1000-questions). ### Option 2 — MCP Mode (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, VS Code…) One command finds the MCP clients installed on your machine and registers the server with each of them (Node ≥ 22 required): ```bash npx -y @roomi-fields/notebooklm-mcp setup ``` It covers Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini CLI, VS Code (Copilot) and Cline. It shows what it found and asks before changing anything, backs each config file up next to itself, never rewrites a file it cannot parse (it prints the snippet to paste instead), and keeps an existing `notebooklm` entry of yours unless you pass `--force`. `--dry-run` shows the changes without making them, `--client cursor,vscode` limits it to some clients, and `--remove` takes the entry out again. By hand, the entry every client expects is: ```json { "mcpServers": { "notebooklm": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@roomi-fields/notebooklm-mcp@latest"] } } } ``` From a clone instead, point the client at `node /path/to/gemini-notebook-mcp/dist/index.js` after `npm install && npm run build`. **Log in once — in a terminal, not through the assistant.** Run the interactive Google login as a command; a visible Chrome window opens, you sign in, and the saved session is then reused by the MCP server: ```bash npx -y -p @roomi-fields/notebooklm-mcp notebooklm-mcp-setup-auth # after `setup` above npm run setup-auth # from a clone ``` Do the login in a terminal rather than by asking the assistant _"log me in"_: some stdio MCP clients (e.g. Claude Desktop) cap tool-call duration and cut off the up-to-10-minute interactive login before you can finish signing in (see [issue #27](https://github.com/roomi-fields/gemini-notebook-mcp/issues/27)). ### Option 2b — MCP over HTTP (containers, remote clients) Clients that cannot spawn a local process — an AI in **another Docker container**, a hosted agent, a workflow runner — reach the **same MCP tools** over streamable HTTP. Start the HTTP server (Option 1) and point the client at `/mcp`: ```json { "mcpServers": { "notebooklm": { "type": "http", "url": "http://localhost:3000/mcp" } } } ``` Stateless, and behind the same auth as the REST API: set `NOTEBOOKLM_API_KEY` and the client sends `Authorization: Bearer `; leave it unset on a trusted container network and it works without one ([issue #42](https://github.com/roomi-fields/gemini-notebook-mcp/issues/42)). ### Option 3 — Docker (NAS, server, headless) ```bash # Build and run docker build -t notebooklm-mcp . export NOTEBOOKLM_API_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 32) docker run -d --name notebooklm-mcp -p 3000:3000 -p 127.0.0.1:6080:6080 \ -e NOTEBOOKLM_API_KEY -v notebooklm-data:/data notebooklm-mcp # Authenticate via noVNC (loopback only; from another machine: ssh -L 6080:localhost:6080 host) # 1. Open http://localhost:6080/vnc.html, password: docker logs notebooklm-mcp | grep Password # 2. Run: curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/setup-auth -H "Authorization: Bearer $NOTEBOOKLM_API_KEY" \ # -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"show_browser":true}' # 3. Login to Google in the VNC window ``` See [Docker Guide](./deployment/docs/08-DOCKER.md) for NAS deployment (Synology, QNAP). --- ## Documentation Full docs site: **** · [OpenAPI 3.1 See [ROADMAP.md](./ROADMAP.md) for planned features and version history. **Latest releases:** - **v4.12.0** (2026-11-28) — One command registers the server with your MCP clients - **v4.11.2** notes (create, delete, and convert are implemented) --- ## Disclaimer This tool automates browser interactions with NotebookLM. # NotebookLM MCP Server - Docker Compose Configuration
#
# Start:   docker-compose up -d
# Stop:    docker-compose down
# Logs:    docker-compose logs -f
# Rebuild: docker-compose build --no-cache

version: '3.8'

services:
  notebooklm-mcp:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    image: notebooklm-mcp:latest
    container_name: notebooklm-mcp

    # Port mapping
    ports:
      - '${HTTP_PORT:-3000}:3000'
      # noVNC shows the browser signed in to your Google account: loopback only.
      # From another machine, use an SSH tunnel (ssh -L 6080:localhost:6080 host).
      - '127.0.0.1:6080:6080' # noVNC web interface for visual auth (password in the logs)

    # Persistent data storage
    volumes:
      # Main data directory (cookies, library, accounts, browser state)
      # Using local directory with existing auth data
      - ./deploy-package/data:/data
      # Optional: mount local library.json for development
      # - ./library.json:/data/library.json:ro

    # Environment configuration
    environment:
      # Server settings
      - NODE_ENV=production
      - HTTP_PORT=3000
      - HTTP_HOST=0.0.0.0

      # Browser settings
      - HEADLESS=true
      - STEALTH_ENABLED=true

      # Data directory (inside container)
      - DATA_DIR=/data

      # Optional: NotebookLM URL (if you have a default notebook)
      # - NOTEBOOKLM_URL=https://notebooklm.google.com/notebook/YOUR_NOTEBOOK_ID

      # Optional: UI locale (fr or en)
      - NOTEBOOKLM_UI_LOCALE=fr

      # Optional: Auto-login settings
      # - AUTO_LOGIN_ENABLED=true
      # - AUTO_LOGIN_TIMEOUT_MS=120000

    # Resource limits
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 2G
        reservations:
          memory: 512M

    # Restart policy
    restart: unless-stopped

    # Health check
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD', 'wget', '--no-verbose', '--tries=1', '--spider', 'http://localhost:3000/health']
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

    # Logging
    logging:
      driver: 'json-file'
      options:
        max-size: '10m'
        max-file: '3'

# Named volumes for persistence
volumes:
  notebooklm-data:
    name: notebooklm-mcp-data
