repository.readme:
# Kurlo **The open-source API client with an agent inside and your secret managers built in.**
Bring any model, Claude Code or Codex, and link variables to Vault, 1Password or your cloud. No account, no paid plan, no telemetry. Collections live as YAML in your Git repo. [![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/stormhop/kurlo)](https://github.com/stormhop/kurlo/releases/latest) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/stormhop/kurlo?style=flat)](https://github.com/stormhop/kurlo/stargazers) [![CI](https://github.com/stormhop/kurlo/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/stormhop/kurlo/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![Platforms](https://img.shields.io/badge/platforms-macOS%20%7C%20Windows%20%7C%20Linux-lightgrey)](https://github.com/stormhop/kurlo/releases/latest) **[Download](https://github.com/stormhop/kurlo/releases/latest)** · [Website](https://kurlo.dev/) · [Docs](https://kurlo.dev/docs/getting-started/installation/) · [Secret managers](https://kurlo.dev/docs/guides/environments/secret-managers/) · [Agent mode](https://kurlo.dev/agent/) · [MCP server](https://kurlo.dev/mcp/) · [Compare](https://kurlo.dev/vs/postman/)
## New in 3.2: Secret managers Link an environment variable to HashiCorp Vault or OpenBao, 1Password, AWS Secrets Manager or Parameter Store, Google Secret Manager, Azure Key Vault, Bitwarden Secrets Manager, Doppler, Infisical, KeePassXC, a command of your own or the environment of the Kurlo process. The environment file in Git keeps only the reference, and each teammate signs in with their own token, AWS profile or CLI. Kurlo fetches the value when a request is sent and shows `[secret]` in responses, history, script logs, `kurlo run` reports and everything an agent sees. Paste an ARN, an `op://` link, an Azure secret URL or a Vault path to fill in the link, or browse the provider's paths. A workspace you clone uses a provider only after you trust it on your machine. All twelve providers are free; Bruno sells cloud vaults in its Ultimate plan and Postman in Enterprise with a security add-on. ```yaml - key: dbPassword secretRef: provider: vault-prod path: secret/data/orders field: password ``` In CI, `kurlo run` fetches the same links with the runner's credentials before the first request and stops with exit code 2 naming any variable it could not get. [Secret managers guide](https://kurlo.dev/docs/guides/environments/secret-managers/) ## Agent mode Ask in plain words and the agent runs your requests and collections, explains why a call failed, writes requests and tests and imports your specs, right inside Kurlo. Pick the Kurlo agent on your own model (OpenRouter, an API key, Ollama or LM Studio), or connect the Claude Code or Codex you already use. Every change and every call other than `GET`, `HEAD` or `OPTIONS` waits for your approval, and the model never sees your secrets. ![The Kurlo agent reads a collection, runs the requests, and asks before adding tests to four of them](.github/assets/agent-mode.gif) [Agent mode on kurlo.dev](https://kurlo.dev/agent/) · [Agent guide](https://kurlo.dev/docs/guides/agent/) ## Why Kurlo - **Secrets from where they already live.** Link variables to Vault, 1Password, AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, Bitwarden, Doppler, Infisical or KeePassXC. Git gets the reference, your API gets the value, and the screen, logs and agents get `[secret]`. - **An agent that asks first.** The Kurlo agent, Claude Code or Codex works on your collections inside the app. It shows every change before it is written, can follow a plan you approve and work on its own Git branch, and keeps chats on your machine. - **Free for a team of any size.** There is no paid plan to grow into and no account to create. A team shares a workspace through any Git host, and every request is a readable YAML file that gets reviewed in the same pull request as the API change. - **Your Postman collections keep working.** Import a Postman, Insomnia, Bruno, OpenAPI, WSDL or HAR file. `pm.test`, `pm.expect` with chai, `pm.sendRequest` and `require('lodash')` run as they were written. - **Share an API reference.** Turn a collection into a searchable HTML file with saved requests and responses. Open it offline or publish it to a static host. - **Or drive it from your terminal.** `kurlo mcp` lets Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and any other MCP client run your saved requests with their auth and tests, write new requests and tests, and explain why the last call failed. Secrets are sent to the API but never shown to the model. - **Small and native.** Built with Go and the system WebView instead of Electron, so the macOS download is 26.8 MB and the Linux one is 14.1 MB. | | Kurlo | Postman | Insomnia | Bruno | |------------------------------|--------------------------------|-------------------------------|------------------------|----------------------------| | Free plan | ✅ Every feature, any team size | 1 user | Up to 3 Git Sync users | Private Git hosts need Pro | | Account needed | ✅ No | For collections | Beyond Scratch Pad | No | | Collections in your Git repo | ✅ | Native Git in the desktop app | ✅ | ✅ | | Postman `pm.*` scripts | ✅ Run as written | Native | Compatibility layer | Converted to `bru.*` | | Mock server | ✅ Local, no cap | Cloud, needs an account | 1,000 requests/mo free | ✅ Local | | MCP | ✅ Client and server | Client | Client | Community servers | Checked against vendor pricing pages on 15 October 2026. Details and sources: [vs Postman](https://kurlo.dev/vs/postman/), [vs Insomnia](https://kurlo.dev/vs/insomnia/), [vs Bruno](https://kurlo.dev/vs/bruno/). If Kurlo saves you time, a ⭐ helps other people find it. --- ## Download Grab the latest build from the [releases page](https://github.com/stormhop/kurlo/releases/latest). | Platform | Installer | |---------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------| | macOS 15 Sequoia or later (Apple Silicon + Intel) | `.dmg` | | Windows 10/11 (x64, arm64) | `.exe` (NSIS installer), `.msix` | | Linux (x64) | `.AppImage` | Every release ships SHA256 checksums and minisign signatures, and the in-app updater refuses any binary that fails either check. The command line (`kurlo run` for CI, `kurlo mcp` for AI agents) is also on npm as [ `@kurlo/cli`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@kurlo/cli), with prebuilt binaries for macOS, Linux and Windows on x64 and arm64. It does not need the desktop app: ```bash npx -y @kurlo/cli --version ``` Guides, the scripting reference, and the YAML workspace format live in the **[documentation site](https://kurlo.dev/)**. --- ## Features **Requests** - All HTTP methods: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS - Query params, headers, body (JSON, form-data, x-www-form-urlencoded, raw text/XML/HTML, binary file) - cURL import — paste a curl command into the URL field, it parses automatically - Bulk edit for params, headers and form fields — switch the table to a `key: value` text area and back - Suggestions while you type — the rest of a URL from history and saved requests, and the next JSON key from saved examples - Build GraphQL operations from a schema, select nested fields and bind typed variables in the query editor - Run GraphQL subscriptions over WebSocket with the `graphql-ws` protocol (and the older `subscriptions-transport-ws`), with a connection payload and a live event log - MQTT 3.1, 3.1.1 and 5 requests over TCP, TLS and WebSocket: subscriptions with wildcards and QoS, publishing with properties, last will and a live message log - Kafka producer and consumer requests with topic discovery, live records, partition offsets, TLS and SASL. - GraphQL, Server-Sent Events, WebSocket, Socket.IO, gRPC, and MCP request types — an MCP call discovers the server's tools, resources and prompts, seeds the arguments from the tool's schema, and shows the raw JSON-RPC exchange - Import Postman v2 JSON or v3 Native Git folders, Insomnia v4, Bruno/OpenCollection, OpenAPI/Swagger, HAR, cURL, and all-data backups - WSDL import — a SOAP 1.1 or 1.2 request with a sample envelope for every operation, from a file or a `?wsdl` link - OpenAPI/Swagger imports from a link as well as a file — paste the spec URL and Kurlo fetches it and builds the collection - OpenAPI sync — keep a collection linked to its spec URL or file, review new, changed and removed endpoints with a three-way merge that keeps your edits, with no monthly limit; `kurlo openapi check` flags drift in CI - Export Postman v2.1 JSON, Postman v3 folders with native gRPC, Insomnia v4, OpenAPI/Swagger, OpenCollection YAML, and all-data backups **Authentication** - Bearer Token - Basic Auth - NTLM (NTLMv2) - Digest Auth — MD5, SHA-256 and SHA-512-256 plus their `-sess` variants, with `qop=auth` and `auth-int` - API Key — in header or query string - JWT Bearer — signed on every send from a secret or a private key (HS, RS, PS and ES algorithms), with claims, an optional lifetime and a token preview - OAuth 2.0 — Client Credentials, Authorization Code (with PKCE), Password, and Device Code grants; loopback browser sign-in, refresh tokens, and automatic token refresh before each send - AWS Signature v4 - Client certificates (mutual TLS), per request or inherited from a collection - Per-request and collection defaults with inheritance **Scripting** — write sandboxed JavaScript in requests, folders and collections. The editor completes `pm.*` methods, variable keys and saved request names, with signatures and examples. ```js // pre-request: inject a header pm.request.headers.set("X-Client", "kurlo") // pre-request: rewrite and sign the body pm.request.body.update(JSON.stringify({...pm.request.body.json(), nonce: pm.crypto.randomHex(8)})) // test: assert status and shape pm.test("status is 200", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200)) pm.test("has an id", () => pm.response.to.have.jsonSchema({type: "object", required: ["id"]})) ``` **Assertions** — check the status, response time, size, a header or a JSON field without code (`status equals 201`, `body.items has length 3`); they run in the app, the collection runner, `kurlo run` and `kurlo mcp`. `require` resolves bundled stand-ins for `lodash`, `ajv`, `tv4`, `uuid`, `crypto-js`, and `chai`, so imported Postman scripts keep working. `pm.sendRequest` makes an HTTP call from a script, and `pm.execution.skipRequest()` skips the send. **Environments & Variables** - Multiple environments per workspace, switch with one click - Environments inherit the variables they do not set from another environment, such as Staging from Base - Matrix view — every variable as a row, every environment as a column, edited in place - `{{variable}}` template syntax in URLs, headers, params, body, auth fields - Set variables from test scripts (`pm.variables.set`, `pm.environment.set`) - Secret managers — link a variable to Vault/OpenBao, 1Password, AWS Secrets Manager and Parameter Store, Google Secret Manager, Azure Key Vault, Bitwarden, Doppler, Infisical, KeePassXC, a command or process env vars, or import every key of one secret; `{{vault:name}}` and `await pm.vault.get()` work as in Postman - Manual-save and autosave modes both cover request and environment edits **Workspaces & Collections** - Multiple workspaces for separate projects or clients - Collections with nested folder hierarchy and empty-folder preservation - Folder defaults — headers, auth, scripts and tests on a folder apply to every request inside it - Drag-and-drop organisation - Request history — every send on its own page, request and stored response side by side, reopenable in the editor ( 14-day retention, 1000 entries) - [Static API documentation](https://kurlo.dev/docs/guides/cli-runner/docs/) — build a standalone HTML reference with `kurlo docs build` or **Build documentation** in the collection menu - Collection runner — sequential or parallel, data files, iterations, an HTML report, and the last run of every collection kept - [Load testing with k6](https://kurlo.dev/docs/guides/load-testing/) — collection flows with extraction and checks, virtual users or iteration rates, thresholds, CSV/JSON data, script export, local runs and last-run reports - Git-backed YAML workspaces with diagnostics, conflict helpers, and local-only secrets; branch, commit, pull, push and open a pull request from the app - Edit a request's YAML file in the File tab with completion, schema checks, Beautify and protected identity fields; the address bar edits the same draft - **CLI runner** — `npx -y @kurlo/cli run ./workspace --env CI` executes requests and their test scripts for CI, with data-driven iterations (`--data`), pretty/JSON/JUnit reporters, variable export, and a non-zero exit code on failure. `kurlo load list|export|run` lists collection load tests, exports k6 scripts or runs local k6 with threshold results and reports **Agent mode** — since 3.0. Pick the Kurlo agent on your own model (OpenRouter, an API key, or Ollama and LM Studio), or connect the Claude Code and Codex CLIs you already use with their own accounts, and ask in plain words. The agent runs requests and collections, explains failures, writes requests and tests, imports OpenAPI, Postman and HAR files, and reads a connected project folder. It asks before every change and every call other than `GET`, `HEAD` or `OPTIONS`, can follow a plan you approve, work on its own Git branch and call your own MCP servers. Trusted hosts and sandbox environments run without asking, protected environments are off limits, and secrets reach the API while the model sees `[secret]`. Chats stay encrypted on your machine, and **Activity** lists every tool call with the files it changed and a way to restore them. See the [agent guide](https://kurlo.dev/docs/guides/agent/). **AI agents (MCP server)** — the Kurlo binary is also a Model Context Protocol server, so Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Claude Desktop or any other MCP client can list your collections and environments, run saved HTTP, GraphQL, unary gRPC, MCP and AI requests, run collections with CSV or JSON data, and send one-off calls with your `{{variables}}`. It can start and compare k6 runs and serve saved examples from a local mock. In the desktop app, Agent Mode can also exchange messages on live connections. It can also keep the workspace up to date: add and change requests with their `pm.*` tests, save responses as examples and set environment variables, in the same YAML the app writes, never storing a secret. It can preview and apply imports, read a connected project folder, edit Markdown docs and generate snippets. It reads the last request you sent from the app, so "why did that fail?" needs no copying. Secret values are sent to the API but masked as `[secret]` in everything the model sees, and environments you mark protected are off limits. One command sets up every client on the machine: ![Claude Code adds tests to a Kurlo collection over MCP, finds a pricing bug and fixes it, while the tests appear in Kurlo](.github/assets/demo.gif) ```bash npx -y @kurlo/cli mcp install --env Staging ``` Add `--project` to write a repository's shared `.mcp.json` and `.cursor/mcp.json` instead, so the whole team gets the server by cloning. Manual setup, the tools and the flags are covered in the [MCP server guide](https://kurlo.dev/docs/guides/mcp-server/). **Response examples** — save any response as a named example on its request: the status, headers and body it came back with, alongside the request that produced it. Secrets are redacted on capture, a clean body is stored byte for byte, and examples are read from Postman, OpenCollection, HAR and OpenAPI and included in Postman v2.1 and OpenCollection exports. A response can be diffed against an example instead of against the previous send. **Cookies** — a per-workspace cookie jar with a per-domain editor, disableable per request. - **Cookie sync**: pair Kurlo with the in-repo browser extension (`apps/desktop/extension`, Chromium + Firefox) and the session you already have in the browser is the session Kurlo sends with. A loopback-only bridge that stays off until you turn it on, an approval you give in Kurlo by matching a six-digit code, and a per-domain allowlist enforced on both sides. Cookies travel one way: browser into Kurlo. **Mock server** — serve a collection's saved examples over HTTP on a local port, so a client can be built against an endpoint that does not exist yet. Routing is by method and the example's path template (`/orders/:id`), a recorded query narrows which example answers, and a live log shows what the client asked for and which example replied. Loopback only; CORS preflight is answered for any origin. **Response viewer** - Syntax-highlighted body with line numbers, foldable JSON, XML and HTML blocks, and optional line wrapping - JSON, XML and HTML sent as plain text or without a `Content-Type` are detected and formatted; a format menu forces JSON, XML, HTML or plain text - Paginated rendering for large responses (512 KB pages, once a response exceeds 10 MB) - Full-text search with match navigation - Save response to file, copy to clipboard - Headers table, parsed `Set-Cookie` cookies, test results, script logs — all in one panel - Hover the status for what the code means, and the size for headers, body and compressed size - Preview tab for HTML, images and PDFs; binary bodies are detected rather than rendered as mojibake - Diff against the previous response or a saved example - Timeline with connection details and the request as it went on the wire, secrets masked, one block per redirect hop - Realtime panels for SSE, WebSocket, Socket.IO, and gRPC responses, with saved WebSocket and Socket.IO messages kept in the request - Filter JSON responses with JSONPath or jq-style paths such as `.items[].id` **Code generation** — copy the current request as a runnable snippet in one of 14 targets: cURL, HTTPie, JavaScript `fetch`, Node.js `fetch`, Axios, Python `requests`, Go `net/http`, Java OkHttp, C# `HttpClient`, PHP cURL, Ruby `Net::HTTP`, Swift `URLSession`, Kotlin OkHttp, and Rust `reqwest`. Secret variables stay as `{{name}}` placeholders. **Browser request emulation** — send with a browser's rules instead of a client's: an `Origin` header, CORS preflight and response checks, and Content Security Policy enforcement, so a request can reproduce what the browser will do before the frontend is written. **Settings per request**: HTTP version (auto / 1.1 / 2), SSL verification, redirect policy (follow, preserve method, preserve auth), cookie jar, timeout, proxy, URL encoding. **Keyboard-first**: all actions have configurable shortcuts. A command palette (`Cmd/Ctrl K`) finds requests and runs commands, quick send (`Cmd/Ctrl Enter`), focus the URL (`Cmd/Ctrl L`), tab switching (`Cmd/Ctrl 1`–`8`, with `9` for the last tab). Kurlo shows `Cmd` on macOS and `Ctrl` on Windows and Linux. **Dark and light themes**, with multiple built-in variations. **Local-first storage** — the local Kurlo profile and its secrets are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM. The key is stored in the OS credential store when available and also kept as a `0600` recovery file in Kurlo's app-data directory. Git-backed workspace YAML is intentionally human-readable; secret values are replaced with local placeholders. --- ## Building from source **Prerequisites** - Go 1.25+ - Node.js 22.12+ - [Wails v2](https://wails.io/docs/gettingstarted/installation) — `go install github.com/wailsapp/wails/v2/cmd/wails@latest` - macOS: Xcode Command Line Tools - Windows: NSIS (for installer builds) and Windows SDK (for MSIX packaging/signing tools) - Linux: `libgtk-3-dev`, `libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev` **Dev mode** (hot-reload frontend + Go backend): ```bash git clone https://github.com/stormhop/kurlo cd kurlo npm install make dev ``` **Production build** for the current platform: ```bash make build ``` **All platforms** (requires each platform's toolchain): ```bash make build-all ``` **Run everyday checks** — lint, frontend types, unit tests and Go tests run concurrently, with Go's test cache enabled: ```bash make check ``` **Run the full test suite**, including the Go race detector and Chromium/WebKit: ```bash make check-full ``` | During development | Command | |-------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------| | One unit-test file | `npm run test:unit -- src/tests/agent.test.ts` | | Watch unit tests | `npm run test:watch -- agent` | | Unit tests related to uncommitted changes | `npm run test:changed` | | Matching Go tests | `make test GO_TEST_FLAGS='-run TestCodex'` | | Go tests without the heavy scale cases | `make test GO_TEST_FLAGS=-short` | | Matching browser tests | `npm run test:e2e -- --grep 'Codex'` | | Both browsers | `npm run test:e2e:all` | | Interactive browser test runner | `npm run test:e2e:ui` | | Retry only failed browser tests | `npm run test:e2e:failed` | Browser tests run against a production build of the frontend that Playwright builds and serves on each run, so they do not keep a dev server compiling modules for every page. Locally they record no video or trace; set `KURLO_E2E_TRACE=1` to keep them for failures (`npm run test:e2e:failed` does), and `KURLO_E2E_SERVER=dev` to test against the Vite dev server, which the `--ui` and `--debug` modes use. Browser tests use up to four workers locally and two in CI. Override this with `--workers=2`; use `--workers=1` for isolated performance comparisons. Screenshot-generation and profiling modes default to one worker. On a memory-constrained machine, `make check CHECK_JOBS=1` runs the independent checks sequentially. Go tests already run packages in parallel; tests sharing process-wide environment variables stay sequential within a package. Go caches successful runs; add `GO_TEST_FLAGS='-count=1'` only when a fresh run is needed. See `make help` for every available target. --- ## Project layout ``` apps/desktop/ Wails v2 desktop application apps/desktop/main.go Entry point, window config, native menus apps/desktop/cmd/kurlo/ Headless CLI (run, load, mcp) published to npm as @kurlo/cli apps/desktop/internal/ api/ HTTP executor, auth, request store, state api/auth/ Bearer, Basic, Digest, API Key, OAuth2, AWS SigV4 model/ Shared Go types (request, response, auth config) script/ JavaScript sandbox and pm.* API apps/desktop/frontend/src/ App.svelte Root shell and layout lib/stores/app.svelte.ts Composed app view-model lib/stores/features/ Feature slices for requests, collections, Git, import/export, etc. lib/components/ UI components lib/backend.ts Wails bridge type definitions apps/desktop/extension/ Cookie Sync browser extension (MV3 + Firefox event page) apps/web/ Astro Starlight documentation site npm/cli/ The @kurlo/cli npm launcher; scripts/build-npm-packages.mjs adds the binaries schemas/ Public Git/YAML workspace JSON Schema perf/ Generated performance fixtures (ignored by Git) ``` --- ## Scripting API reference Scripts run in a sandboxed JavaScript environment with a two-second default timeout, configurable per request up to 60 seconds. The sandbox blocks module imports, filesystem access, processes, and direct network access. Requests can opt in to HTTP calls through `pm.sendRequest`. The full surface — every method, the variable-scope precedence rules, and the Chai-style assertion aliases — is in the [scripting API reference](https://kurlo.dev/docs/reference/scripting-api/). The short version: | Surface | What it covers | |-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | `pm.request` | `url`, `method`, `set_url()`, `headers.get/set/unset`, `params.get/set` | | `pm.request.body` | `raw`, `mode`, `json()`, `update()`, plus `urlencoded` / `formdata` field lists | | `pm.response` | `code`, `status`, `responseTime`, `size`, `body()`, `json()`, `headers.get()` — test scripts only | | `pm.variables` · `pm.globals` · `pm.environment` · `pm.collectionVariables` | `get` / `set` / `unset` / `clear`, differing only in which scope they read and write | | `pm.iterationData.get(key)` | The current data-row value in a data-driven run (read-only) | | `pm.info` | `requestName`, `eventName`, `iteration`, `iterationCount` | | `pm.cookies` | `get` / `has` / `names` for the cookies this request's jar would send | | `pm.crypto` · `CryptoJS` | MD5/SHA digests, HMAC, base64, `randomHex()`, `uuid()` | | `pm.sendRequest(req, cb)` | A synchronous HTTP call through the regular request engine | | `pm.execution.skipRequest()` | From a pre-request script, skips the send — reported as skipped, not failed | | `pm.test(name, fnOrResult)` | Register a named assertion | | `pm.expect(value)` | `.equal` · `.contains` · `.exists` · `.has_key` · … plus `.to.equal(v)`, `.to.include(v)`, `.to.have.property(k)` | | `pm.response.to.have.*` | `status(code)`, `header(name)`, `jsonBody(path?, value?)`, `jsonSchema(schema)` (draft-07) | | `pm.log(...values)` | Output to the Scripts panel | `require` resolves bundled stand-ins for `lodash`, `ajv`, `tv4`, `uuid`, `crypto-js`, and `chai`. There is no event loop: `setTimeout`, `async` and `await` are not available, and `pm.sendRequest`'s callback runs immediately. --- ## Support Kurlo Kurlo is free for teams of any size and will stay that way. If it saves you time, you can support development on [Boosty](https://boosty.to/kurlo): it pays for the server, macOS code signing and the hours that go into new features. Supporters get dev updates and early release candidates. --- ## Contributing Bug reports, feature requests, and pull requests are welcome. Start with [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) — it covers the dev setup, what CI enforces, and how to scope a change. Everyone taking part is expected to follow the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). Found a security problem? Please **don't** open a public issue — see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for private reporting instead. --- ## License [MIT](LICENSE)

    branches: [main]

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  test:
    name: Desktop and web checks
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Setup Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@v7
        with:
          go-version-file: apps/desktop/go.mod
          cache-dependency-path: apps/desktop/go.sum

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: package-lock.json

      - name: Install frontend dependencies
        run: npm install

      - name: Lint
        run: npm run lint

      - name: Check frontend
        run: npm run frontend:check

      - name: Test frontend
        run: npm --workspace @kurlo/desktop-frontend run test

      - name: Test release scripts
        run: python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'

      - name: Build frontend
        run: npm run frontend:build

      - name: Build web docs
        env:
          KURLO_SITE_URL: ${{ vars.KURLO_SITE_URL }}
          KURLO_SITE_BASE: ${{ vars.KURLO_SITE_BASE }}
        run: npm run web:build

      - name: Check web docs
        env:
          KURLO_SITE_BASE: ${{ vars.KURLO_SITE_BASE }}
        run: npm run web:check-docs

      - name: Check download links
        run: npm run web:check-downloads

      - name: Install Wails Linux dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libgtk-3-dev libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential pkg-config

      - name: Check Go formatting
        run: |
          unformatted=$(gofmt -l apps/desktop/)
          if [ -n "$unformatted" ]; then
            echo "::error::These files need 'gofmt -w':"
            echo "$unformatted"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "All Go files are formatted."

      - name: Check generated Wails bindings are current
        working-directory: apps/desktop
        run: |
          go run github.com/wailsapp/wails/v2/cmd/wails@v2.16.0 generate module
          if ! git -c core.fileMode=false diff --quiet -- frontend/wailsjs; then
            echo "::error::wailsjs bindings are out of date. Run 'make bindings' and commit the result:"
            git -c core.fileMode=false diff --stat -- frontend/wailsjs
            git -c core.fileMode=false diff -- frontend/wailsjs
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Generated bindings match the Go source."

      - name: Vet Go
        run: go vet ./apps/desktop/...

      - name: Test Go (race detector)
        run: go test -race ./apps/desktop/...

      - name: Dead code check
        run: |
          output=$(go run golang.org/x/tools/cmd/deadcode@v0.45.0 -test ./apps/desktop/...)
          if [ -n "$output" ]; then
            echo "::error::Unreachable (dead) code detected — remove it or wire it up:"
            echo "$output"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "No dead code."

  npm-cli:
    name: Build npm CLI
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Setup Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@v7
        with:
          go-version-file: apps/desktop/go.mod
          cache-dependency-path: |
            apps/desktop/go.sum
            scripts/build-npm-packages.mjs

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 22

      - name: Build the npm CLI without cgo
        run: node scripts/build-npm-packages.mjs --version 0.0.0-ci --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/npm"

  build-and-test:
    name: Build & Test
    needs: [test, npm-cli]
    if: ${{ always() }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04

    steps:
      - name: Require desktop and web checks and the CLI build to pass
        env:
          TEST_RESULT: ${{ needs.test.result }}
          CLI_RESULT: ${{ needs.npm-cli.result }}
        run: |
          if [ "$TEST_RESULT" != "success" ] || [ "$CLI_RESULT" != "success" ]; then
            echo "::error::Desktop and web checks finished with '$TEST_RESULT', CLI build with '$CLI_RESULT'"
            exit 1
          fi

  go-cross-platform:
    name: Go tests (${{ matrix.os }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}

    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: macos-latest
            race: true
          - os: windows-latest
            race: false

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Setup Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@v7
        with:
          go-version-file: apps/desktop/go.mod
          cache-dependency-path: apps/desktop/go.sum

      - name: Stand in for the embedded frontend
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p apps/desktop/frontend/dist
          echo '<!doctype html><title>ci placeholder</title>' > apps/desktop/frontend/dist/index.html

      - name: Vet Go
        run: go vet ./apps/desktop/...

      - name: Test Go
        if: ${{ !matrix.race }}
        run: go test ./apps/desktop/...

      - name: Test Go (race detector)
        if: ${{ matrix.race }}
        run: go test -race ./apps/desktop/...

  e2e-tests:
    name: E2E (${{ matrix.suite }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04

    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - suite: chromium
            browsers: chromium
            args: --project=chromium --grep-invert @scale --workers=2
          - suite: webkit-1
            browsers: webkit
            args: --project=webkit --grep-invert @scale --workers=2 --shard=1/2
          - suite: webkit-2
            browsers: webkit
            args: --project=webkit --grep-invert @scale --workers=2 --shard=2/2
          - suite: scale
            browsers: chromium webkit
            args: --grep @scale --workers=1

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: package-lock.json

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install

      - name: Install Playwright browsers
        run: npx playwright install --with-deps ${{ matrix.browsers }}
        working-directory: apps/desktop/frontend

      - name: Run E2E tests
        run: npm exec --workspace @kurlo/desktop-frontend -- playwright test ${{ matrix.args }}
        env:
          KURLO_E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/playwright-${{ matrix.suite }}

      - name: Upload Playwright report
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: playwright-report-${{ matrix.suite }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/playwright-${{ matrix.suite }}/html-report
          retention-days: 3
          if-no-files-found: ignore

  e2e:
    name: E2E (Playwright)
    needs: e2e-tests
    if: ${{ always() }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04

    steps:
      - name: Require all E2E suites to pass
        env:
          E2E_RESULT: ${{ needs.e2e-tests.result }}
        run: |
          if [ "$E2E_RESULT" != "success" ]; then
            echo "::error::E2E suites finished with '$E2E_RESULT'"
            exit 1
          fi

# Kurlo **The open-source API client with an agent inside and your secret managers built in.**
Bring any model, Claude Code or Codex, and link variables to Vault, 1Password or your cloud. No account, no paid plan, no telemetry. Collections live as YAML in your Git repo. [![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/stormhop/kurlo)](https://github.com/stormhop/kurlo/releases/latest) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/stormhop/kurlo?style=flat)](https://github.com/stormhop/kurlo/stargazers) [![CI](https://github.com/stormhop/kurlo/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/stormhop/kurlo/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![Platforms](https://img.shields.io/badge/platforms-macOS%20%7C%20Windows%20%7C%20Linux-lightgrey)](https://github.com/stormhop/kurlo/releases/latest) **[Download](https://github.com/stormhop/kurlo/releases/latest)** · [Website](https://kurlo.dev/) · [Docs](https://kurlo.dev/docs/getting-started/installation/) · [Secret managers](https://kurlo.dev/docs/guides/environments/secret-managers/) · [Agent mode](https://kurlo.dev/agent/) · [MCP server](https://kurlo.dev/mcp/) · [Compare](https://kurlo.dev/vs/postman/)
## New in 3.2: Secret managers Link an environment variable to HashiCorp Vault or OpenBao, 1Password, AWS Secrets Manager or Parameter Store, Google Secret Manager, Azure Key Vault, Bitwarden Secrets Manager, Doppler, Infisical, KeePassXC, a command of your own or the environment of the Kurlo process. The environment file in Git keeps only the reference, and each teammate signs in with their own token, AWS profile or CLI. Kurlo fetches the value when a request is sent and shows `[secret]` in responses, history, script logs, `kurlo run` reports and everything an agent sees. Paste an ARN, an `op://` link, an Azure secret URL or a Vault path to fill in the link, or browse the provider's paths. A workspace you clone uses a provider only after you trust it on your machine. All twelve providers are free; Bruno sells cloud vaults in its Ultimate plan and Postman in Enterprise with a security add-on. ```yaml - key: dbPassword secretRef: provider: vault-prod path: secret/data/orders field: password ``` In CI, `kurlo run` fetches the same links with the runner's credentials before the first request and stops with exit code 2 naming any variable it could not get. [Secret managers guide](https://kurlo.dev/docs/guides/environments/secret-managers/) ## Agent mode Ask in plain words and the agent runs your requests and collections, explains why a call failed, writes requests and tests and imports your specs, right inside Kurlo. Pick the Kurlo agent on your own model (OpenRouter, an API key, Ollama or LM Studio), or connect the Claude Code or Codex you already use. Every change and every call other than `GET`, `HEAD` or `OPTIONS` waits for your approval, and the model never sees your secrets. ![The Kurlo agent reads a collection, runs the requests, and asks before adding tests to four of them](.github/assets/agent-mode.gif) [Agent mode on kurlo.dev](https://kurlo.dev/agent/) · [Agent guide](https://kurlo.dev/docs/guides/agent/) ## Why Kurlo - **Secrets from where they already live.** Link variables to Vault, 1Password, AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, Bitwarden, Doppler, Infisical or KeePassXC. Git gets the reference, your API gets the value, and the screen, logs and agents get `[secret]`. - **An agent that asks first.** The Kurlo agent, Claude Code or Codex works on your collections inside the app. It shows every change before it is written, can follow a plan you approve and work on its own Git branch, and keeps chats on your machine. - **Free for a team of any size.** There is no paid plan to grow into and no account to create. A team shares a workspace through any Git host, and every request is a readable YAML file that gets reviewed in the same pull request as the API change. - **Your Postman collections keep working.** Import a Postman, Insomnia, Bruno, OpenAPI, WSDL or HAR file. `pm.test`, `pm.expect` with chai, `pm.sendRequest` and `require('lodash')` run as they were written. - **Share an API reference.** Turn a collection into a searchable HTML file with saved requests and responses. Open it offline or publish it to a static host. - **Or drive it from your terminal.** `kurlo mcp` lets Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and any other MCP client run your saved requests with their auth and tests, write new requests and tests, and explain why the last call failed. Secrets are sent to the API but never shown to the model. - **Small and native.** Built with Go and the system WebView instead of Electron, so the macOS download is 26.8 MB and the Linux one is 14.1 MB. | | Kurlo | Postman | Insomnia | Bruno | |------------------------------|--------------------------------|-------------------------------|------------------------|----------------------------| | Free plan | ✅ Every feature, any team size | 1 user | Up to 3 Git Sync users | Private Git hosts need Pro | | Account needed | ✅ No | For collections | Beyond Scratch Pad | No | | Collections in your Git repo | ✅ | Native Git in the desktop app | ✅ | ✅ | | Postman `pm.*` scripts | ✅ Run as written | Native | Compatibility layer | Converted to `bru.*` | | Mock server | ✅ Local, no cap | Cloud, needs an account | 1,000 requests/mo free | ✅ Local | | MCP | ✅ Client and server | Client | Client | Community servers | Checked against vendor pricing pages on 15 October 2026. Details and sources: [vs Postman](https://kurlo.dev/vs/postman/), [vs Insomnia](https://kurlo.dev/vs/insomnia/), [vs Bruno](https://kurlo.dev/vs/bruno/). If Kurlo saves you time, a ⭐ helps other people find it. --- ## Download Grab the latest build from the [releases page](https://github.com/stormhop/kurlo/releases/latest). | Platform | Installer | |---------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------| | macOS 15 Sequoia or later (Apple Silicon + Intel) | `.dmg` | | Windows 10/11 (x64, arm64) | `.exe` (NSIS installer), `.msix` | | Linux (x64) | `.AppImage` | Every release ships SHA256 checksums and minisign signatures, and the in-app updater refuses any binary that fails either check. The command line (`kurlo run` for CI, `kurlo mcp` for AI agents) is also on npm as [ `@kurlo/cli`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@kurlo/cli), with prebuilt binaries for macOS, Linux and Windows on x64 and arm64. It does not need the desktop app: ```bash npx -y @kurlo/cli --version ``` Guides, the scripting reference, and the YAML workspace format live in the **[documentation site](https://kurlo.dev/)**. --- ## Features **Requests** - All HTTP methods: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS - Query params, headers, body (JSON, form-data, x-www-form-urlencoded, raw text/XML/HTML, binary file) - cURL import — paste a curl command into the URL field, it parses automatically - Bulk edit for params, headers and form fields — switch the table to a `key: value` text area and back - Suggestions while you type — the rest of a URL from history and saved requests, and the next JSON key from saved examples - Build GraphQL operations from a schema, select nested fields and bind typed variables in the query editor - Run GraphQL subscriptions over WebSocket with the `graphql-ws` protocol (and the older `subscriptions-transport-ws`), with a connection payload and a live event log - MQTT 3.1, 3.1.1 and 5 requests over TCP, TLS and WebSocket: subscriptions with wildcards and QoS, publishing with properties, last will and a live message log - Kafka producer and consumer requests with topic discovery, live records, partition offsets, TLS and SASL. - GraphQL, Server-Sent Events, WebSocket, Socket.IO, gRPC, and MCP request types — an MCP call discovers the server's tools, resources and prompts, seeds the arguments from the tool's schema, and shows the raw JSON-RPC exchange - Import Postman v2 JSON or v3 Native Git folders, Insomnia v4, Bruno/OpenCollection, OpenAPI/Swagger, HAR, cURL, and all-data backups - WSDL import — a SOAP 1.1 or 1.2 request with a sample envelope for every operation, from a file or a `?wsdl` link - OpenAPI/Swagger imports from a link as well as a file — paste the spec URL and Kurlo fetches it and builds the collection - OpenAPI sync — keep a collection linked to its spec URL or file, review new, changed and removed endpoints with a three-way merge that keeps your edits, with no monthly limit; `kurlo openapi check` flags drift in CI - Export Postman v2.1 JSON, Postman v3 folders with native gRPC, Insomnia v4, OpenAPI/Swagger, OpenCollection YAML, and all-data backups **Authentication** - Bearer Token - Basic Auth - NTLM (NTLMv2) - Digest Auth — MD5, SHA-256 and SHA-512-256 plus their `-sess` variants, with `qop=auth` and `auth-int` - API Key — in header or query string - JWT Bearer — signed on every send from a secret or a private key (HS, RS, PS and ES algorithms), with claims, an optional lifetime and a token preview - OAuth 2.0 — Client Credentials, Authorization Code (with PKCE), Password, and Device Code grants; loopback browser sign-in, refresh tokens, and automatic token refresh before each send - AWS Signature v4 - Client certificates (mutual TLS), per request or inherited from a collection - Per-request and collection defaults with inheritance **Scripting** — write sandboxed JavaScript in requests, folders and collections. The editor completes `pm.*` methods, variable keys and saved request names, with signatures and examples. ```js // pre-request: inject a header pm.request.headers.set("X-Client", "kurlo") // pre-request: rewrite and sign the body pm.request.body.update(JSON.stringify({...pm.request.body.json(), nonce: pm.crypto.randomHex(8)})) // test: assert status and shape pm.test("status is 200", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200)) pm.test("has an id", () => pm.response.to.have.jsonSchema({type: "object", required: ["id"]})) ``` **Assertions** — check the status, response time, size, a header or a JSON field without code (`status equals 201`, `body.items has length 3`); they run in the app, the collection runner, `kurlo run` and `kurlo mcp`. `require` resolves bundled stand-ins for `lodash`, `ajv`, `tv4`, `uuid`, `crypto-js`, and `chai`, so imported Postman scripts keep working. `pm.sendRequest` makes an HTTP call from a script, and `pm.execution.skipRequest()` skips the send. **Environments & Variables** - Multiple environments per workspace, switch with one click - Environments inherit the variables they do not set from another environment, such as Staging from Base - Matrix view — every variable as a row, every environment as a column, edited in place - `{{variable}}` template syntax in URLs, headers, params, body, auth fields - Set variables from test scripts (`pm.variables.set`, `pm.environment.set`) - Secret managers — link a variable to Vault/OpenBao, 1Password, AWS Secrets Manager and Parameter Store, Google Secret Manager, Azure Key Vault, Bitwarden, Doppler, Infisical, KeePassXC, a command or process env vars, or import every key of one secret; `{{vault:name}}` and `await pm.vault.get()` work as in Postman - Manual-save and autosave modes both cover request and environment edits **Workspaces & Collections** - Multiple workspaces for separate projects or clients - Collections with nested folder hierarchy and empty-folder preservation - Folder defaults — headers, auth, scripts and tests on a folder apply to every request inside it - Drag-and-drop organisation - Request history — every send on its own page, request and stored response side by side, reopenable in the editor ( 14-day retention, 1000 entries) - [Static API documentation](https://kurlo.dev/docs/guides/cli-runner/docs/) — build a standalone HTML reference with `kurlo docs build` or **Build documentation** in the collection menu - Collection runner — sequential or parallel, data files, iterations, an HTML report, and the last run of every collection kept - [Load testing with k6](https://kurlo.dev/docs/guides/load-testing/) — collection flows with extraction and checks, virtual users or iteration rates, thresholds, CSV/JSON data, script export, local runs and last-run reports - Git-backed YAML workspaces with diagnostics, conflict helpers, and local-only secrets; branch, commit, pull, push and open a pull request from the app - Edit a request's YAML file in the File tab with completion, schema checks, Beautify and protected identity fields; the address bar edits the same draft - **CLI runner** — `npx -y @kurlo/cli run ./workspace --env CI` executes requests and their test scripts for CI, with data-driven iterations (`--data`), pretty/JSON/JUnit reporters, variable export, and a non-zero exit code on failure. `kurlo load list|export|run` lists collection load tests, exports k6 scripts or runs local k6 with threshold results and reports **Agent mode** — since 3.0. Pick the Kurlo agent on your own model (OpenRouter, an API key, or Ollama and LM Studio), or connect the Claude Code and Codex CLIs you already use with their own accounts, and ask in plain words. The agent runs requests and collections, explains failures, writes requests and tests, imports OpenAPI, Postman and HAR files, and reads a connected project folder. It asks before every change and every call other than `GET`, `HEAD` or `OPTIONS`, can follow a plan you approve, work on its own Git branch and call your own MCP servers. Trusted hosts and sandbox environments run without asking, protected environments are off limits, and secrets reach the API while the model sees `[secret]`. Chats stay encrypted on your machine, and **Activity** lists every tool call with the files it changed and a way to restore them. See the [agent guide](https://kurlo.dev/docs/guides/agent/). **AI agents (MCP server)** — the Kurlo binary is also a Model Context Protocol server, so Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Claude Desktop or any other MCP client can list your collections and environments, run saved HTTP, GraphQL, unary gRPC, MCP and AI requests, run collections with CSV or JSON data, and send one-off calls with your `{{variables}}`. It can start and compare k6 runs and serve saved examples from a local mock. In the desktop app, Agent Mode can also exchange messages on live connections. It can also keep the workspace up to date: add and change requests with their `pm.*` tests, save responses as examples and set environment variables, in the same YAML the app writes, never storing a secret. It can preview and apply imports, read a connected project folder, edit Markdown docs and generate snippets. It reads the last request you sent from the app, so "why did that fail?" needs no copying. Secret values are sent to the API but masked as `[secret]` in everything the model sees, and environments you mark protected are off limits. One command sets up every client on the machine: ![Claude Code adds tests to a Kurlo collection over MCP, finds a pricing bug and fixes it, while the tests appear in Kurlo](.github/assets/demo.gif) ```bash npx -y @kurlo/cli mcp install --env Staging ``` Add `--project` to write a repository's shared `.mcp.json` and `.cursor/mcp.json` instead, so the whole team gets the server by cloning. Manual setup, the tools and the flags are covered in the [MCP server guide](https://kurlo.dev/docs/guides/mcp-server/). **Response examples** — save any response as a named example on its request: the status, headers and body it came back with, alongside the request that produced it. Secrets are redacted on capture, a clean body is stored byte for byte, and examples are read from Postman, OpenCollection, HAR and OpenAPI and included in Postman v2.1 and OpenCollection exports. A response can be diffed against an example instead of against the previous send. **Cookies** — a per-workspace cookie jar with a per-domain editor, disableable per request. - **Cookie sync**: pair Kurlo with the in-repo browser extension (`apps/desktop/extension`, Chromium + Firefox) and the session you already have in the browser is the session Kurlo sends with. A loopback-only bridge that stays off until you turn it on, an approval you give in Kurlo by matching a six-digit code, and a per-domain allowlist enforced on both sides. Cookies travel one way: browser into Kurlo. **Mock server** — serve a collection's saved examples over HTTP on a local port, so a client can be built against an endpoint that does not exist yet. Routing is by method and the example's path template (`/orders/:id`), a recorded query narrows which example answers, and a live log shows what the client asked for and which example replied. Loopback only; CORS preflight is answered for any origin. **Response viewer** - Syntax-highlighted body with line numbers, foldable JSON, XML and HTML blocks, and optional line wrapping - JSON, XML and HTML sent as plain text or without a `Content-Type` are detected and formatted; a format menu forces JSON, XML, HTML or plain text - Paginated rendering for large responses (512 KB pages, once a response exceeds 10 MB) - Full-text search with match navigation - Save response to file, copy to clipboard - Headers table, parsed `Set-Cookie` cookies, test results, script logs — all in one panel - Hover the status for what the code means, and the size for headers, body and compressed size - Preview tab for HTML, images and PDFs; binary bodies are detected rather than rendered as mojibake - Diff against the previous response or a saved example - Timeline with connection details and the request as it went on the wire, secrets masked, one block per redirect hop - Realtime panels for SSE, WebSocket, Socket.IO, and gRPC responses, with saved WebSocket and Socket.IO messages kept in the request - Filter JSON responses with JSONPath or jq-style paths such as `.items[].id` **Code generation** — copy the current request as a runnable snippet in one of 14 targets: cURL, HTTPie, JavaScript `fetch`, Node.js `fetch`, Axios, Python `requests`, Go `net/http`, Java OkHttp, C# `HttpClient`, PHP cURL, Ruby `Net::HTTP`, Swift `URLSession`, Kotlin OkHttp, and Rust `reqwest`. Secret variables stay as `{{name}}` placeholders. **Browser request emulation** — send with a browser's rules instead of a client's: an `Origin` header, CORS preflight and response checks, and Content Security Policy enforcement, so a request can reproduce what the browser will do before the frontend is written. **Settings per request**: HTTP version (auto / 1.1 / 2), SSL verification, redirect policy (follow, preserve method, preserve auth), cookie jar, timeout, proxy, URL encoding. **Keyboard-first**: all actions have configurable shortcuts. A command palette (`Cmd/Ctrl K`) finds requests and runs commands, quick send (`Cmd/Ctrl Enter`), focus the URL (`Cmd/Ctrl L`), tab switching (`Cmd/Ctrl 1`–`8`, with `9` for the last tab). Kurlo shows `Cmd` on macOS and `Ctrl` on Windows and Linux. **Dark and light themes**, with multiple built-in variations. **Local-first storage** — the local Kurlo profile and its secrets are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM. The key is stored in the OS credential store when available and also kept as a `0600` recovery file in Kurlo's app-data directory. Git-backed workspace YAML is intentionally human-readable; secret values are replaced with local placeholders. --- ## Building from source **Prerequisites** - Go 1.25+ - Node.js 22.12+ - [Wails v2](https://wails.io/docs/gettingstarted/installation) — `go install github.com/wailsapp/wails/v2/cmd/wails@latest` - macOS: Xcode Command Line Tools - Windows: NSIS (for installer builds) and Windows SDK (for MSIX packaging/signing tools) - Linux: `libgtk-3-dev`, `libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev` **Dev mode** (hot-reload frontend + Go backend): ```bash git clone https://github.com/stormhop/kurlo cd kurlo npm install make dev ``` **Production build** for the current platform: ```bash make build ``` **All platforms** (requires each platform's toolchain): ```bash make build-all ``` **Run everyday checks** — lint, frontend types, unit tests and Go tests run concurrently, with Go's test cache enabled: ```bash make check ``` **Run the full test suite**, including the Go race detector and Chromium/WebKit: ```bash make check-full ``` | During development | Command | |-------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------| | One unit-test file | `npm run test:unit -- src/tests/agent.test.ts` | | Watch unit tests | `npm run test:watch -- agent` | | Unit tests related to uncommitted changes | `npm run test:changed` | | Matching Go tests | `make test GO_TEST_FLAGS='-run TestCodex'` | | Go tests without the heavy scale cases | `make test GO_TEST_FLAGS=-short` | | Matching browser tests | `npm run test:e2e -- --grep 'Codex'` | | Both browsers | `npm run test:e2e:all` | | Interactive browser test runner | `npm run test:e2e:ui` | | Retry only failed browser tests | `npm run test:e2e:failed` | Browser tests run against a production build of the frontend that Playwright builds and serves on each run, so they do not keep a dev server compiling modules for every page. Browser tests use up to four workers locally and two in CI. Override this with `--workers=2`; use `--workers=1` for isolated performance comparisons. Screenshot-generation and profiling modes default to one worker. On a memory-constrained machine, `make check CHECK_JOBS=1` runs the independent checks sequentially. Go tests already run packages in parallel; tests sharing process-wide environment variables stay sequential within a package. Go caches successful runs; add `GO_TEST_FLAGS='-count=1'` only when a fresh run is needed. See `make help` for every available target. --- ## Project layout ``` apps/desktop/ Wails v2 desktop application apps/desktop/main.go Entry point, window config, native menus apps/desktop/cmd/kurlo/ Headless CLI (run, load, mcp) published to npm as @kurlo/cli apps/desktop/internal/ api/ HTTP executor, auth, request store, state api/auth/ Bearer, Basic, Digest, API Key, OAuth2, AWS SigV4 model/ Shared Go types (request, response, auth config) script/ JavaScript sandbox and pm.* API apps/desktop/frontend/src/ App.svelte Root shell and layout lib/stores/app.svelte.ts Composed app view-model lib/stores/features/ Feature slices for requests, collections, Git, import/export, etc. lib/components/ UI components lib/backend.ts Wails bridge type definitions apps/desktop/extension/ Cookie Sync browser extension (MV3 + Firefox event page) apps/web/ Astro Starlight documentation site npm/cli/ The @kurlo/cli npm launcher; scripts/build-npm-packages.mjs adds the binaries schemas/ Public Git/YAML workspace JSON Schema perf/ Generated performance fixtures (ignored by Git) ``` --- ## Scripting API reference Scripts run in a sandboxed JavaScript environment with a two-second default timeout, configurable per request up to 60 seconds. The sandbox blocks module imports, filesystem access, processes, and direct network access. Requests can opt in to HTTP calls through `pm.sendRequest`. The full surface — every method, the variable-scope precedence rules, and the Chai-style assertion aliases — is in the [scripting API reference](https://kurlo.dev/docs/reference/scripting-api/). The short version: | Surface | What it covers | |-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | `pm.request` | `url`, `method`, `set_url()`, `headers.get/set/unset`, `params.get/set` | | `pm.request.body` | `raw`, `mode`, `json()`, `update()`, plus `urlencoded` / `formdata` field lists | | `pm.response` | `code`, `status`, `responseTime`, `size`, `body()`, `json()`, `headers.get()` — test scripts only | | `pm.variables` · `pm.globals` · `pm.environment` · `pm.collectionVariables` | `get` / `set` / `unset` / `clear`, differing only in which scope they read and write | | `pm.iterationData.get(key)` | The current data-row value in a data-driven run (read-only) | | `pm.info` | `requestName`, `eventName`, `iteration`, `iterationCount` | | `pm.cookies` | `get` / `has` / `names` for the cookies this request's jar would send | | `pm.crypto` · `CryptoJS` | MD5/SHA digests, HMAC, base64, `randomHex()`, `uuid()` | | `pm.sendRequest(req, cb)` | A synchronous HTTP call through the regular request engine | | `pm.execution.skipRequest()` | From a pre-request script, skips the send — reported as skipped, not failed | | `pm.test(name, fnOrResult)` | Register a named assertion | | `pm.expect(value)` | `.equal` · `.contains` · `.exists` · `.has_key` · … plus `.to.equal(v)`, `.to.include(v)`, `.to.have.property(k)` | | `pm.response.to.have.*` | `status(code)`, `header(name)`, `jsonBody(path?, value?)`, `jsonSchema(schema)` (draft-07) | | `pm.log(...values)` | Output to the Scripts panel | `require` resolves bundled stand-ins for `lodash`, `ajv`, `tv4`, `uuid`, `crypto-js`, and `chai`. There is no event loop: `setTimeout`, `async` and `await` are not available, and `pm.sendRequest`'s callback runs immediately. --- ## Support Kurlo Kurlo is free for teams of any size and will stay that way. If it saves you time, you can support development on [Boosty](https://boosty.to/kurlo): it pays for the server, macOS code signing and the hours that go into new features. Supporters get dev updates and early release candidates. --- ## Contributing Bug reports, feature requests, and pull requests are welcome. Start with [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) — it covers the dev setup, what CI enforces, and how to scope a change. Everyone taking part is expected to follow the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). Found a security problem? Please **don't** open a public issue — see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for private reporting instead. --- ## License [MIT](LICENSE)

repository.readme:
# Monica

Architecture agents can follow. Systems humans can inspect.

English | 简体中文

Monica is modular .NET infrastructure for agent-driven development. Applications can adopt its modules independently, while developers and coding agents share a typed vocabulary for composition, DDD Building Blocks, and runtime diagnostics. That makes generated code structurally predictable and running systems inspectable. > Monica is approaching 1.0 and is still allowed to make breaking architectural improvements before the stable release. ## Why Monica - **A graph, not startup glue.** `AddMonica(...)` records the complete module graph for one host, validates dependencies and cycles, then applies registrations in deterministic phases. - **A vocabulary agents can follow.** Building Blocks describe application services, domain services, entities, repositories, events, handlers, configurations, and jobs by their supported responsibilities. - **Inspectable by default.** Operational modules expose the same graph, configuration, jobs, telemetry, and application structure that produced the running process. - **Host-scoped state.** A Monica composition belongs to its host. Multiple hosts in one process do not share module registries, options, mapping rules, or Building Block catalogs. ## Start in one minute Install only the packages used by your application: ```bash dotnet add package Monica.BuildingBlocks --prerelease dotnet add package Monica.JobScheduler --prerelease dotnet add package Monica.JobScheduler.UI --prerelease ``` Compose the host in one bounded callback: ```csharp using Monica.Core.Modularity.Extensions; using Monica.Modules; var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args); builder.AddMonica(monica => { monica.ConfigureApplication(options => { options.AppName = "Orders"; options.AppId = "orders"; }); monica.ConfigureModuleSystem(options => { options.DefaultApiGroupName = "Orders"; }); monica.AddEventBus().UseNoOpDistributedEventBus(); monica.AddBuildingBlocks(options => { options.Naming.Enabled = true; }); monica.AddJobScheduler(options => { options.ProjectName = "Orders"; }) .UseSchedulerScope("orders") .UseInMemoryStore(); monica.AddJobSchedulerUI(); }); var app = builder.Build(); app.UseMonica(); app.MapMonica(); app.Run(); ``` With a durable production store, execution leases provide at-least-once recovery after a worker crash, while fencing rejects mutations from an expired lease. Each host synchronizes, schedules, and executes the jobs it discovers under its own owner identity; replicas coordinate through durable compare-and-swap operations. Concurrency gates are keyed by scheduler scope, owner, and `JobKey`. Fencing cannot make arbitrary job side effects exactly-once, so jobs should use idempotency keys or transactional business boundaries for those effects. The JobScheduler UI workspace includes a runtime tab showing the host's effective configuration, storage identity, local scheduling-plane readiness, and every owner's durable footprint with a documented liveness threshold (three snapshot-sync intervals). Hosts that also register ServiceDiscovery can add `monica.AddJobSchedulerServiceDiscoveryInsight()` (package `Monica.JobScheduler.ServiceDiscovery`) to enrich that tab with live worker-instance heartbeats; without it, the tab hides the worker table behind a setup hint instead of failing. The callback is the complete composition boundary. Captured `ModuleRegistration<,>` handles cannot mutate the graph after it closes, and startup fails early when the graph is incomplete or cyclic. For a runnable DDD application rather than a toy snippet, see [`examples/Monica.ReferenceApplication`](examples/Monica.ReferenceApplication). For the smallest operational scheduler UI host, see [`examples/JobSchedulerMinimal`](examples/JobSchedulerMinimal). ## The architecture contract Every module follows the same public shape: - `Module{Name} : MonicaModule` — the host-owned lifecycle strategy. - `Module{Name}Option : ModuleOptions` — startup-frozen configuration and defaults. - `Module{Name}BuilderExtensions` — the discoverable `monica.Add{Name}()` entry point, returning a host-bound `ModuleRegistration<,>`. - `Module{Name}RegistrationExtensions` — optional provider and capability choices that enrich that registration. The strategy declares hard dependencies and optional ordering in `Describe(ModuleDescriptor)`. It reads its own finalized `Option` directly and can read another module's options only through one of those declared relationships. Business-type work is declared once through `DeclareTypeDiscovery(...)`; Monica combines non-empty structural queries into one type-universe scan and commits matches serially in graph order. A Building Block is an application code element with a defined responsibility that Monica recognizes through a supported kind contract. The current discoverable kinds are: `ApplicationRequestHandler` · `CrudApplicationService` · `DomainService` · `Repository` · `DomainEvent` · `DistributedEventHandler` · `LocalEventHandler` · `Seeder` · `RecurringJob` · `TriggeredJob` · `HttpApi` · `Entity` · `RequestDto` · `Configuration` · `HostedService` Each discovered Building Block can carry explicit agent context and requirement traceability: ```csharp using Monica.Application.Abstractions; using Monica.ApplicationModel.Annotations; [BuildingBlockMetadata( "Approve Order", Description = "Approves an eligible order.", Tags = ["ordering", "approval"])] [BuildingBlockRequirement("ORD-REQ-001")] public sealed record CommandApproveOrder(Guid OrderId) : ICommand; ``` Metadata describes a Building Block; it does not make an unsupported type discoverable. Add metadata separately to handlers and other discovered types. When `AddBuildingBlocksUI()` is registered in a web host, `Monica.Framework.UI` exposes a `/building-blocks` workspace with kind distribution, dependencies, alerts, and independent metadata, description, ownership, and requirement coverage. When Minimal APIs are enabled with `EnableMinimalApi = true` or the host default, the typed `/framework/building-blocks`, `/framework/building-blocks/dashboard`, and `/framework/building-blocks/{key}` APIs expose catalog data without leaking reflection objects. ## Module diagnostics Hosts opt in with `monica.AddModuleSystem()`. Its `ModuleDiagnosticsFacade` exposes one immutable, revisioned snapshot of composition outcome, timings, callbacks, startup work, type-discovery stages, findings, and direct dependency topology. Assembly inventory is lazy, option diagnostics are loaded separately, and portable exports omit option data, assembly paths, stack traces, and raw exception details. `monica.AddModuleSystemUI()` includes the Core diagnostics module automatically. Every public module-option property remains visible by clean type name. Ordinary bounded values are shown automatically; `[ModuleOptionDiagnosticsSensitive]` or a host policy reduces sensitive content to a non-secret presence, count, or protected-address representation as appropriate. `RevealSensitive` can reveal only bounded sensitive scalars and is restricted to Development-only debugging. The Module System workbench is also Development-only by default; exposing it elsewhere requires both explicit enablement and a host authorization policy. ## Knowledge for coding agents The canonical Monica Agent Skills live under [`skills/`](skills/). Nine consumer skills are the single source of reusable infrastructure usage guidance: [`monica-infra-persistence`](skills/monica-infra-persistence), [`monica-infra-messaging`](skills/monica-infra-messaging), [`monica-infra-jobs`](skills/monica-infra-jobs), [`monica-infra-configuration`](skills/monica-infra-configuration), [`monica-infra-hosting`](skills/monica-infra-hosting), [`monica-infra-observability`](skills/monica-infra-observability), [`monica-infra-ai`](skills/monica-infra-ai), [`monica-infra-web`](skills/monica-infra-web), and [`monica-infra-ui`](skills/monica-infra-ui). Other skills cover application architecture, framework authoring, testing, UI development, and contribution workflows. Start with `monica-guide` for installation and framework source discovery, then use the skill that owns the task. Repository-local discovery copies under `.agents/skills/` and `.claude/skills/` are generated on demand by `python scripts/sync_agent_skills.py --write`; they are local agent state and are not tracked in git. [Monica.Docs](https://monica.dpdns.org/) publishes the skills from an immutable release knowledge archive (`monica-knowledge.json` and its checksum) alongside stable editorial guides. Local site development can preview the current source checkout. ## Third-party ecosystem Independent packages use the publisher-first ID `.Monica.[.]`; one NuGet package may contain any coherent number of infrastructure, provider, web, and UI modules. The official `Monica.*` prefix and purple logo remain reserved for first-party packages. Start with the [`monica-third-party-module-development`](skills/monica-third-party-module-development) skill to scaffold, validate, test, pack, and publish an independent package. The compatibility identity and usage rules are summarized in [BRANDING.md](BRANDING.md), with the complete bilingual guide in [Monica.Docs](https://monica.dpdns.org/). ## Package maturity The maturity label describes the compatibility promise, not package quality. | Tier | Promise | Representative packages | |---|---|---| | **Stable** | The supported 1.0 application path | Core, BuildingBlocks, WebApi, Configuration, Repository, JobScheduler, OpenTelemetry, UI | | **Integrations** | Versioned adapters around external systems | EF Core, Kafka, Redis/StackExchange, Dapr, SignalR | | **Labs** | Deliberately fast-moving exploration | AI/RAG/MCP, DataChannel, DevOps and profiling, Office, Experimental | Applications can adopt Stable without taking a dependency on Labs. Integration packages remain optional and provider-specific; CI validates both complete package classification and one-way maturity dependencies. ## Runtime surfaces Monica includes operational Blazor surfaces for module dependencies, Building Blocks, configuration, jobs, dependency injection, telemetry, repositories, and other registered capabilities. They share a theme contract and first-party `en-US` and `zh-CN` localization resources. The one-minute demo shows JobScheduler operations, module dependency inspection, and runtime configuration: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/250e1e5f-0a78-4b8b-b832-756d682a01bd ## Documentation and community - Documentation: - Read-only documentation API: - Example documentation host: - Changelog: [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) - Issues: - Discussions: - Security: [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) Contribution and release guidance is in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## License and acknowledgements Monica is MIT licensed. See [LICENSE.txt](LICENSE.txt). A small subset of Monica modules was informed by the [ABP Framework](https://github.com/abpframework/abp), licensed under LGPL-3.0. Directly adapted code retains its original notices. Monica is an independent project and is not affiliated with ABP.

## ❌ Without Context7

LLMs rely on outdated or generic information about the libraries you use. You get:

- ❌ Code examples are outdated and based on year-old training data
- ❌ Hallucinated APIs that don't even exist
- ❌ Generic answers for old package versions

## ✅ With Context7

Context7 pulls up-to-date, version-specific documentation and code examples straight from the source — and gives them to your coding agent.

```txt
Create a Next.js proxy that checks for a valid JWT in cookies
and redirects unauthenticated users to `/login`. use context7
```

```txt
Configure a Cloudflare Worker script to cache
JSON API responses for five minutes. use context7
```

```txt
Show me the Supabase auth API for email/password sign-up.
```

Context7 fetches up-to-date code examples and documentation right into your coding agent's context. No tab-switching, no hallucinated APIs that don't exist, no outdated code generation.

Works in two modes:

- **CLI + Skills** — installs a skill that guides your agent to fetch docs using `ctx7` CLI commands (no MCP required)
- **MCP** — registers a Context7 MCP server so your agent can call documentation tools natively

## Installation

> [!NOTE]
> **API Key Recommended**: Get a free API key at [context7.com/dashboard](https://context7.com/dashboard?tab=settings) for higher rate limits.

Set up Context7 for your coding agents with a single command. The `ctx7` CLI requires Node.js 22.13 or newer.

```bash
npx ctx7 setup
```

Authenticates via OAuth, generates an API key, and installs the appropriate skill. You can choose between CLI + Skills or MCP mode. Use `--cursor`, `--claude`, or `--opencode` to target a specific agent.

To remove the generated setup later, run `npx ctx7 remove`. If you globally installed the CLI with `npm install -g ctx7`, remove that package separately with `npm uninstall -g ctx7`.

To configure manually, use the Context7 server URL `https://mcp.context7.com/mcp` with your MCP client and pass your API key via the `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY` header. See the link below for client-specific setup instructions.

**[Manual Installation / Other Clients →](https://context7.com/docs/resources/all-clients)**

## Important Tips

### Use Library Id

If you already know exactly which library you want to use, add its Context7 ID to your prompt. That way, Context7 can skip the library-matching step and directly retrieve docs.

```txt
Implement basic authentication with Supabase. use library /supabase/supabase for API and docs.
```

The slash syntax tells Context7 exactly which library to load docs for.

### Specify a Version

To get documentation for a specific library version, just mention the version in your prompt:

```txt
How do I set up a Next.js 16 proxy? use context7
```

Context7 will automatically match the appropriate version.

### Add a Rule

If you installed via `ctx7 setup`, a skill is configured automatically that triggers Context7 for library-related questions. To set up a rule manually instead, add one to your coding agent:

- **Cursor**: `Cursor Settings > Rules`
- **Claude Code**: `CLAUDE.md`
- Or the equivalent in your coding agent

**Example rule:**

```txt
Always use Context7 when I need library/API documentation, code generation, setup or configuration steps without me having to explicitly ask.
```

## Available Tools

### CLI Commands

- `ctx7 library <name> <query>`: Searches the Context7 index by library name and returns matching libraries with their IDs.
- `ctx7 docs <libraryId> <query>`: Retrieves documentation for a library using a Context7-compatible library ID (e.g., `/mongodb/docs`, `/vercel/next.js`).

### MCP Tools

- `resolve-library-id`: Resolves a general library name into a Context7-compatible library ID.
  - `query` (required): The user's question or task (used to rank results by relevance)
  - `libraryName` (required): The name of the library to search for
- `query-docs`: Retrieves documentation for a library using a Context7-compatible library ID.
  - `libraryId` (required): Exact Context7-compatible library ID (e.g., `/mongodb/docs`, `/vercel/next.js`)
  - `query` (required): The question or task to get relevant documentation for
  - `language` (optional): The programming language you write in, used to rank code examples in that language first

Projects listed in Context7 are developed and maintained by their respective owners, not by Context7. If you encounter any suspicious, inappropriate, or potentially harmful content, please use the "Report" button on the project page to notify us immediately. By using Context7, you acknowledge that you do so at your own discretion and risk.

name: Test

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [master]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "22"

      - name: Setup pnpm
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 10

      - name: Get pnpm store directory
        id: pnpm-cache
        shell: bash
        run: |
          echo "STORE_PATH=$(pnpm store path)" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Cache pnpm dependencies
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: ${{ steps.pnpm-cache.outputs.STORE_PATH }}
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-pnpm-store-${{ hashFiles('**/pnpm-lock.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-pnpm-store-

      - name: Install Dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Lint
        run: pnpm lint:check

      - name: Format
        run: pnpm format:check

      - name: Build
        run: pnpm build

      # The Admin MCP console page is committed as a built module (Vercel runs no UI build).
      - name: Admin MCP console bundle is up to date
        run: pnpm --filter @upstash/context7-admin-mcp build:ui && git diff --exit-code packages/admin-mcp/src/ui/console-html.ts

      # The context7-mcp skill served over MCP is committed as a module generated from skills/context7-mcp/SKILL.md.
      - name: MCP skill module is up to date
        run: pnpm --filter @upstash/context7-mcp build:skill && git diff --exit-code packages/mcp/src/lib/skill-md.ts

      - name: Typecheck
        run: pnpm typecheck

      - name: Test
        run: pnpm test
        env:
          CONTEXT7_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CONTEXT7_API_KEY }}
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}

      - name: SDK Integration Test
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
        run: pnpm --filter @upstash/context7-sdk test:integration
        env:
          CONTEXT7_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CONTEXT7_API_KEY }}

# AutoClip ### Turn any video, link, or live stream into ready-to-post clips. **The open-source OpusClip alternative** — local-first AI clipping for **podcasts, interviews, and gaming streams** with smart reframing, captions, covers, titles, and built-in **MCP for AI agents**. Zero subscriptions, no paywall.

       


  


Website  ·  Download  ·  Live Replays (v1.6)  ·  Showcase  ·  Quick Start  ·  Docs  ·  Issues

English · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Español · Português · Русский · Français · Bahasa Indonesia · Türkçe · Tiếng Việt · Deutsch


⭐ Free, MIT-licensed, zero subscriptions — everything cuts and renders on your machine. Star the repo if you find it useful!


APIMart
Low-cost AI image & video API · GPT-Image-2 from $0.006/img 		Sponsor / Partner with AutoClip
Put your AI API or creator tool in front of AutoClip users worldwide (cloud dynamic provider listing supported, zero client release needed).
christine_zhouye@163.com
--- ## Overview Drop in a link, local video, or **live stream replay** — AutoClip finds the best moments, tracks the speaker, burns in captions, generates covers, and exports ready-to-post clips for TikTok, Shorts, Reels, YouTube, Douyin, Xiaohongshu, and Bilibili. **Local-first by design:** cutting and rendering run directly on your computer with no upload queues and no monthly fee. Bring your own API key or run 100% offline with **Ollama / LM Studio + Whisper / SenseVoice**. ![AutoClip v1.6 Live Stream Replays Walkthrough](docs/images/v1.6/autoclip-v1.6-demo.gif)

Home → 6 Live Replay sources → OBS WebSocket setup → Twitch import → Finished clip with captions & one-click publish.

--- ## What's New in v1.6 | Feature | Details | | :--- | :--- | | **6 Live Replay Sources** | Dedicated **Live Replay** tab supporting **OBS Studio, Twitch, YouTube, Kick, Discord, and local recordings**. | | **OBS Auto-Capture** | Connect OBS WebSocket (`4455`), trim losslessly (`-c copy`), and auto-queue clips right after you end stream. | | **Game Highlights** | Generalized highlight detection supporting **8s+** standalone plays with tighter vision/OCR budgets. | | **One-Click Repurpose** | Unified playable clip cards — switch target platforms in one click without losing previous exports. | | **13 Languages** | Full desktop UI, tray menus, and docs in 13 languages (`+ zh-TW, de, id, tr, vi`) plus Arabic RTL captions. |
